2016-07-22 RETREAT

Date

22 July 2016 RETREAT 

Attendees

 

  •                @autumnsunshine     

 

Ground Rules:

  • honor time limits (starting and ending)
  • no interrupting /interject at appropriate times
  • listen and be considerate of all opinions
  • be present (limit device distraction)
  • no disruptive side conversations
  • shared responsibility for LEAD goals/outcomes

Schedule for day with notes:

  • Arrive between 8-8:30 for coffee and snacks and settling in.  

  • Start promptly at 8:30 with Who Am I? icebreaker.

  • 9ish -11ish am Melissa Yamamoto (AD for Leadership Development at OSU)  will be coming to do a 2 hours StrengthsFinder activity.
    The goal is to help us understand each other's strengths and how we can work better as as team

  • 11-11:10- BREAK

  • 11:10-12:30:   Scenarios/role playing for dealing with difficult patrons  - in small groups, share with large group  - Lori 


 

You get a report from a patron of a person talking LOUDLY to themselves on the 4th floor.

  • Ask for more info first and why is this upsetting  them; do you need to help them move to a quieter floor? or, do they feel unsafe? Need to determine the real issue

  • Send staff to check out the situations and possibly ask the person talking to themselves: “is everything okay?”  (NOT “someone complained about you” but if they ask anything you can say you are “worried about them”.

  • Depends on what they are saying too = are they threatening to kill someone or themselves?  -> if so call security!

  • If it’s nothing but them being loud, and you go to the area and more people are complaining then it’s best to ask the person to move to a non quiet floor or a study room - give them choices and options.

  • Zac asked about the 3 strikes rule they had at Denver Public and Lori said she was not keen on that but we could all talk about it further  another time if we wanted to

 

You get a complaint (or you see) a person viewing porn on a computer in the Learning Commons.

  • We have a policy on this (Link?) - its okay as long as they are not “active” while viewing.
  • Is it child porm? If so you must call the cops
  • If others are upset they can go to the public library down the street where there are privacy screens - question: do we have privacy screens for computers? If not should we get someone victoria?
  • Remember sometimes there is a class working on a project/research that might involve porn
  • How do you talk to student employees about this? Everyone agreed they should go to the staff and never have to handle this themselves.

Someone refused to do what they are asked/a policy or procedure. (Ex: refusal to show ID for 24/5 and run past into the library)

  • If it is a security issue, call security first!
  • If you can talk to the person, explain the reason for the policy and show on website
  • If they are not cooperating anyway, can we stop allowing them to have access to that “service” or note in their record?
  • Varies according to what the person is refusing to do : smoking in the building vs cord stretching across the room to plug into an outlet. The first one is much easier as i’ts a law on campus and they must leave. The latter one, how do you handle it? Tell them its a saftey hazzard, give them options like study room or better desk with a plug, etc. Do you unplug it if they refuse still - will that have legal ramifications? Beth suggested accidentally tripping over it which in turn unplugs it but not sure passive aggressive  responses are  the best method :)

A patron jumps over the circ desk as another patron comes toward them. (they might not have had a chance to say much to you before this, but they seems upset)

  • There is the emergency red phone  under circ, just knocking off the handle and it calls security and they can hear everything - IF it’s a real threat/ do this!
  • Might have been best to move the jumper away from the desk, separate them
  • If you were the only staff member, best to call security
  • Ask the name and ID #
  • Cameras in the building were mentioned - can we access them if we need to see what happened before they came to the desk? Don, Zac, and Dave M have access to view  ??)

Someone comes to the desk to report someone on another floor threatened to shoot him.

  • Get the reporting person away asap and safe - have them stay in the safe spot to talk to security when they come!  If they will not stay though they can go, its their choice! Try to get as much info as possible from the reporter.
  • Appraise the situation as you learn more - call security - staff do NOT need to approach this person on their own!
  • Loop in another staff member and notify other desks; have staff wait at main entrance to meet the officers when they arrive.
  • If a gun is actually seen, what do we do?. If a gun is seen but not an active shooter do we want to pull the alarm OR will that make it worse??  We discussed gun laws in oregon and were unclear.  Beth emailed the TAT team to ask about this!

 

 

  • 12:30-1pm Lunch will be brought in from Valley Catering 

  • 1-1:20 ish - Who Am I? wrap up 

  • 1:30- 4:30 pm Affinity Mapping work - Beth and Uta:

    • Circ Services at Info Desk

    • Info Desk Services at Circ Desk  

  • 4:30 Plus/Delta summary of the day and clean up


 


2016.09 In-Service Activities

350.org Corvallis “Drive-Less” campaign & CCL Carbon Fee + Dividend Proposal (Jim + Others)

This session will be an introduction to the local chapters of 350.org and the Citizens Climate Lobby (CCL) and their current  projects. 350.org is a leading worldwide climate organization and the local chapter, led by Kris Paul, is working on a "drive-less" campaign, among other exciting projects. The Citizens Climate Lobby (CCL) seeks to influence Congress to address climate change and revenue neutral carbon pricing. Join Carla Wise, the leader of the local chapter of the CCL, to find out why CCL believes the CCL Carbon + Dividend to be the best solution for passing carbon pricing.

Presenters - Carla Wise, Kris Paul, and Jim Rankin ~ Location: Willamette Rooms ~ Track: Healthy You, Healthy World

 

Plastics Recycling Session (Rima & Uta)

 

Title: Days in the Life of Tubby (An Average Plastic Container)

Abstract: When it comes to recycling household and workplace materials, almost nothing causes quite a much confusion as determining what plastics can or cannot be recycled. Recycling options depend on where you live and

what you are trying to recycle. Why can a juice bottle be recycled? Why can a plastic salad container not be recycled? Why does it matter if you live in Benton or Linn or Lane or "Whatever" County? We'll investigate these questions and more

by looking at specific days in the life of an average plastic container (Tubby). Two Benton County Master Recyclers-in-Training will utilize games, videos, discussion, and straight-up informational presentation to clarify and demystify the plastics recycling process.

We invite you to bring your trickiest plastics recycling items to contribute as a game piece and, of course, your urgent plastics recycling questions to keep the discussion lively. We'll also invite you to commit to one action for reducing your plastic footprint.

 

Outcomes:

  • Reduce/Reuse/Recycle
  • understand the lifecycle of recycled plastic
  • know what plastics can/cannot be recycled
  • have fun learning about plastic recycling
  • know one or more actions to help reduce plastic waste

 

Materials:

Video:

Handout: http://sustainablecorvallis.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/02/Captains-Fall-2015-Plastic-Shapes.pdf

"Tricky" Items: Roll to Win game (give items a number 1-12), have multiple sets of dice, teams roll and have to figure out if the item they land on can by recycled (FIGURE OUT PRIZES)

 

Session Structure

  • Reflection: What plastic waste I generate (name at least 3 things)
  • Show video of MRF
  • Info presentation
    • what does recycling symbol on plastics mean
    • plastics recycling economics: http://fa.oregonstate.edu/sites/fa.oregonstate.edu/files/recycling/resources/MR_Class/curbside_recycling.pdf; http://www.plasticrecycling.com/index.html
    • what can be recycled (Benton/Linn County/Lane: http://lanecounty.org/Departments/PW/Documents/BrochPlasticRecycling.pdf;http://sustainablecorvallis.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/02/Captains-Fall-2015-Plastic-Shapes.pdf
    • what is made from recycled plastic: http://blogs.uoregon.edu/elpgreen/files/2014/07/updated08recyclers_guide2bweb-2e6zqcf.pdf( pg. 14)
    • Q&A
  • Recycling game
  • Reflection/sharing: 1 action to reduce (most impactful) or reuse (more impactful) or recycle (impactful)

2017 Library Swag Purchasing Recommendations

Library Swag Purchasing  - DRAFT

OSU Libraries Sustainability Committee

June 2017

The greenest swag is that which does not exist at all.

(Greening_Libraries_----_(Pg_201–215).pdf pg. 201)

 

 

 

SCOPE (westhampton_library_sustainable_purchasing_policy_rev_april_13_2011_final.pdf) - figure out how to fold this into the Vacaville document structure

2.0 Scope

This purchasing policy applies to the purchase of:

Ongoing Consumables: Paper Products

Batteries

Lamps/bulbs

Cleaning Products

Soaps Paints, sealants, adhesives, caulks

Lawn/yard products

Electricity

Durable Goods

Furniture

Appliances

Electrical equipment

Maintenance & Cleaning Equipment

Facility Alterations and Additions

 

STATEMENT OF PURPOSE (http://www.calrecycle.ca.gov/LGCentral/Library/Innovations/Procurement/Vacavill.htm)

The City of Vacaville:

  • Recognizes the need to strengthen markets for materials collected in local recycling collection systems,
  • Desires to maximize reduction of discarded materials,
  • Desires to ensure that every department purchases environmentally-preferred products and services without compromising overall budgetary or performance requirements,
  • Recognizes the need to be proactive and to serve as an example to other agencies and organizations in the community, and
  • Complies with California state law, which requires local agencies to buy recycled products and which allows local agencies to adopt purchasing preferences for recycled products.
  • desires to build relationships over supporting support a consumer culture

1.0 STATEMENT OF POLICY

1.1 In accordance with the provisions of the Public Contract Code, it is the policy of the City of Vacaville to purchase recycled products instead of non-recycled products whenever available at no more than the total cost of non-recycled products, fitness and quality being equal. Such products shall be available within a reasonable time.

1.2 Price preferences for materials categories may be instituted in the future.

1.3 Source reduction and recycled products purchased shall contain the highest amount of post-consumer material practicable or, when post-consumer material is impracticable for a specific type of product, contain reasonable amount of pre-consumer recovered material.

1.4 All equipment bought, leased or rented shall be compatible with the use of source reduction and recycled products, whenever reasonable in terms of price, performance, warranty and maintenance.

1.5 The City of Vacaville shall promote its use of source reduction and recycled products whenever feasible.

2.0  DEFINITIONS

2.1 "Buyer" means anyone authorized to purchase on behalf of the jurisdiction or its subdivisions.

2.2 "Contractor" means any person, group of persons, business, consultant, designing architect, association, partnership, corporation, supplier, vendor or other entity that has a contract with the City of Vacaville or serves in a subcontracting capacity with an entity having a contract with the City of Vacaville for the provision of goods or services.

2.3 "Ownership Cost" means total ownership costs during a product’s life cycle, including, but not limited to, acquisition, extended warranties, operation, supplies, maintenance, disposal costs and expected lifetime compared to other alternatives.

2.4 "Post-consumer Material" means a finished material that would normally be disposed of as a solid waste, having completed its life cycle as a consumer item, and does not include manufacturing or converting wastes. Example of post-consumer materials includes, but not limited to, old newspapers, office paper, yard waste, steel, aluminum cans, glass, plastic bottles, oil, asphalt, concrete and tires.

2.5 "Pre-consumer Material" means material or by-products generated after manufacture of a product is completed but before the product reaches the end-use consumer. Examples of pre-consumer recovered material include, but not limited to, obsolete inventories of finished goods, rejected unused stock, and paper waste generated during printing, cutting, and other converting operations.

2.6 "Price Preference" means the percentage allowance for a recycled product that costs more than a comparable virgin product. In bid situations, it is the percentage above the lowest cost of a comparable virgin product allowed for a recycled product when both bidders are responsible and responsive.

2.7 "Purchasing Documents" means all documents used to solicit bids and purchase products, including but not limited to: invitations for bids, requests for proposals, requests for quotations, and purchase order.

2.8 "Recovered Material" means fragments of products or finished of a manufacturing process, which has converted a resource into a commodity of real economic value, and includes pre-consumer and post-consumer material, but does not include excess resources of the manufacturing process.

2.9 "Recycled Content" means the percentage of recovered material, including pre-consumer and post-consumer materials, in a product.

2.10 "Recycled Content Standards" means the minimum or maximum level of recovered material and/or post-consumer material necessary for products to qualify as "recycled products", as established by the City of Vacaville.

2.11 "Recycled Product" means a product that meets the City of Vacaville’s recycled content policy objectives for post-consumer, pre-consumer and recovered material.

2.12 "Remanufactured Product" means any product diverted from the supply of discarded materials by refurbishing and marketing said product without substantial change to its original form.

2.13 "Reused Product" means any product designed to be used many times for the same or other purposes without additional processing except for specific requirements such as cleaning, painting or minor repairs.

2.14 "Source Reduction Product" means a product that results in a net reduction in the generation of waste compared to the previous or alternate version and includes durable, reusable and remanufactured products; products with no, or reduced, toxic constituents; and products marketed with no, or reduced packaging.

3.0 POLICY IMPLEMENTATION

3.1 The Finance Manager or authorized representative, in cooperation with the Director of Public Works or authorized representative and relevant departments, offices and agencies, shall aggressively implement the City of Vacaville Source Reduction and Recycled Product Procurement Policy.

3.2 The Finance Manager or authorized representative, in cooperation with the Director of Public Works or authorized representative, shall establish recycled content standards and is authorized to raise or lower them to meet the objectives of this policy. The decision to change any recycled content standard shall be substantiated in the annual report.

3.3 The Finance Manager or authorized representative may establish price preferences for materials categories as deemed necessary to meet the objectives of this policy.

3.4 The City of Vacaville is authorized to participate in, and encourage other public jurisdictions to participate in, cooperative purchasing agreements.

3.5 All departments, offices and agencies shall evaluate their product specifications and purchasing documents and remove all obstacles feasible to buying recycled and source reduction products. Among the obstacles to be removed are:

  • Requirements for virgin materials only,
  • Language that excludes recycled products,
  • Unnecessary qualifications (e.g., High brightness levels for paper),
  • Specifications written to describe particular non-recycled products, unless justified per Sec.3.17.
  • Performance standards unrelated to actual need,
  • "New" requirements that exclude remanufactured, reused or recycled content products.

3.6 Performance standards must be reasonable and related to operational need, and shall be designed to encourage the purchase of source reduction and recycled products.

3.7 Buyers shall specify recycled content standards, as established by the Finance Manager or authorized representative, in applicable bid solicitations and purchasing opportunities.

3.8 Buyers shall obtain quotes for comparable recycled and non-recycled items to fulfill reporting requirements.

3.9 Buyers shall establish virgin prices on a case-by-case basis at the time of the bid:

  • On annual contracts, agreements and/or blanket orders, request both virgin and recycled product pricing during the bidding process;
  • On annual contracts, agreements and/or blanket orders, if asking for recycled product only, survey the market for virgin product prices by contacting at least thee suppliers at the time of establishing the annual contract;
  • For items not covered by annual contracts, agreements and/or blanket orders, either request both virgin and recycled product pricing during the bidding process or survey the market for virgin product prices by contacting at least three suppliers.
  • If buyers do not, or cannot, obtain prices for virgin counterparts, recycled product is to be considered the low-cost alternative and no price preference applies.

3.10 All departments, offices and agencies shall submit to the Director of Public Works or authorized representative any evaluative information from the testing of recycled content products and content, quantity type and cost information as available.

3.11 When no recycled content standards exist, buyers shall purchase products with the highest percentage of post-consumer materials practicable, as long as quality, performance and availability meet requirements and price is reasonable within the parameters of this policy, or when post-consumer material is impracticable for a specific type of product, contain substantial amount of pre-consumer recovered material.

3.12 Purchasing documents shall request identification of recycled content (recovered and post-consumer materials, as applicable) for products whenever feasible. Successful bidders shall be required to certify the percentage content of post-consumer and/or total recovered material, as specified in products to be purchased. Individual buyers should make every effort to confirm recycled content information when seeking telephone or faxed quotes or direct purchases. Buyers shall insert recycled content certification forms in all appropriate purchasing documents for non-exempt product categories.

3.13 Bids shall state bidders’ failure to prove recycled content information as appropriate shall mean zero recycled content.

3.14 The percentage of post-consumer and total recovered materials content in paper products shall be fiber weight. Total product weight shall be used for all other types of products. For products with varying surface treatments, such as insulation, total product weight shall refer to only the core materials.

3.15 Bidders shall be requested to minimize packaging to the greatest extent practicable. Individual buyers shall encourage vendors to reduce packaging as much as possible.

3.16 Bidders shall be encouraged to offer source reduction product alternatives if they can substantiate the source reduction benefits.

3.17 Buyers shall justify in writing purchases of non-recycled or non-source reduction products to the Finance Manager or authorized representative, who may waive in writing a requirement of this policy when he/she determines justification supports such a waiver and it is in the best interests of the City of Vacaville. In those instances where it is deemed impracticable to a source reduction or recycled product, a specific explanation for the exclusion must be included in the purchasing record.

3.18 Equipment purchased or rented by the City of Vacaville shall be compatible, whenever practicable, with the use of source reduction and recycled products. If deemed impracticable, a specific reason for using incompatible equipment must be included in the purchasing record.

3.19 All departments, offices, and agencies shall ensure that they use both sides of paper sheets whenever practicable.

3.20 Whenever practicable, recycled products shall be labeled as such in a standard format. Example:

  • Printed pieces and copies, including letterhead and business cards, shall carry the following notation:

Printed on recycled paper.

3.21 All City of Vacaville vendors, contractors, and service providers shall be notified of this requirement to label or otherwise designate recycled products as such at the time competitive bids or proposals are solicited and at other appropriate opportunities.

3.22 The Finance Manager or authorized representative, in cooperation with the Director of Public Works or authorized representative, shall educate buyers on issues relevant to buying source reduction and recycled products whenever necessary and appropriate.

3.23 Buyers shall educate vendors, suppliers and contractors on issues relevant to source reduction and recycled products whenever necessary and appropriate.

4.0 PRECEDENCE

4.1 The order of purchasing preference is, (1) the highest percentage of recycled content of "post-consumer recovered material" available in the marketplace, and (2) the highest percentage of "pre-consumer recovered material" available in the marketplace.

4.2 In addition to the recovered material content of a product, important criteria in selecting products shall also be:

  • Reduction: the quantity, volume, weight or toxicity of waste and by-products of a given product, and the packaging generated in their manufacture, use, recycling and disposal. Products and packaging designed to minimize waste and toxic by-products in their manufacture, use, recycling and disposal shall be preferred.
  • Reusability: the ability of its packaging to be reused or reconditioned for use.
  • Recyclability: the ability of a product and its packaging to be recycled through existing recycled collection programs.

Whenever possible, buyers shall combine these components to achieve the greatest environmental benefit possible. Example:

It may be better to replace a recycled product with a reusable product. An even better choice would be a reusable product that also has recycled content.

4.3 All City of Vacaville departments, offices and agencies may evaluate environmental benefits and ownership cost when evaluating prices to determine the lowest responsible bid.

4.4 When no bidder meets the specified minimum recycled content standard, buyers may purchase the product with the highest percentage of post-consumer content or, when post-consumer content is not practicable, the highest percentage of recovered material. This can only occur when the purchasing document explains it as a method for contract award.

4.5 When standards are specified for both recovered material and post-consumer material, buyers may accept the lowest cost bid that offers a substantially higher amount of post-consumer content than the specification requires but does not meet specified recovered material requirements, even when other bidders meet the specification in the purchasing document. This can only occur when the purchasing document explains it as a method for contract award.

5.0 APPLICATION

5.1 All City of Vacaville departments, offices and agencies shall comply with this policy.

5.2 Any RFP or bids for services requested by the City shall include a standard statement that the City of Vacaville has implemented a source reduction and buy recycled policy and that the City encourages other businesses to adhere to similar principles. It shall further be requested that submitted proposals be printed two-sided on recycled content paper. Any consultants or contractors producing reports for the City will submit such on (post-consumer) recycled and recyclable paper.

5.3 Contractors shall be further requested to report to the City the post-consumer and total recovered material content of any recycled products produced for City-funded work.

6.0 REPORTS

6.1 The Recycling Coordinator may prepare an annual report, with the cooperation of all buyers, noting the annual dollar expenditures, percent change from previous years, percent represented of total purchasing budget, total savings or cost for using recycled or source reduction purchases, and the number of product types bought in each category. The annual report shall also include identification and discussion of instances in with this policy has been waived or found impracticable, a discussion of other barriers to the procurement of recycled products, and any instances when recycled content standards or price preferences were adjusted.

6.2 Buyers may specify in annual contracts or other long-term purchasing agreements that vendors are required to provide information furnish annual vendor reports by July 31st indicating the quantity, dollar amount, percentage(s) and type(s) of recycled content for all products furnished to the City of Vacaville. A copy of this information will be forwarded to the Director of Public Works or authorized representative.

24-5 Statistics

 

Overview

The 24/5 floor count statistics were collected between the Spring 2010 24/5 pilot and Spring 2015. After Spring 2015 the statistics were discontinued because there was no longer a specific purpose for them; they weren't being used for any active research and weren't necessary to support the continued existence of the 24/5 hours.

The data from the daily 24/5 floor counts was inputted daily into that term’s Excel spreadsheet and the data was then aggregated over the entire term. Each term's 24/5 statistics spreadsheet is attached to this page.

Floor Count Instructions

*The following section contains instructions for how to do the 24/5 building walk-through and floor counts.

On every hour from 1am to 6am we walk through the entire building (excluding Java II), count patrons, and categorize their activity. See the Statistics section below for the compiled statistics by term.

  • Take the floor count statistics clipboard and one walkie-talkie on every walk. Leave the other walkie-talkie on the Circulation desk. The walkie-talkies should always be set to channel 3.
  • Start on the 2nd floor and then walk through the other floors in any order. Depending on how many patrons are in the building, it may take up to 45 minutes to finish.
  • Staff: clear any copier jams and restart any scanners that have frozen.

Security/safety measures during the floor count:

  • The phone numbers for the Circulation desk and campus security are located at the bottom of the first page of the statistics sheet in case you may need them.

  • You can wear headphones while doing the floor count but please play the music low enough that you can hear what's going on around you in case of a security or medical emergency. 

  • Should you witness any activity that is illegal or in violation of student conduct, notify a staff member or security immediately. There are red emergency phones in each stairwell that are a direct line to campus security. Use these phones in case of an emergency. If you need to contact a staff member you can use your walkie-talkie or a black campus/local phone to dial Circulation (7-7254). These phones are located on each floor on the wall by the table nearest to the west stairwell.

The library is a big building and there are a lot of nooks and crannies that students can occupy. It is important to be thorough to ensure accurate counts. Places of note are:

  • In all the rotundas there are alcoves that are on the north and south curves of the rotunda. Please actually walk into these alcoves to count patrons.
  • Near the catalog computers on each floor there are desks built into a hollowed out pillar.
  • In the CLC (Collaborative Learning Center) and LC (Learning Commons) students like to create spaces with whiteboards and it can be easy to miss someone lying down, sleeping.
  • The Archives & Maps area of the 3rd floor has a lot of nooks and crannies that students move tables to and study in.  
  • On the 5th floor there is a lobby for Special Collections with benches that students like to nap on.  
  • Check all study rooms including the ones whose lights are turned off because students like to take naps in the study rooms at night.

Access Services Conference Notes - Bryan

Hello.

Following is a summary of the Access Services Conference in Atlanta GA Nov. 15-17 I attended with Lori Hilterbrand.

First of all I would like to thank Lori for making this trip and presentation possible. It was her idea to submit a proposal to present and to our surprise it was excepted. She also wrangled up a $1000 travel scholarship to help pay for the expenses. Thank you Lori! And a big thank you to Beth, Anne Marie and Faye for approving the trip. Also nice that Anne Marie was there to support us.

The conference was held at the Global Learning Center on the Georgia Tech campus.

Wed evening Lori and I attended the reception at the Renaissance Atlanta Midtown Hotel Ballroom. We had a nice dinner and my first taste of grits which I enjoyed. I sat down at a table with a couple from Minnesota. Unbeknownst to either of us we happened to be the two travel scholarship award winners which was presented after dinner. Thank you Lori for the nomination.

Thursday Sessions

Welcome Address and Keynote Presentation – Brian Mathews, Assoc. Dean for Learning, Virginia Tech Libraries

  • Brian was an entertaining speaker and has been involved in a wide variety of library work. He is a learning strategist developing campus-wide programs for digital literacy, active learning curation and ePortfolios.
  • He used a pirate analogy to describe project planning – goals, strategic planning, ability to adapt, intelligence gathering, daring quick thinking, speed ability
  • We should focus on not just what we did but how we talked about it.
  • With innovative space use we should be building excitement about and around the library
  • Parlay = try different things to see what evolves
  • Important are skills of facilitating, organizing, marketing, communication, assessment and being proactive. Use your resources and staff accordingly.
  • 5 keys to strategic planning
    • Parlay – lots of little things can have a big impact. Understand the whole process and interact. Inquiry leads to discovery. Work with what you have and build from there. Tinker as needs emerge. Don’t make things so rigid where you will miss opportunities.
    • FIOAYG = Figure It Out As You Go – Help fill in the blank parts of the map. Libraries are becoming different from each other as they are no longer collection based. Proactively identify improvements. Patrons can show us unmet needs. Decide how are we trying to make an impact. Be aware of your “bubble” or tunnel vision.
    • Be The Face – frontline staff shape the user experience
    • Know More, Do More – the more that you know about users, the more that you can accomplish. What do we know, don’t know, think we know, want to know and what users want us to know? Be curious about the people and environment around you.
    • Be A User – need to know the problems to appreciate what needs to be fixed. Find out for yourself what needs to be improved.

Re-Evaluating Library Usage AFTER a Library Renovation – Jo-Ann Cooley and Kari Mofford, UMASS Dartmouth

  • Began with a short history of the Claire T Carney Library
  • Went through a library renovation in 2011-13 and found everything was not perfect, so needed to adapt to improve the user experience
  • Renovation improved library usage but began thinking what could be improved – chose to live in the space awhile to see how it was being used. Immediate improvements included:
    • Re-oriented the stacks so they were perpendicular to the windows for more light
    • Added privacy panels to with location numbers to study areas
    • Determined problem areas – wifi not working on upper floors, not enough seating, needed more quiet space, needed 24/7 hours, needed more computers, needed more whiteboards
    • Created a Space Committee and began gathering feedback from students and staff and created a wish list. Based on the wish list and what the budget would allow, they chose the top 5 and kept the rest of the list as an “extended wish list” for future consideration. Included:
      • Open/Taken signage for study rooms. Open meant anyone could study in the area while Taken meant private group.
      • Stressless Day and Therapy Dogs
      • Game Night
      • Continuing projects include problem of having glass walls for study rooms & active shooter events and creating a building maintenance plan
      • Space Committee had strong and committed participation, shared common goals and motivations, engaged in frank discussions, and Asst. Dean provided insights on renovation decisions.

Badges of Service: Engaging, Customer-oriented Student Employee Training – Lori Hilterbrand and Bryan Feyerherm, OSULP

  • Our presentation in their largest auditoriu.. Let me begin by saying if you are nervous about presenting, co-present with Lori. She set the tone and the presentation went smoothly. During audience feedback they were very talkative and willing to participate and overall a nice crowd. We estimated over 100 attended.
  • Really enjoyed Q&A. We took 75 training buttons to share and only came back with 10. After Q&A there were several who came up to us and asked further questions and we gave out our email addresses for further collaboration. Also thereafter at the conference others would share that they enjoyed the presentation. It was a nice feeling and we could now relax to enjoy the rest of the conference.
  • Lori and I plan on giving a brief overview of the presentation at our next LEAD meeting with a few photos at Beth’s invite.

Librarian or Emergency Responder – Jennifer Hughes, Kimbel Library, Coastal Carolina University

  • Interesting topic in how libraries are becoming routinely called upon to respond to a wide-variety of emergency situations.
  • The library is open 24 hours and averages 500 patrons per hour.
  • The Kimble Library began experiencing real emergencies beyond handing out band aids and realized they were unprepared. Very often in the evenings and weekends the library is the only public building that is open on campus.
  • Incidents included sexual harassment and a hoax rape call which lasted 1.5 hours.
  • Responded by:
    • Requiring all staff to be certified in CPR and first aid. No exceptions.
    • Fire extinguisher training
    • Active shooter training. Use SAFE (Secure/Alert/Fight/Escape) instead of Run/Hide/Fight.
    • Emergency PreparAthon Day organized by university Emergency Management
    • Collaboration with counseling services and the Title IX coordinator
    • Collaboration with Dean of Students and Student Conduct Board – communication is very important as it can record a history of misconduct
    • Emergency Response Partners – Narcan training (used for opioid overdose), exam time counseling, library flu shot clinic
    • Pet Therapy
    • The library staff have been designated as essential personnel due to their direct care services. So, when the weather is bad, they need to come in if safe to do so.
    • Tips
      • Plan and have the authority to initiate action
      • Take action when you know it is needed
      • Test different scenarios and discuss your plan
      • Give new employees a Safety Bag
      • Inform staff that dialing 911 on a mobile phone may not indicate where you are located
      • Call 911 immediately and begin talking, even if a dispatcher has not answered, your call will be recorded

Poster Session

  • All of the posters will be shared online so didn’t review too closely but did notice these topics:
    • We Buy Textbooks So Students Don’t Have To
    • Offering More Than A Job: Building Capacity in Students by Reframing the Student Employment Program
    • Are Daily Fines Effective in Reducing the Number of Days an Item is Kept Out Past Its Due Date?
    • Course Reserves at MacOdrum Library: Past, Present and Future
    • Finding the Sonic Sweet Spot: Implementing a Noise Management Program in the Learning Commons
    • Level Up! Online Strategies for Managing Student Workers
    • Understanding Diverse Populations: Opportunities and Challenges of Access Services
    • A Positive Police Presence: Partnering with Campus Police to Secure Your Library
    • The Environmental Slap: Student Initiated Renovation of Group Study Rooms
    • Virtual Reality (VR) Headsets in Circulation and Instruction

A Bibliometric Analysis of ILL Data at the NASA Goddard Space Flight Center – Brynne Norton, NASA Goddard Library, Cadence Group

  • Saw NASA in the title and had to go. Wasn’t anything else more interesting offered at this time.
  • Brynee demonstrated the process and tools that can be used to run a bibliometric analysis of ILL data using the NASA Goddard Space Flight Center as a case study.
  • Goddard’s library uses mostly eResources and ILLiad
  • The study measured the impact of ILL and most popular subjects requested for 2015-16
  • Original ILLiad data needed cleanup using VOS Viewer Network Mapper and Sublime Text Editor
  • Used Google for help writing Regular Expressions
  • Used Open Refine to further clean Metadata
  • Reviewed results using VOS graphic results

Friday

Investing in Access Services Student Employees: Utilizing Library Employment Skillsets to Increase Advocacy – Christopher Bishop and Jalesia Horton, Agnes Scott College and Augusta University

  • Focused on participatory engagement of student workers leading to greater student investment as employees are given tools to become library advocates.
  • Areas of focus include project learning, student leadership in developing events/activities, active solicitation of ideas, and resume workshops to translate work skills to their future careers.
  • Jalesia had previously worked at Oxford where there was a high student employee turnover and freshman were not allowed to provide feedback.
  • Issues at Augusta – only 6 student employees, minimal duties, students had no idea of library’s mission
  • Issues at Agnes Scott – no student feedback, high turnover, only 6 student employees, no idea of library’s mission
  • Students as Outreach Advocates
    • Students reach places that staff and faculty cannot
    • Advertises for student employees at the library
    • Utilizing project management skills
      • Promotion, events, activities, collection development initiatives, displays
      • Schedule students specifically for project time, around 2-4 hours per week
      • A list of projects is kept at the Circ desk
      • Project assignments are based on interest and skills
      • When hiring interviewee’s are asked about project interests and skills
      • Students work on the blog, social media, library signage, collection promotion, design exhibits, public relations assistants, manage events like Game Night or Murder Mystery
      • Investment and Student Feedback
        • Helps students understand their job in the big picture
        • How they can leave their mark on the library and become invested
        • Always encourage student feedback and participation
        • Project Planning Committee
          • Members include staff and students
          • Plan project development like Event Escape Rooms and Banned Book Week
          • Dealing with students that are not interested in projects
            • Give them projects anyway and most of the time they become invested
            • Resumes & Referrals –
              • classes involving resume creation,
              • professionally adding project descriptions, skills and responsibilities
              • Can apply student advocacy to staff and encourage staff feedback and ideas on skilled projects

User-Centered Access: Planning and Implementing a Fine-Free Policy – Maryke Barber and Karen Ryan, Hollins University

  • Successfully implemented a proposal to extend lending and eliminate overdue fines
  • Local study’s showed that fines had no impact on return rates and students cannot afford overdue fines
  • Trust = better community relationships
  • What Works – longer loan periods, more notices, billing for replacement & blocking accounts
    • Students often have semester long projects so longer loan periods help them succeed. Gave them semester long loan periods.
    • Fewer renewals
    • Pushed ILL for items not available
    • Need to communicate changes to library patrons & created a libguide
    • Forgave all fines when beginning program
    • Considered with Proposal – mission, people & financial impact, timeline, benchmark successes, positive feedback

Navigating the Storm: Leadership in Times of Crisis – Katie Glaeser, Sweet Briar College

  • Dealt with managers coping with times of crisis, like budget or employee turnover
  • Katie dealt with a 2015 attempted closure of SBC and a 2012 consolidation of Augusta University
  • 3 tools in dealing with crisis
    • Remain calm
    • Focus on your mission
      • Realign library priorities with new needs, assess the situation, do a SWOT analysis
  • Prioritize the welfare of others
    • Change = shift in behavior
    • Lead with care – make it worth it to stay
    • How you treat people impacts morale
    • Maintain transparency – will reduce people creating their own explanations
    • Manage expectations
    • Rumors are information but need to verify and ignore the obviously untrue – don’t let it be a distraction
    • Recommended reading
      • Our Iceberg is Melting
      • Who Moved My Cheese
      • Strategic Planning and Management for Library Managers
      • Switch: How to Change Things When Change is Hared
      • The No Asshole Rule

Overall the trip went smoothly and greatly enjoyed the conference and Atlanta. Many interesting ideas esp. in with the topics of safety and student employees. Also found time to visit the Center for Puppetry Arts (includes the Jim Henson Collection) and the Georgia Aquarium.

-          Bryan

Advanced Reservations

When a patron has made a reservation for a study room, they must check-in at the LEAD Desk for two reasons:

  • So staff can check them into their reservation. If that doesn't happen, the reservation may be cancelled by desk staff as a "no-show".
  • To check out a key card for their room.

Patrons who have successfully made an advanced reservation will receive a confirmation email. If they do not have a confirmation email, they do not have a reservation.

Confirm Identity

Regardless of how you search for the patron's advanced reservation, always confirm their identity before handing them a key card. You need their ID number anyway to ensure it is attached to the reservation. You can confirm identity 3 different ways:

  • Use their OSU ID card
  • Use their picture ID to look them up in Alma and get their OSU ID number
  • Look them up in Atrium and get their OSU ID number.

Checking in Advanced Reservations with the Booking Explorer Tab

In the Booking Explorer tab, you can find patron bookings using the search feature.

  • Select "LibAuth Account" as your search filter.
  • Click the cursor in the search field then ask the patron to swipe their ID card. Their ID number will automatically populate the field. Click "Go"
No ID Card

If the patron doesn't have their OSU ID card, you must confirm their identity and manually enter their OSU ID number into the search field. You can do this a couple different ways:

  • Ask for photo ID. Look them up in Alma to get their OSU ID number.
  • Look them up in Atrium and get their OSU ID number that way.
  • All of their advanced reservations will show up. Select the reservation for the current day and click the Booking ID in the left column.
    • Pro tip: To ensure you get the right reservation, you can narrow your search by first selecting "Today" in the date filter at the top of the page.

 

  • Click the Booking ID hyperlink for booking details and a window will pop up.

                        

  • Scan the barcode of the key card into the Internal Notes field.
  • Click "Add Note" to save the information.
  • Click the "Check in now" hyperlink to check the patron into their booking. Forgetting to do this my result in staff canceling their booking as a "no show".
  • Hand the patron their key, and they are ready to go.

Checking in Advanced Reservations with the Booking Grid Tab

This option works well if the patron remembers which floor they are on and things are quiet. Because you aren't searching for their reservation using their ID number, remember to verify their identity before proceeding.

This is the default view for the Booking Grid tab. Select the category (Study rooms for 1st, 2nd, or 5th floor).

Once you do, you will get a grid showing all of the bookings at that moment.

When you hover over a booking (indicated in red), details will pop up about the booking including the patron name.

  • Click on the appropriate booking and scroll to the bottom of the page.
  • Scan the barcode of the key card into the Internal Notes field.
  • Click "Add Note" to save the information.
  • Click the "Check in now" hyperlink to check the patron into their booking. Forgetting to do this my result in staff canceling their booking as a "no show".
  • Hand the patron their key, and they are ready to go.

Checking In Advanced Reservations with Confirmed Bookings Tab

This tab can also work well when things are quiet and there aren't many advanced reservations. The nice thing about this tab is that you can see all the spaces on one screen. Again, this works well when there aren't very many advanced reservations. The default view will be a monthly calendar.

In the upper right corner, change the view to Agenda. LibCal will default to the Week view. Select Day view and you get this.

As you can see, it is very full when all the rooms are selected which is the default setting.

  • Deselect the spaces you don't want to view by either clicking "Toggle All" to deselect everything at once, or by individually unchecking spaces.
  • Hover over individual reservations to see details including the patron's name, time and place of reservation, etc.

  • Click on the appropriate booking and scroll to the bottom of the page.
  • Scan the barcode of the key card into the Internal Notes field.
  • Click "Add Note" to save the information.
  • Click the "Check in now" hyperlink to check the patron into their booking. Forgetting to do this my result in staff canceling their booking as a "no show".
  • Hand the patron their key, and they are ready to go.

Checking Out

For the most part, you won't need to check out patrons. They will most likely leave on their own. If you do, follow the steps above. When you reach the end, click the Check Out button. This will check the patron out of their reservation and make the space available again in the system.


Affiliate Spouse/Partner

Affiliate-Spouse/Partner is a spouse, partner, or dependent of an OSU student, Faculty, or Staff member.

  • Issued an OSU ID with the title "Affiliate S/P" and an OSU ID # that starts with "100." (Some of them start with 93#, for example if they were a former student)

  • Same borrowing rights as their spouse/partner/parent- so you have to ask if their partner/parent is faculty, staff, or student.

    • Affiliate dependent (minor) also eligible for same borrowing rights

  • Not in Banner and need to have a 93 number created for them which is why we need a library card application.

Creating an Account

  1. Search in ALMA by the patron's name to see if they already have an account.

    1. Library account, but is is expired; you can look up their spouse/partner by name in Atrium to verify they are still active and update their account accordingly.

    2. No library account, have them fill out a Library Card Application.

      1. Verify their spouse/partner by name in Atrium to verify they are still active and update their account accordingly.

    3. Verifying in Atrium

      1) If they have ANY other status than listed below, they are a Convenience Card User Group.
      1. PtStudent ← this is a student, in Alma the User Group will usually be "Undergrad" or "Post-Bacc"
      2. PtEmployee ← this is a campus employee Staff or Faculty, in Alma the User Group will usually be "OSU Staff" or "OSU Faculty/GTA"
  2. In ALMA, under Manage Patron Services, click the Register a new patron.
  3. Fill out each required field with the information on the application.
    • Name: first, middle, last

    • Primary Identifier: Enter their ID number from their OSU ID card. They will use this university ID number to log into their account online.

    • User Group: Use spouse/partner status in Atrium - faculty, staff, or student, and select correct group from drop down menu

    • Campus: Select correct campus from drop down menu (OSU Main Campus)

    • Expiration date: one year

    • Birth date

    • User Management Information Patron has institutional record = No 

    • Password = Patron last name (1st letter capital) and last 4 digits of ID no.

       If the patron's last name is 3 letters or less, add extra digits of the ID no. so total characters = 8

      (i.e., for a 3 letter last name add the last 5 digits of the patrons ID no.)

       The last name follows the following rules:

      • No punctuation

      • No hyphen

      • No spaces

      • Example:

        • John Mac Gruder-Smith with ID# 000-186-954 would have the following password:“MacGruderSmith6954”Verify Password: same as above


    • Verify Password: same as above

    • Force password change on next login: Yes. Always check this box.

    • Email address: check appropriate box and enter email address

    • Addresses: Select Address type as "Work" and enter the patron's mailing address

    • Phone number: Select appropriate box and enter telephone number area code first. (format xxx-xxx-xxxx)

  4. Choose Update User to add the Patron Barcode

    • Click on their Patron ID number. to enter their account.

      • Choose Add Identifier

      • Choose Identifier Type = Barcode

      • Scan ID card for Value

      • Add and Close

  5. Add note:

    • Click on the "notes" tab

    • Click the "add note" button

    • In the note field add note: Affiliate Account: Name of their Spouse/Partner

    • In the Type drop-down menu select: Circulation

  6. Save and exit the record.

  7. Fill out the Staff Use section of the application

    1. Mark off that you verified their photo ID & address
    2. Write down the name of their OSU Spouse/Partner
    3. Write down today's date & your initials

  8. Inform patron about their library account

    1. They have the same borrowing privileges as their spouse/partner
    2. Library brochure
    3. How to log into their online account
  9. Place application in Circ inbox

Affiliate vs. Associate

An Affiliate is the Spouse or Partner of an OSU Student, Faculty or Staff member. They are allowed the same borrowing privileges as their partner. Their OSU ID number always starts with "100."

An Associate is an employees of an organization or federal agencies housed on OSU campus, providing teaching, research, or funding to OSU are eligible for the Associate status. Their OSU ID number starts with "93#" and the word Associate is printed on their card.

Weirdness: There are "Associates" with 100# IDs that are not Affiliates. The ID will have the word "Associate" printed on it when this is the case.

Reporting Alma System Outages

Alma Down Procedures

Alma Analytics Tips and Tricks

This page contains some basic things to remember when creating or editing analyses in Alma Analytics. This page is not an instruction manual for Alma Analytics but it can be useful for any LEAD staff member that is interested in pulling Alma statistics from Analytics.

Cataloging and configuration changes can mess up statistics in Alma Analytics!

If you are using Title, Permanent Call Number, Item Policy, Location Code, etc. filters in Analytics and the name of that Title, Permanent Call Number, etc. changes in Alma, Analytics will NOT automatically update the name in your filter. Any time a cataloging or configuration name change happens, you will have to manually update your filters in Analytics to the new name. See the section below for more information.

Do NOT change bib record titles, holdings record call numbers, Item Policy names, or any other commonly used filters lightly. The same goes for deleting bib records. Talk to other staff members first to see how this will change their statistics.

Fulfillment Analyses - Loans and Returns

The following tips apply to "Fulfillment" subject area analyses. These are the analyses generally used to pull loan and return statistics.

ALL loan analyses should include the following filters

  • "In House Loan Indicator" is equal to "N". Why? When an available item is checked in, the second check-in is registered as an "In House Loan" in Alma. In House Loans are recorded as a loan in Alma so they skew loan statistics for Circulation items that are frequently checked-in twice at the Circulation Desk (laptops, study room keycards, etc.). Setting the "In House Loan Indicator" field (under the "Loan Details" folder) equal to No removes all of the In House Loans from the statistics. CM staff measure In House Loans for books left around the library but Circulation staff do not want to measure In House Loans in their statistics.
  • "Loan Date" is greater than 12/04/2014. Why? December 5th, 2014 was when Alma went live; this is the start date of accurate loan records in Analytics. This is an issue because Alma imported some (but not all) loans from before that date into Analytics. Since only some of the loans were brought over, any loans from before 12/5/14 are not accurate so we want to exclude them from the analysis.

Cataloging and configuration changes can mess up analyses

  • If your analysis filters items by "Title", any changes to the title (in the bib record) in Alma will change your statistics.
    • Analytics doesn't automatically update the "Title" filters to the new title; the filter will still contain the old title. Basically, this removes that title from your statistics. So, every time a title you're using in an analysis changes, you will have to manually update the "Title" filter to the new title. If you don't update it, you won't be pulling that title's statistics anymore.
    • Note: Changing the title does NOT delete the loans for the old title. But, it does change the title of all of the loans including the historic ones. So, all of the loans for the old title will now have to be pulled using the new title. For example, if you change the name of the phone cables from "Valley Computer Adapters" to "Valley USB Cables" in 2015, you will need to use the new title "Valley USB Cables" to pull loans from 2014 because Analytics retroactively changed the title associated with all of those loan.
  • If your analysis filters items by "Item Policy" or any other useful Alma configuration filter like "Location Code", any changes to the Item Policy's (or Location Code's) name will change your statistics. This works exactly the same as the "Title" problem above.
  • If your analysis filters items by "Title" and new titles are added to that collection, you will need to add those titles to your "Title" filter manually. Any title filter seeking those statistics will need to be updated! The same goes for new Item Policies, new Location Codes, etc.
  • Also be careful when deleting titles. Analytics keeps statistics for withdrawn titles but you have to know the title in order to filter by it. Deleting titles if you're using strict filters (like "Title" filters) can result in you removing that title's loans and returns statistics from your analysis if you're not careful. This is an issue if you're trying to get total loans or returns for a type of equipment (like all laptops) but some titles for that equipment type have since been deleted.

Physical Items Analyses

The following tips apply to "Physical Items" subject area analyses. These are the analyses generally used to pull more detailed information about items like their Replacement costs and Fulfillment Notes.

Current vs withdrawn items

Use the filter "Lifecycle" is equal to "Active" to pull information only about current items and not withdrawn items. Analytics saves information about withdrawn items which can clutter up your analysis. Withdrawn items have a "Lifecycle" (under the "Physical Item Details" folder) of "Deleted." Current items have a "Lifecycle" of "Active."

Local Parameters

Alma Analytics allows us to set local parameters that correspond to select MARC fields for more direct filtering. Currently, there are four parameters set: Local Parameter 5 - 590 field; Local Parameter 7 - 776 field; Local Parameter 8 - 856 field; Local Parameter 9 - 976 field.

Alma Down Procedures

If Alma goes down, please consult the page and follow instructions to report.

Because extended Alma Down events have become infrequent, we will use to track loans when the system is now rather than the Alma Offline Circulation application. 

There are printed versions of the spreadsheet in the Emergency binder to use if the power is out or you can't access a digital copy of the spreadsheet but please use the digital one if at all possible. 

Returns should be gathered together on a cart labeled with the "Item Not Yet Checked In" sign.

Once Alma access is restored

  1. Use the backdate feature in the Check In Items Module <Procedures Needed/Linked to> to return items
    • Check the items on the cart against the spreadsheet to see if any are on the offline circulation spreadsheet. Do not check these out to the borrower!
  2. Use the the information on the spreadsheet to check items out to users that haven't been brought back while the system was down




Alternate Borrowers

This page is under construction. See policies here: https://library.oregonstate.edu/alternate-borrowers

Policy

An alternate borrower, Alma calls them a proxy user, is someone who is authorized to borrow materials on behalf of another person. The account holder is the person on whos account the items will be checked out. This can be set up temporarily (for example, to retrieve holds while quarantining) or permanently (for example, to allow a caregiver to pick up materials for you). Researchers will sometimes designate their research assistant as an alternate borrower.

  • Alternate borrowers cannot change account information or receive any information about the status of the patron's account.
  • Any OSU patron can have an alternate borrower set up and any OSULP cardholder can be an alternate borrower
    • Exception: Computer User Only cardholders
  • Account holders can have more than one alternate borrower or be the alternate borrower for more than one patron

Adding an Alternate Borrower (Proxy User) to Alma

  1. Only the account holder can designate other people to check items out for them.
    1. Alternate borrowers are not permitted to change any information on the account. 
    2. You are not permitted give any account information to the alternate borrower (fines, address, etc. this is patron confidentiality)
  2. The alternate borrower must also have an account in Alma; this means they will have an OSU or Convenience Card account.
  3. Ask the account holder on whose account items will be checked out on to fill out an Alternate Borrower Form.
  4. Open the patron record of the account holder:
    1. Click on their ID number
    2. Click on the "notes" tab
    3. Click the "add note" button
    4. In the note field add note: Alternate Borrower: Doe, John
    5. In the Type drop-down menu select: Circulation
    6. Select User Viewable, yes.
  5. Click Add/Close
  6. Open the Alternate Borrower's patron record:
    1. Click on their ID number
    2. Click on "proxy for" tab
    3. Search by name or ID number
    4. Click the "add user" button
    5. Click "save"
  7. Initial and date the application in the Office Use Only area "ALMA updated by" section
  8. Place the application in the Circulation Inbox

Removing an Alternate Borrower

When:

  1. An alternate borrower can asked to be removed.
  2. The account holder can asked for the proxy to be removed.

How:

  1. Go into the alternate borrower's account to the "Proxy For" tab
    1. Select the account holder member being removed and "delete," then save.
  2. Go into the "notes" tab of the account holder removing their alternate borrower
    1. Delete the "Alternate Borrower" note
    2. Delete the Alternate Borrower request form from the 'attachments' tab in Alma.

FAQ

How do I check out an item on the account holder's account for an alternate borrower?

  1. On the Patron Identification screen, check the Use proxy box
  2. Ask for the alternate borrower to swipe their OSU ID or library card
  3. In the Proxy For drop-down menu, choose the account holder's name, then click Go. 
  4. The account holder's account appears with the line "Proxy by (proxy user's name)" under the patron name. Check out the items as usual and click Done to email a receipt.

Caution: Alternate borrowers are also account holders.  Be careful to check out items on the correct account holder's account.

What if the account holder can't come to the library in person?

  1. If the account holder cannot bring the completed application in-person, they can submit it via their the contact email address in their library account.
    1. A staff member can email them a blank application form, but a signed form must be completed before the proxy user is added.

Where do I find a user's completed Alternate Borrower Form?

Completed alternate borrower forms are scanned and uploaded to the viewable from the "attachments" tab in Alma. 

April Zeller's 2019 SSD Conference notes & files

"Transforming Together: Building a Better Library"

The 25th Conference of the Support Staff Division of OLA. 

Tuesday, July 16, 2019. Monarch Hotel & Conference Center, Clackamas, OR

  • First, the 4pm traffic on I-205 north is nuts. I just want to get that out of the way. 
  • My review of the Monarch Hotel accomodations; they have a pool, the AC unit in my room was excellent, there was a mini-fridge in the room which is cool, the bed was "meh" and the sheets were scratchy, but overall not a bad location for a conference. During the conference the presentation rooms were freezing cold! 
  • Things I wish I would have known before going: no need to overpack other than a notebook and pen, bring cash for the raffle (a free night at the Sylvia Beach hotel) & massueses (there were massueses at the break,) dress in layers.

Session 1: Othering in the Library

  • Presentor: Sonja Ervin
  • This presentation went over some of the history of Oregon and how systems of oppression were built into Oregon law since the beginning of it's statehood, and how institutional rasicm is why there are such gross disparities between people of color and whites.
  • She shared this YouTube video from Walidah Imarisha, Why Aren't There More Black People in Oregon: https://youtu.be/FTZlNEZ3NEw
  • A lot of the message she was stressing was 'represenation matters.' We did a few exercises where we talked about our library collections and how much representation is in them by acting a role. Also staff demographics reflecting their patronage. 
  • Moving Forward and Taking Action
    • Be Aware and Check Your Privilege
    • What can you do to create a more inclusive environment?
    • What will you do to create a more inclusive environment at work?
    • Familiarize yourself with the diverse programs offered at the library (and on campus) and seek out opportunities to participate in events outside the library with cultures different from your own. 

Session 2: Promoting Democracy and Civic Engagement through Reference Services

  • Presentor: Donna Cohen
  • This presentation went through how you can use reference as a way to teach patrons how to engage in local, state, and national politics. She talked about why it's important to be a part of the poltiical process, and how citizens can make changes and make a difference. She went over why we shouldn't be afraid of the court system because the judicial process is how precidents are set and changes get made.
  • She went over some practical search advice; such as using site:gov to eliminate .com websites from searches, she went over how to find city & state ordinances, and also how to communicate with our legislators to get heard.
  • This link in particular caught my attention: Community Tool Box http://ctb.ku.edu/en but I have yet to explore the site. 
  • One point that really stuck with me is how one voice can spark a great change- she used an example of a facebook post which started a discussion in the community and eventually led to a law change. 

Session 3: Historical Trauma to Historical isdom: Better Understanding Your Tribal Neighbors

  • Presentors: Dr. Kelly Gonzales, Jennifer Pirtle
  • The presentation started with a native song- it was amazing! They talked about the importance of 'land acknowledgement' and the respect we should show for the first peoples. 
  • This presentation discussed the oppression of the Native American/Native Alaskan peoples especially in healthcare policies and poverty levels. She stressed that it's not about having white people swoop in and try to save them, but to build relationships on mutual respect and gain the trust of the community. She encourage everyone to step outside their own culture and take part in native events in your area. 
  • She asked what specifically each of our libraries is doing to bring native culture into people's consciencness and every group answered nothing. 
    • Both this presentation and Othering made me think of what I can do in my role at the library to increase awareness and inclusivity; my idea was to send a notice to the cultural centers on campus when I am hiring in order to encourage students to apply that might not normally think about applying with us. 

 

 

 

Associate

Information

  • Permanent employees of certain organizations and governmental agencies that are housed on OSU campuses and provide teaching, research or funding for OSU programs are eligible for an Associate ID card. Associates are eligible to purchase Recreational Sports (Dixon) memberships, ONID (OSU Network ID) accounts, OSU Card Cash account, and checking out materials at Valley Library. Associates are not eligible for free Corvallis Transit bus rides, remote access to Valley Library databases or interlibrary loan privileges (unless they have an ONID account.) Associate ID card fee is $30.00.
  • Check out privileges same as a Convenience Card. See Patron Application Matrices
  • If they don't have a OSU ID card they can contact their Verifier for any questions.
    • The (excel file) comes from the ID center.

Creating a Library Account

  1. Have the patron complete a Library Card Account Application Form.
    1. If the Associate has an OSU ID, verify their status using Atrium.
      1. In Atrium, their tag will say "PtAssociate"
    2. If they do not have an OSU ID, they will need a Convenience Card and must pay $1.
  2. Use the Associate's information to create a "Convenience Card" User Group account for the patron.
    1. If they have an OSU ID, use the ID card for their Primary Identifier and Barcode.
    2. If they need a Convenience Card, use the numbers from the card for their Primary Identifier and Barcode.

Reminder: No study rooms, no laptops, no kindles. They can get ILL/database access if they have an ONID account.

Atrium

How a Patron Can Change Their Password in Primo

  1. Click on My Account at the top right corner of the screen
  2. Have them login to their account by choosing “Community Cardholder” and entering their card number and supplied password (xxx-xxx-xxx, Smith2435)
  3. Choose "Personal Details" from the the My Account screen
  4. Click on "Update Login Credentials" in smaller box on the right side of the screen
  5.  
  6. A new boxes will appear. Enter the old password (for example Smith2435) and replace it with a new password at least 8 characters long containing upper and lower case letters and at least one number. Click update and the process is complete.

How to Use Atrium to Verify an OSU Status

Information

Atrium is the system we use to verify if someone is a part of the OSU System.

You should only use Atrium for official purposes - no searching for people you know for curiosity.

It is a real-time system and can verify new students/faculty/staff immediately. 

  1. https://oregonstate.atriumcampus.com/
  2. If you need the same username and password, please ask a staff member.

Remember that a person status of "Active" does not mean they are a student, staff or faculty. You need to check the tags listed at the bottom.

Here are a few of the tags in Atrium which indicates their user group:

  • PtStudent ← this is a student, in Alma the User Group will usually be "Undergrad" or "Post-Bacc"
  • PtEmployee ← this is a campus employee Staff or Faculty, in Alma the User Group will usually be "OSU Staff" or "OSU Faculty/GTA"
  • PtAssociate ← this is a tricky one, in Alma the User Group will usually be "Convenience Card" because most people who have an Associate status still only get Convenience Card level borrowing privileges

Verifying an OSU Patron

  1. Choose Login Method: Login with Atrium


  2. Click the "People" tab


  3. Enter the OSU ID number in the "Input Value" field with no dashes, no spaces
  4. There are alternate ways to search, such as by last name if you change the drop down menu from "University ID" to "Last Name". You should only need this if they are not providing an OSU ID, but an alternate form of ID such as driver's license. 
  5. If they show up with an "Active" status account, they are still part of the OSU system. Their scheduled date of deactivation is below their picture. (Since this example is a staff account rather than student it has a bit more information.) And their "tags" will determine their status.

Barcoding Materials at Checkout

Existing Bibliographic and Holdings Records

Alma allows staff to create and attach a temporary item record to an existing bibliographic and/or holdings record but don't do it! Accidentally attaching an item to the wrong record can cause problems for patrons and staff alike. Following the instructions below creates a completely temporary set of records (bibliographic, holdings, and item); this allows Cataloging to fix our records or start from scratch AND LEAD staff don't need to worry about creating a perfectly accurate record.

There's no barcode on the item I'm trying to check out or there is a barcode and an Item Not Found error is generated when I scan the barcode.

  1. Is it a Valley Library item not on the list below? Proceed
  2. Not a Valley Item? Fill out follow-up form using Interlibrary Loan/Summit category. Include patron information so we can follow up with them.

List of item types without barcodes that do not circulate:

  • Microfiche
  • Microfilm

Barcoding Procedure:

  1. Use the Alma Search Bar at top of the page 
  2. Change the first dropdown menu to Physical items
  3. Change the second dropdown menu to Permanent call number
    1. Type the call number the search box and search. Note: Spaces matter with call number searching.

  4. If item record is found (call number and description match exactly, no barcode or barcode starts with an i), attach the barcode.
    1. Click edit
    2. Place a barcode on the upper left corner of the item
    3. Select the Barcode field and scan the barcode on the item (it should save automatically)
    4. Return to the patron record and check out the item as normal
  5.  If item record is not found, create a temporary bibliographic and item record. 
    1. Return to the patron record
    2. Click on Create Item
    3. Choose Holding Type → New and Citation Type → Book
      1. Note: Do not use Existing, temporary item records should not be attached to existing records. 
    4. Enter item information → Title, Author, Call Number, Volume (if any), and Number (if any)
    5. Choose Library = Valley Library
    6. Choose Location = Valley BIB (vge)
      1. Note: Though other locations can be chosen as appropriate; Valley BIB is never wrong because the location determines loan periods and overdue fines.
    7. Place a barcode on the upper left corner of the front cover
    8. Select the Barcode field and scan the barcode (automatically saves) or enter the barcode by hand and click Save
    9. The item should now be checked out to patron 


Behavior Guidelines

As a reminder for both staff and student workers, here's what we've agreed upon for behavior at the Borrowing & Information Desk:

  • It is very important to be approachable and responsive, therefore:
    • We will select on-desk activities that allow us to be interrupted, face forward & have our eyes up, and which do not require intense concentration.
      • Bring conversations between staff and students to the front (avoid credenza conferences)
      • Avoid watching videos, playing video games, using your cell phone for social media, texting, etc.
    • We will eat away from the desk (covered drinks are fine)
    • We will keep the front desk work surfaces relatively clear of our stuff e.g., study items, personal tech devices, reading books, etc.
    • We will keep our conversations quiet, discreet, and on topics appropriate to be overheard by all.
  • We should and will leave the desk regularly to help patrons.
  • We should teach our patrons how to do things for themselves rather than simply doing it for them.
    • It’s okay for a line to form - slow down and focus on quality over speed.
  • We will do our best to have projects that can be done at the desk and a list of tasks to keep students busy.
    • After the task list and other projects have been completed, homework, web browsing, puzzles, etc. can be done on the desk computers.
  • It is our responsibility to oversee the student employees.
