Building Evacuation, Power Interruption/Outage Procedures

Whenever you update this page:

  • please print a copy for the Borrowing and Information Desk Doomsday Binder
  • please print copies for the red binders attached to the evacuation equipment in the book drop closet

Building Evacuation Procedures

When the fire alarm is activated:

Door Monitor North (Main Entrance) Responsibilities

Door Monitor East (Java II) Responsibilities

 Door Monitor West (Loading Dock) Responsibilities
Staff member (or Lead Student)
currently in charge of the desk		 Staff backup or Student Assistant Staff backup or Student Assistant
1. Collect equipment from book drop closet.
2. Evacuate building and meet at north end of library plaza (next to the grass in the quad).
3. Turn on radios to channel 3.
4. Assign door monitors to east (Java II) and west (loading dock) sides of building. Confirm your door monitor assignment with the lead staff member. Confirm your door monitor assignment with the lead staff member.

5. Call 9-1-1 and tell dispatch what you know about the evacuation. Use any available cell phone.

 Monitor east exits (Java II side of building). Using megaphone, keep people from entering building and keep people 50 feet away from building, directing them north to the library quad. Using radio (ch. 3), listen for instructions and report information other door monitors should know. If radios are not working, ask library staff to relay information to the other door monitors. Monitor west exits (loading dock side of building). Using megaphone, keep people from entering building and keep people 50 feet away from building, directing them north to the library quad . Using radio (ch. 3), listen for instructions and report information other door monitors should know. If radios are not working, ask library staff to relay information to the other door monitors.

6. Evenings/Weekends: Call library administrators in the following order until you reach someone. If no answer, leave a message with your name, the time, and whatever you know about the evacuation.

  • Anne-Marie Deitering: 503-348-5943
  • Rachel Burgess: 317-464-9225
  • Richenda Hawkins: 415-847-5438
  • Steve Weber: 206-327-4053
  • Sagan Wallace: 503-754-2905
  • for more, see section

7. Monitor main entrance (north). Using megaphone, keep people from entering the building and keep people 50 feet away from building, beyond the library plaza and walkways along the north side. Using radio (ch. 3), listen for instructions and report information other door monitors should know. If radios are not working, ask library staff to relay information to the other door monitors.

Building reentry (approved by fire department personnel):

Outside...

  • Using radio, communicate with the other door monitors.

  • Using megaphone, notify everyone that it is now OK to reenter the building. Walk toward back (south side) of building to be sure everybody hears your announcement.

Back inside...

  • Check in with lead staff member. You may be assigned to turn off emergency door alarms, reopen stairwell fire doors, check that elevators are working, or cover the desk.
  • Return equipment to book drop closet.

8. Building reentry (approved by fire department personnel):

Outside...

  • Using radio, communicate with the other door monitors.

  • Using megaphone, notify everyone that it is now OK to reenter the building.

Back inside...

  • Call back the library administrators you contacted earlier.
  • Assign staff to t urn off emergency door alarms, reopen stairwell fire doors, check that elevators are working, and cover the desk.
  • Fill out an Incident Report.
  • Return equipment to book drop closet.

9. Building closure (decided by fire department personnel):

  • Using radio, communicate with the other door monitors.
  • Using megaphone, notify everyone that the library has been closed.
  • Call back the library administrators you contacted earlier.
  • Take home evacuation equipment and return it the next day.
  • Fill out an Incident Report as soon as possible.

Building closure (decided by fire department personnel):

  • Using radio, communicate with the other door monitors.
  • Using megaphone, notify everyone that the library has been closed. Walk toward back (south side) of building to be sure everybody hears your announcement.
  • Take evacuation equipment to lead staff member at main entrance. Someone will have to take it home and return it the next day.

Power Interruptions

In the event of a power interruption (brief power blip or loss), some doors and equipment may need to be reset.

Throughout the building:

  • Fire doors (stairwells): Check that all fire doors in the stairwells are open and reopen as needed. Push the door into the open position until the magnet activates and holds it in place.
  • Scanners (2nd floor copy center, 1st, 3rd, and 5th floors): Reboot as needed (shut down if necessary, wait 30 seconds, then turn on).
  • Add Value machine (2nd floor copy center): Check the machine and as needed.
  • Kiosks (2nd & 4th floors): Check the machine and reboot as needed.
  • Compact shelving (1st floor): Given a power fluctuation, all modules will turn off. The modules can be turned back on with the manager key (also at Jim's desk). Be sure to make moveable again any carriages that have defaulted to stationary when the system was restarted. 

In the Borrowing & Information Desk area: 

  • Desk computers: If they shut down, reboot them and log back in to Alma and other programs. Reboot the dual-monitor station computer as needed.
  • Pagers: If the pagers are activated, unplug the charger base and plug it back in to reset them.
  • Self-checkout unit: as needed.

Learning Commons:

  • Learning Commons computers: Check all computers in the following order and reboot as needed:
    • Make sure all the printers and card swipe units are on and functioning.  If the card swipe units aren’t working, they have to be restarted by unplugging, then plugging back in.
    • ONID computers in the Learning Commons
    • Mothership computer in Kristin’s office that runs PC Reservation software
    • Valley Patron computers in the Learning Commons
  • If patrons have lost work, have them reopen the program and see if the file is in Recent Documents. If not, check the temporary files through the Start menu.

Follow the .

If the power does not return after 15 minutes

Contact library administrators. Library Administration will determine if the library will be evacuated or closed.

  • Weekdays: call Library Administration at 541-737-3411 (7-3411 from a campus phone)
  • Evenings and weekends: consult the  section and call library administrators in the order listed until you reach someone. If no answer, leave a message with your name, the time, and whatever you know about the power outage.

Building Evacuation

If Library Administration decides to evacuate the building:

  1. The Dean or designee will contact the LEAD head, who will notify the LEAD unit supervisors; if unreachable, directly contact the three LEAD unit managers, who will inform their employees. If a unit manager is unavailable another unit manager or LEAD department head will take point with their employees. 
  2. Make a PA announcement.
    • Script: "Your attention please. The library is being evacuated due to the power outage. Use the stairs and exit via the main entrance. Do not use elevators. If you are unable to use stairs, wait on the stair landings for assistance."
    • Make the announcement at 15-minute intervals.
  3. Call the Department of Public Safety dispatch at the non-emergency number (541-737-3010) to inform them of the evacuation.
  4. Lock the main entrance doors (2nd floor and Java II) and assign door monitors to prevent people from entering the building.
  5. If the power returns and the building reopens:
    1. unlock the doors
    2. inform the people waiting outside
    3. follow the .
  6. If the power does not return and the building is closed:
    1. inform the people waiting outside
    2. follow the .

Building Keys

The Building Key Coordinator is part of Spaces department. Any concerns and questions can be directed to the coordinator by any of the following methods:

  • emailing , the Building Key Coordinator
  • emailing mailto:library.maintenance@oregonstate.edu
  • filling out a follow-up form under the "Building Issues" category

Overview

  • Building keys and key cards are cataloged in Alma and stored in the Locked Closet. 
  • Most keys are labeled by who uses them or what areas they open. While there will always be room for exceptions, below is a list of general permissions guidelines.
    • Keys and key cards that work on external doors (doors through which you enter Valley Library) only go to staff. 
    • Keys that open internal doors will usually have a tag with a list of names.
    • Key cards that open staff areas are usually for staff only. If they are for student workers, they will have a list of names on the tag.
    • Keys that open cabinets, etc. will not usually have a list of names and can be loaned to staff and student workers.
  • Key loan period is one day but can be extended when appropriate.

Procedures

Checking out keys and key cards

  1. Find appropriate key in locked closet.
  2. When necessary, verify patron has appropriate permissions.
    1. If the key tag has a list of names, is the patron listed on the tag?
    2. Is the key a staff only key? Is the patron Library staff?
  3. Check out the key.

Checking in keys and key cards

  1. Check in key.
  2. Put key back in locked closet on the key rack in labeled spot.

Key Permissions

  1. Keys that are checked out to Library Staff only:
    1. Library Master key - Master key for the entire building
  2. Keys with an tag that are for the staff in that area only
    1. Archives (Rm. 3169) (updated list of authorized users attached)
    2. SMS Event Tech Key (4th floor offices)
    3. Recycling (loading dock and all dock elevator lobbies) 


Building Things

Canceling Reservations

Users can cancel reservations by clicking the link in their confirmation email. We can also do it for them on request in the staff side interface.

When a person is at least 20 minutes late to check into their reservation and pick up a keycard, we will cancel their reservations so the others might use the room.

Procedure for Canceling Reservations

  • Go to Booking Grid & Availability Tab
  • Select Category
  • Click Go

  • Red line shows now. Look two boxes to the right of the line to find possible reservations to cancel
  • Solid red indicates that the reservation hasn’t been checked in to yet
  • Before canceling check to see if keycards are both in its slot
  • Click on the reservation and scroll to the bottom of the page.
  • Click on Cancel All

  • Make sure Send Email to notify user is selected.
  • Add message in Additional Information field. “Your reservation was canceled because the start time was more than 15 minutes ago and the room’s keycard wasn’t picked up.”
  • Click on Cancel Booking


Changing a Reservation Time

  • Find the reservation you'd like to change.
  • Click on the Date/Time link

  • Set a new start time

  • Warning: When changing a start time the reservation length will stay the same by default.  This means you must adjust the end time if you want it to end at the same time as the original reservation.

  • Click Update Booking button.



Check In

truenone


This page focuses on the Alma part of the checking in process. Check out the page for information about where books get returned and how the cart is managed.

Quick Reference:

  1. Check for damage
  2. Go to Alma > Return Items
  3. Scan in the barcode
  4. Check what the "next steps" say and follow them

What gets checked in?

  • All OSU-owned materials (books, media, laptops, equipment) - see below for specific procedures
  • Some room keys
  • All Summit returns

ILLiad (ILL) items do NOT get checked in by LEAD. Use a highlighter to draw a line through the bookstrap and place it on the second shelf of the check-in cart.

How To Check In Items

Best practices:

  • Save check-ins for non-busy times at the desk. Do not try to multitask
  • If in doubt, don't check it in. Add a note and place it on the bottom shelf of a cart

OSU-owned items:

    1. Check over the item for any damage.

If it is damaged, do not check it in, but instead follow the procedure listed .

  1. Navigate to the Return Items page. Make sure the "Place directly on hold shelf" toggle is set to Yes.
  2. Scan the item's barcode. Watch for any pop-up messages!
    1. No pop-ups? Check the Next Steps:
      1. If it is shelved in the main collection, place the item on the top shelf of the Checked-in Cart in rough call number order (i.e. to the first cutter).
      2. If it is shelved anywhere else, add a bookmark and place it on the bottom shelf of the Checked-in Cart. Items to be shelved on the 2nd floor can either be placed on the bottom shelf, or you can shelve them as you have time.
    2. Pop-ups?
      1. Item is on hold for a patron: Go to scan in items. Make "Place directly on hold shelf" is set to Yes. Print the hold slip. Place this slip in the book and shelve on the Hold Shelf.
      2. Item should be sent to a different location: Place a laminated bookmark in the book and set the book on the bottom shelf of the cart to indicate it needs special processing.
  3. Once the cart is full or it is the end of the day, deliver it to the 3rd floor annex. 

Summit Items:

    1. Check over the item for any damage.

If it is damaged, do not check it in. Add a Damaged bookmark, write the date returned on it, and place the book on the bottom shelf of the Checked-in cart. Fill out a LEAD Follow up Form and select category 'Damaged'.

  1. Navigate to the Return Items page.
  2. Scan the item's barcode. A pop-up message will appear stating it is a Summit item. Click OK.
  3. Draw a line through the book strap or sticker using a highlighter. Do not use Sharpies as these can bleed through and damage the book.
  4. Place the book on the 2nd shelf of the Checked-in Cart.

ILL items:

  1. Draw a line through the book strap or sticker using a highlighter. Do not use Sharpies as these can bleed through and damage the book.
  2. Place the book on the 2nd shelf of the Checked-in Cart.

How to Check In an Item in Alma

  • Navigate to the Return Items page
  • Backdate the return if necessary, such as if you find something on the shelf that didn't get checked in (see 'Waiving fines for library mistakes' below).
  • Scan the item barcode
    • Important: Check the "Next Step" column for any special instructions
    • "Reshelve to Valley Bib" means this gets shelved upstairs like normal
    • If the item is on hold, you'll see a message pop up and a hold slip prints. Place the slip in the book and shelve it with the other holds
    • Any Next Step that is not "Reshelve to Valley Bib" should get a laminated bookmark (ex: Guin-HMSC, Storage, etc.) and be placed on the bottom shelf of the cart.

Avoid using Scan In Items or the Return tab in a patron's account to return items. Only use the Return tab if the patron requests a Return Receipt.

Return Receipts

Sometimes a patron returns library materials to the Circulation desk and specifically asks us to check in the materials there and provide a receipt. With the exception of ILL materials, we can do this in Alma. 

Anything but ILL materials
  1. Bring up the patron record in Alma, and click the Returns tab.
  2. Scan each item barcode and watch the screen carefully for messages–either in pop-up windows or in the Next Step column.
  3. When you are finished, click on Send Return Receipt (below the Active balance link) to send an email to the patron summarizing the batch of items you've checked in.
  4. Click Done to exit the patron's account.
  5. Explain that the patron will receive an email listing the items returned.
  6. If you returned the items and closed the patron's record before clicking Send Return Receipt, you will need to go back into the patron's record, select the Returns tab, change the drop-down bar to say All instead of This Session, then when the returns show up you can print the page from your web browser.
ILL materials
  1. Explain to the patron that ILL items cannot be checked in by us at the Circulation desk; they can only be checked in by the ILL staff because they are in a separate system and we don't have access to it. Assure the patron that the ILL items will be routed upstairs to the ILL office for check-in during their business hours. ILL materials do not accrue overdue fines on days the ILL office is closed.

Backdating Items

If an item wasn't checked in on time, the return should be backdated in Alma. Note: Backdating can also be used to prevent fines when an item is checked out but found on the shelf. Otherwise, incorrect fines will need to be waived from the patron's account. This method makes Alma think that the item was returned before it became overdue.

  1. In Alma, go to Return Items and click  Change Return Date. The Select Return Date dialog box opens.
    1. Click in the  Return Date  box and select the appropriate return date from the calendar. To prevent fines, pick a return date & time PRIOR to when the item went overdue. Items cannot be backdated prior to their loan date. 
    2. Click in the At (HH:MM) box and enter the appropriate time in 24-hr format. When the time is not specified, Alma uses the closing time of the new return date. If you're backdating several days in the past, it's fine to leave this field empty.
  2. Click Submit. The new return date will display next to the Change Return Date button.
  3. Scan the barcode of the item(s).
  4. Click Reset Return Date. The return date will be reset to the current date.

Previous Patron Information

To determine the last patron to have an item, check the "History" tab in the item record :

  1. In Alma, open the item record.

  2. In the item record, click on the History tab and then on Fulfillment activities directly below that.

    1. Note: Alma runs a job (Fulfillment – Handle Historical Archiving ) at 11pm that removes the names & IDs of previous patrons from the item history.


Checking in "Lost" items

See the page for information about items placed in lost status.

Policies for returning lost general collection items are on the library's policies page.

As long as the item has not been caught in the "close lost loans" job (which happens slightly more than 1 year after it was set to "lost" status) it can still be checked in.

You can still check in items that are "Lost" if the patron's account is expired, as long as they still have an account in the system.

BNC Textbook Lending Program Books

The BNC lends textbooks to underprivileged students for a whole term, similar to our Course Reserves collection. These are all labelled with a large "HSRC" or "BNC" sticker on the front cover.

To return these:

  1. Follow the above
  2. The "Next Step" column on the "Return Items" screen should say "HSRC Textbook Lending Program"
  3. Place the books on the BNC/Public Library returns shelf below the incoming Course Reserves books shelf.

Checking the printer status for BLACK/WHITE PRINTERS

How do I know the trays need a fill?

Check the status column and when it says 20-40% then it needs to be filled (beginning with tray 5).

How do I know the ink needs to be replaced?

Check the top left "non-HP Black Cartridge" and if it is at 1% (or when it says we have 450 pages left to print) then we change the ink. Or when a patron states the printer isn’t printing correctly (fading lines or faded text).

How do I know the maintenance kit needs to be replaced?

Look at the top left of the page and it will say "Maintenance kit  needs replaced” -  even though it is at 0% and it says we need to change it - we only change it when the printer begins to have problems (paper jams in the left door continuously).

How do I know the waste cartridge needs to be replaced?

Change it when a message pops-up saying the Waste Cartridge needs replaced.


Adding paper correctly to prevent jams:

  • Add paper without creases or bent corners.
  • Keep all sliders aligned and tight against the paper.

Checking the printer status for COLOR PRINTERS

How do I know the trays need a fill?

The white part of the numbers "1 2 3 4" will show grey as the amount of paper in each tray decreases.  Add paper when it is at 20- 40%.

How do I see tray 4? 

Click the second dot under tray 3.

How do I know the ink needs to be replaced?

The "C M Y K" refer to the colors for the printer. You can see the percentage as well as a visual for how much ink is left. We only change it when it is at 1%. 

How do I know the waste cartridge needs to be replaced?

A message will pop up at the top when it needs to be replaced.


Adding paper correctly to prevent jams:

  • Add paper without creases or bent corners.
  • Keep all sliders aligned and tight against the paper.

If the color printer is jamming repeatedly or displaying issues with a paper tray, check the settings - on the printer - for that printer tray (before replacing the maintenance kit):

  • The screen on the printer tells you where the jam is and instructs you on removing the jammed paper.
  • If there is a vertical rectangle on the paper tray setting screen, check that the printer paper is loaded vertically.
  • If there is a horizontal rectangle on the paper tray setting screen, the printer paper should be loaded horizontally.
  • The rectangle icon is very small and easy to miss:

Checkout

truenone

Basic checkout

Check out OSU and Summit items using the Manage Patron Services screen in Alma.

  1. Have the patron swipe or tap their card to bring up their Alma account
  2. If the patron doesn’t have their ID card, ask for their OSU ID #. Ask them their name to confirm that you have found the right account.
  3. If they don't know their OSU ID #, you can look them up by name. However, this is the easiest way to get into the wrong account so take your time and ask for an additional piece of information from the account to verify.
  4. Scan the item barcode.
  5. Watch the screen at each scan to ensure that each item is checking out.
  6. State the due dates and due times aloud to the patron.
  7. Be sure to click Done when the transaction is complete, otherwise the patron won't receive their email receipt.

If an item won’t check out for any other reason, do not give it to the patron, get a staff member for help. A staff member can determine whether an exception can be made or not.

Click here for how to make an exception...

If you try to check out an item and get the following message, that means that item is not configured to check out to that patron in Alma. I.e., Alma does not have any rules that let that item be checked out by that patron.

If you click Override and check the item out to the patron, Alma is going to make the due time the same as the check out time! Again, this is because Alma is not configured to connect that item to that patron.

If a staff member makes the judgement call to allow that patron to have the item, you will have to use Change due date to move the due time forward so that it's not due immediately.

Checking out materials to a proxy user

Patrons can designate other people to check out materials for them. We call them . They are called "proxy users" in Alma.

When a proxy user comes to pick up items for the faculty member:

  1. Ask for the proxy user's OSU ID or library card
  2. On the Patron Identification screen, check the Use proxy box.
  3. Swipe the proxy user's card
  4. In the Proxy For drop-down menu, choose the name of the person they are checking out items for, then click Go. 
  5. The account appears with the line "Proxy by (proxy user's name)" under the patron name. Check out the items as usual and click Done to email a receipt.

Non-circulating items that don't check out

Non-circulating items are designated for use in the library only. Patrons should be encouraged to scan and/or copy the pages that they need to access outside of the library.

Procedures for checking out items that don't have a barcode or have a barcode but generate an Item Not Found error when you try to check them out.

Interlibrary Loan (ILL) checkout using ILLiad Web Circulation

  1. Have the patron swipe or tap their ID to verify identity and check name then retrieve the ILL item from the hold shelf.
  2. Bring up ILLiad Web Circulation in a browser tab.
  3. Make sure cursor is in the Check Out box.
  4. Scan the barcode on the ILL label on the front of the item.
    • If the barcode won't scan, type the TN number into the Check Out box.
  5. Point out and state aloud the due date (highlighted in yellow) to the patron.

Circulation Statistics Instructions

Circulation statistics for Valley, Guin and OSU/Cascades are completed at the beginning of each month. They consist of gathering and tallying monthly departmental statistics and entering them into an Excel worksheet.  

A yearly report is done on the 11th day of July by the department head. The yearly statistics are the completed version of the July-June monthly statistics and, after being reviewed by the Dept. Head, are forwarded to Library Administration Office.

Note:  These statistics are collected, tallied and entered by the Circulation supervisor or assigned staff.

1st day of the Month:

1. Collect Gate Count Statistics

  • Retrieve and total the Gate Count Sheet (found in the opening folder at the Circulation counter – replace with a new Gate Count Sheet).
    • Look down through the days to see if the gate count starts over again. The gate counter counts up to 1,000,000.  Therefore, if the counter reaches 1,000,000 in the middle of the month, subtract the number from the first day of the month from 1,000,000 and then add this to the number from the last day of the month. This will be the raw total.
    • Subtract the first day of the month and the first day of the next month, divide the raw total by 2 (accounts for patrons entering and exiting). This will be the total you will list in the Excel file.
  • Enter the daily gate counts into the DailyGateCounts.xlsx file located at S:\IUS\IUS Dept\Statistics. Note any holidays or days closed. Shortened hours or non-scheduled closures should be noted with comments. When finished upload to the Wiki within the CRSD Statistics page. 

2. Open the CRSD Monthly Stats worksheet

  • Open Excel and navigate to \\cn-share\Library\IUS\IUS Dept\Statistics\
  • Select the current CRSD Stats file.  (e.g. CRSD stats 2013-14.xls). Open Monthly Stats worksheet.

3.  Open the Innopac Millennium Web Management Reports

  • Open Internet Explorer or Firefox
  • Enter url address; http://128.193.4.75:4448/managerep/mainview/0/
  • Under Circulation category, click on the Circ Activity box
  • Enter your Millennium initials and password 

4. Enter Statistics into the CRSD Monthly Stats Worksheet

  • Gate Count - Valley: Enter the total from the Gate Count sheet on the Gate count – Valley (line 6)
  • Innopac Millennium Web Management Reports
  • Total Borrowers

          a. Click on Hourly under the Circ Stats category

           b. Click on Patrons under Total category and click on Submit button. 

           c. Check to see that the heading denotes the month you would like to collect statistics for. If not, click on Recalculate and select the correct month and year and Submit Query.

                          

           d. Click on the up/down arrow key until Group 102 report appears

                           

           e. Enter total at the bottom of the TOTAL column under the appropriate month of the Monthly Stats worksheet Borrowers row (line 5)

                        

5. Circulation – Valley, Guin, OSU/Cascades

a. Click on Checkout under Circ Stats

b. Click on Last Mo under Dates

c. Click on One only under Locations

d. Click on I type under Type and click on Submit 

e. Click on Submit (Valley Library should be the default)

           

        f. Enter the total under the QTY column on the Circulation – Valley_ (line 10) row of the Monthly Stats worksheet

            

g. Click on Recalculate and repeat for Guin (line 15) and OSU/Cascades (Line 18). 

1) for OSU/Cascades, only record the statistics with lines beginning with Cascade. COCC statistics are for Central Oregon Community College.

6. Renewals - Valley, Guin, OSU/Cascades

a. Click on Renewal under Circ Stats

        b.. Click on Submit

        c. Enter the total under the QTY column on the Renewals – Valley (line 11) row of the Monthly Stats worksheet

                    

e. Click on Recalculate and repeat for Guin (line 16) and OSU/Cascades (Line 19). 

1) for OSU/Cascades, only record the statistics with lines beginning with Cascade. COCC statistics are for Central Oregon Community College.

     

7. Study Rooms, Laptops, Course Reserves – Valley

a. Click on Checkout under Circ Stats

        b. Click on Submit and Recalculate

        c. Click on Submit (Valley Library should be the default in Locations Served)

        d. Enter the QTY (quantity) Study Rooms – Valley (line 21), Laptops – Valley (line 22), Course Reserves (line 23) row of the Monthly Stats worksheet

                      

8. Recalls – Valley, Guin, OSU/Cascades

a. Click on All Activity under Circ Stats

        b. Click on Item Location and Submit 

        c. Add up all Valley (t** & v** codes) location totals under the H1/RECLL column and enter the results on the Recalls – Valley (line 29) row of the Monthly Stats worksheet

                  

          d. Add up Guin (h***) locations under the Hl/RECLL column and enter on the Recalls - Guin (line 30) row of the Monthly Stats worksheet

                  

          e. Add up the OSU/Cascades (ec**) locations under the Hl/RECLL column and enter on the Recalls – OSU/Cascades (line 31) row of the Monthly Stats worksheet

                   

 

5. Checked In - Valley & Guin

  • Valley Checked In: Go back to the Circulation Activity by Item Location report in the Innopac Millennium Web Management Report. Under the CHKINS column, subtract locations starting with e, h, m,vrb, vili from the grand total under the CHKINS column. Enter the total on the Checked in (line 40) 
  • Guin Check In: Enter the CHKINS column for locations starting with h (line 43)   

7. Save and close the CRSD Stats Excel file

8. File the Gate Count statistics sheet with the Circulation Statistics Coordinator.

Closing/Opening a room

Sometimes a room needs to be closed because of an emergency maintenance need, lost key cards, etc.

Whenever possible, close the room by changing the room status instead of blocking out the room with a booking.

  • Blocking out rooms by creating a booking interferes with accurate usage statistics.
  • This can only be done by staff, not student employees because it requires Admin level permissions.

Updating Room Status

Changing the status of a room requires an account with Admin level permissions. All LEAD staff have Admin permissions. The service desk accounts do not. 

Updated instructions for changing room status can be found at Springshare. You must be logged into your LibCal account to access this link.

Brief overview of steps

  • In the ribbon menu at the top of the page, Select Admin, then Spaces and Equipment.
  • Under the Locations tab, locate the Valley Library location. Click on the hyperlink in the Spaces column.
  • Locate the room that needs closing and click the edit space icon (box with a pencil) for that space.
  • Click the Status tab.
    • To close a room, change the status to Inactive.
    • To open a room, change the status to Active.
  • Click the Save Settings button or the status will not be changed.

Closing PA Announcements Script

30 Minutes Before Closing

"Good evening. The library will close in 30 minutes."

15 Minutes Before Closing

"Good evening. The library will close in 15 minutes. If you have any library materials to return or borrow, please bring them to the desk at this time."

5 Minutes Before Closing

"The library will close in 5 minutes. Please prepare to leave the building at this time."

At Closing

"The library is now closed. Have a good night!"

Whenever you update this page, please print it and replace the laminated copy located near the microphone.

Concierge Service

Below is historic information about the concierge program including links to statistics spreadsheets.

Concierge Planning Notes  as of 8/30/15

  • Hours staffed--10am-4pm, Monday-Wednesday

Confidentiality of Records

Confidentiality of Records

Patron information is strictly confidential. It is for the use of library staff and patrons only. Patron information IS NOT to be given out to parents, friends, professors, university administrators, police, FBI, university security staff, or the CIA. Only a court order can require the disclosure of patron records. The university librarian is responsible for compliance with such orders.

The Oregon State University Libraries follow Oregon state law which exempts libraries from public disclosure of “the records of a library, including (a) circulation records, showing use of specific library material by a named person; (b) the name of a library patron together with the address or telephone number of the patron; and (c) the electronic mail address of a patron.” (ORS 192.355.23)

This means you give no information to anyone.  Ever. If someone insists, get a staff member.

Staff Responsibilities

Permission to Release Student Education Records

Students may allow the release of their library information to specific persons by completing a Permission to Release Student Education Records form. Contact the Department Head for this.

OSU Libraries will maintain this disclosure authorization as long as the specific records disclosed are maintained by OSU according to its Records Retention Schedule. The release will expire one year from the date of signing unless an earlier date is specified.

More Information

Convenience Card Accounts

Information

  • Any Oregon resident, minor, Associate, OSU Alumni, Oregon Passport patron, EPA, oSU Retired, GWLA member or OCLC member can get a Concenience Card
  • 30 day check out period, max. 25 items, 3 renewals
  • Required
    1. Government issued photo ID
      1. Drivers license, passport, military ID, etc.
    2. Proof of Oregon address (either ID, or mail)
      1. They must be an Oregon resident, or part of OCLC or GWLA
    3. We are no longer charging for cards as of 2021 $1 for the Convenience Card
      1. This can be paid at a later date

Determine Eligibility

Who can have a Convenience card?

The convenience card is the card that we give to many of our non-OSU patrons, but is also given to those that are on campus, but not technically part of OSU.

Patrons:

Description:

Residents

Includes any person who currently lives or pays property taxes in Oregon and has proof of address.

This DOES NOT INCLUDE anyone using an Oregon "General Delivery" address at the post office.

Minors

A minor is anyone under the age of 16. Oregon residence and Parent/Guardian signature required.

Alumni

Includes anyone with a current OSU Alumni Association card. Alumni can live anywhere in the world (don't have to have an Oregon address) as long as they are an OSU Alumni Association member.

As a courtesy to OSU Alumni Association members, we waive the $1 fee for the convenience card.

Library privileges include borrowing at the Valley Library and the Guin Library at HMSC; their privileges don't include ONID computer use or remote access to online databases that require an ONID.

Oregon Passport Program

Anyone who has a library card at these participating libraries can also get a library card from us!

Here is a list of participating Oregon Passport Program libraries; http://www.olaweb.org/passport-directory

EPA

Environmental Protection Agency: Any member of the EPA with an EPA issued identification. Not all EPA members have OSU ID.

OSU Retired

An individual has retired from OSU if he or she has terminated from the University and is immediately drawing benefits or retirement allowances from their retirement plan offered through OSU employment.
GWLA

A member of the 

Greater Western Library Alliance

What is GWLA?

The Greater Western Library Alliance (GWLA) is a consortium of 36 research libraries located in the central and western United States.

GWLA is a dynamic, effective, project-oriented consortium, nationally recognized as a leader in the transformation of scholarly communication, and a facilitator in the application of new information technologies.

What does that mean to me?

Members of GWLA can get a convenience card and check out materials. They do not need to be residents of the state of Oregon, but they do need to be a member of one of the GWLA institutions.

Here is a list of the GWLA participating institutions; GWLA Members

What do I do differently?

  • First, bring up the list of GWLA institutions, and check that their institution is on the list.
  • They need to have a University ID for their University, and $1 for the card. Otherwise, everything else is the same as a Convenience Card!
  • At the top of the Library Card Application, where it says "Where did you hear about our resident patron card?" put: "GWLA member," and the University they are affiliated with.

Associate

Permanent employees of organizations or federal agencies housed on OSU campus, providing teaching, research, or funding to OSU are eligible for the associate status.
OCLC

A member of the 

Online Computer Library Center

What is OCLC?

The Online Computer Library Center (OCLC) is a nonprofit cooperative organization "dedicated to the public purposes of furthering access to the world's information and reducing information costs".

OCLC is a global library cooperative that provides shared technology services, original research and community programs for its membership and the library community at large.

What does that mean to me?

Members of OCLC can get a convenience card and check out materials. They do not need to be residents of the state of Oregon, but they do need to be a member of one of the OCLC institutions.

Here is a list of the OCLC participating institutions; OCLC PDF list of participating institutions

What do I do differently?

  • First, bring up the list of OCLC institutions, and check that their institution is on the list.
  • They need to have a University ID for their University, and $1 for the card. Otherwise, everything else is the same as a Convenience Card!
  • At the top of the Library Card Application, where it says "Where did you hear about our resident patron card?" put: "OCLC member," and which University they are affiliated with.

Creating an Account

  1. Look up the patron BY NAME in Alma
    1. If you find an expired account for the patron, see Expired Patron Accounts .
    2. If the patron was once a student, and is now a convenience card patron, get a staff member! Only they have the permissions to toggle the account type.
    3. If you find 2 or more records for the patron, fill out a Follow Up form so staff can merge the records. Continue with the Convenience Card record.
  2. Match the address from the goernment ID or mail to the one on the application.
    1. The mail should be something official, like a phone bill.
    2. If the addresses are different, ask teh patron for proof of current address.
      • If they don't have proof, they need to come back when they do. They cannot check out items until we have proof of address.
  3. Retrieve a convenience card from the drawer or one of the baskets on the desk.

  4. In ALMA, under >Fulfillment > Check Out/Check In > Manage Patron Services > Register New User

    Click to enlarge image of Alma screenshots: (there are two)

  5. Enter the User details:  

    1. Fill out each required field with the information on the application.
      1. Legal Name: First name, Middle name, Last name
      2. Preferred Name: First name, Middle name, Last name (as applicable)
      3. Primary Identifier: the 9 digit Convenience Card number located on the back of the Convenience Card and starts with 000
        use the dash format so the patron can access their library account, example: 000-633-131
         
      4. User Group: Select Convenience card group from drop down menu
      5. Campus: Select correct campus from drop down menu (OSU Main Campus)
      6. Birth date
      7. Expiration Date: one year from date of record creation
        1. NO purge date, leave this blank.
      8. User Management Information
        Patron has institutional record: No 
      9. Password = Patron last name (1st letter capital) and last 4 digits of ID no.

         If the patron's last name is 3 letters or less, add extra digits of the ID no. so total characters = 8

        (i.e., for a 3 letter last name add the last 5 digits of the patrons ID no.)

         The last name follows the following rules:

        1. No punctuation
        2. No hyphen
        3. No spaces
        4. Example:
          • John Mac Gruder-Smith with ID# 000-186-954 would have the following password:“MacGruderSmith6954”
      10. Verify Password: same as above
      11. Email address: check appropriate box and enter email address
        1. If the patron does not have an email address put: noemail@noemail.com
      12. Addresses: Select Address type as "Work" and enter the patron's mailing address
      13. Phone number: Select appropriate box and enter telephone number area code first.
        Use format: ### ###-####
        1. Click to enlarge this image



        3.
  6. Choose Update User to add Alternate ID and Patron Barcode
    1. Click on their ID number to enter their account.
      1. Click the "Identifiers" tab
        1. Click: Add Identifier
          1. Choose Identifier Type = Additional ID 1
          2. Value = Alternate ID Number (example: drivers license or passport number)
          3. Enter the ID type in the notes field (example: ODL, US passport, military ID, etc.)
          4. Add  
        2. Click: Identifier Type = Barcode
          1. Value = swipe the Convenience Card, it will populate the barcode from the card. (example: 110000000001)
      2. Add and Close
      3. A completed Library Card Application
      4. Click on the image to enlarge
  7. Ask the patron for the $1. We can only take exact change. Place the money in the slot of the cash box and fill out the circulation cash ledger.

    • If the patron doesn't have a $1, they can try to get exact change from Java II or they can pay later.

    • If they pay later, add a note into their record (never add a fine for their library card)



      How to add a "note"




  8. Review - are all the fields filled out?
  9. In the Staff Use section of the application form:
    1. Check off that you verified photo ID & address
    2. Check off what you did with the fee, whether the patron paid today or will pay later
    3. Check off if the patron are coming to us as part of the Oregon Passport Program.
      1. Link to information about Oregon Passport Program
    4. If this a Summit Institution patron; write down the name of their institution and their school ID number
    5. If this is an Affiliate patron; write down the name of their spouse/partner
    6. If this is an OSU student/faculty/staff; write down their OSU ID number
    7. If this is a Convenience card account; write down the Convenience card number
    8. Enter today's date and your initials
      1. If you are making an account exception (staff or lead only) for any reason please make a note on the application for review.
  10. Place the application in the Circulation Inbox
  11. Information for the Patron

Please be sure to present your Government Issued Photo ID with your library card at checkout.

Please sign the back of your library card, a fine tip Sharpie marker works best on the hard plastic.

You may check out up to 25 items at a time, for up to 30 days at a time, with a maximum of 120 days. Media collection items, such as DVDs, have a 1 week checkout, with a maximum of 4 weeks. Lockers check out for 3 days.

Your items will renew automatically unless they are otherwise requested, have a block on your account, or your account is expired/expiring.

We recommend you change your password in your library account upon receipt of your new card.

    • Go to The Valley Library website, on the right corner there is a link for "My Account" 
    • Sign in as a Community Cardholder
    • On the left there should be a link to Personal Settings
    • Click on Edit Details
    • Click on Update Login Credentials (here is where you change your password)
    • Click Update when finished.

Please be sure to keep your email address on file current, that’s how we send you notifications such as due dates. You can change this by logging into your account online, or by contacting the circulation desk.

Your library account will expire within 1 year of creation, in order to keep it open another year contact the Circulation desk so we may verify your account information is still accurate. Circulation (541) 737-7254.

You may also use your library account to use one of the eight guest internet computers in the Collaborative Learning Center located near the Information Desk on the second floor for up to 3 hours per day. To log in the username is your library card number.

Cross-training Program Procedures and Expectations

Welcome to the LEAD Cross-Training Program!

The purpose of this program is to give LEAD students the opportunity to not only learn new skills and work in different units (Circulation, Info Desk, Building Crew) but also to be a valued part of another unit and be able to serve as backup if needed.

We do require a student employee to have worked here for 1 year or if a supervisor feels you are ready. We would like you to feel very comfortable at your current postion first.

You will also need to have time available, at least 2 hours per week, to train and work at the other desk. If you are at 20 hours per week you will need to work with your supervisor to arrange a schedule.

The program is scheduled term by term so you always have the option of continuing or not participating each term.

Your true supervisor will still be the supervisor who hired you.

You will clock in under your normal assignment and receive the same rate of pay.

How it works

  • Your supervisor will ask you each term if you are interested in cross-training and which unit (Circ, Info Desk or Building Crew). If you have already been cross-trained you will be asked if you would like to continue.
  • If so, your supervisor will contact the cross-training unit supervisor and they will contact you about scheduling.
  • Once you have a schedule you will train and work with the new unit. You will also serve as a back up if available.
  • At the end of the term we will ask you to complete a survey of how it went for you! Your cross-training supervisor may also be asked to contribute to your annual evaluation.
  • That is all! Enjoy your new work experience!

 

Cross-Training Students in LEAD Program

Student Supervisors for Cross-Training Program

  • Circulation - Bryan Feyerherm, back up April Zeller
  • Information Desk - Erin Kooyman, back up Kristin Swetland
  • Building Crew - Rachel Ziegler, back up Lucinda Amerman

Definitions

  • Immediate supervisor - supervisor who hired the student employee.
  • Cross-training supervisor - supervisor who will be cross-training the student. 

Overview

LEAD will be offering student employees the opportunity to cross-train between the Circulation and Information Desks and Building Crew. This will allow student employees to acquire new skills in different areas of LEAD and to have student employees trained for backup. Cross-trained student employees will learn about how the department works as a whole.  Cross-trained students will not be fully trained as regular students are but will be able to fullfill a backup (baseline) role. The program will be offered each term on a volunteer basis.

Selecting Students

Interested students will be selected based on having at least one year library experience or deemed ready by their immediate supervisor.

Procedure

  • The immediate supervisor inquires with eligible student employees before the beginning of the next term to see if they are interested in the program or in continuing the program. Too many students leave during break so training will begin early the next term. We are also fairly slow at that time.
  • The immediate supervisor informs the cross-training supervisor of their interest.
  • If approved by the cross-training supervisor, both supervisors will arrange for scheduling needs and provide the student with . Approval includes having the time for training and available scheduling for cross-trained students.

Training

The unit that the student will be cross-training with will provide baseline training for the student employee and introduce the students to staff.

Once the student has been trained they will be available for backup duty and receive a Cross-training button.

Lead students can help with the training.

Once fully trained the cross-training supervisor will inform the rest of the unit's staff on their availability as a backup.

Scheduling

WTW schedules will be combined under one account so students will only need one login to access their schedules.

Cross-training students will be scheduled at least 2 hours per week in the other unit. Students may add the hours to their schedule or replace hours in their current schedule as long as a replacement is found and with supervisor approval. If the student is already working 19-20 hours per week they will need to adjust their original schedule to stay within 20 hours per week.

The unit cross-training the student will arrange for training times and scheduling the student. 

Budget

Cross-training student employees will clock in under their original assignment (Circ, Info Desk, Building Crew). They will receive their normal pay rate.

We also have the option of sending UABC a new SERF for the cross-training assignment/job title.

Feedback

At the end of each term each cross-trained student will be asked to complete a survey on their experience with the program. 

The students immediate supervisor may also ask the cross-training supervisor for input in their annual evaluation. The cross-training experience should be a part of their evaluation.

Dropping a shift

  1. When you know in advance that you will be out for the day or part of a day, put a note in the Note to Employees section of Schedule Notes.
  2. Remove your name from the schedule. 
    1. Change your name to unassigned.
    2. Set color to red.
    3. If BU shift, you are done.
    4. If you are primary on desk, you should also:
      1. Change your now unassigned shift to BU category
      2. Change BU shift to blue
      3. Change category of BU shift to Sub
    5. The person who was the BU is now the primary. This is how it would look if Dominic had been your BU and you needed to drop a shift.
  3. Notify the person who was BU that they are now primary.
    1. You can do this by making sure that notify affected employees is checked before you click save.
  4. If you are at work and dropping a shift day of, please send out message asking for a BU sub.

Email Notifications

Patron Says They Are Not Getting Their Emails

If a patron is claiming they are not getting their notification emails:

  1. Double check their email address first. Verify there are no typos and it is a current email address.
  2. Ask if they checked their spam folder.
  3. Ask if they have their email address set up to redirect to another email address. When these emails are returned to us as "undeliverable" there is no way for me to note the account that it needs fixed, because the bounced email comes from the redirected account, not the address they have in Alma.
  4. Test their account while they are standing there. A lot of people have email on their phone and can verify emails are getting through while you're helping them.

Affiliate Accounts (and Affiliate Dependent)

    1. Bring up patron record
    2. Click on their ID #
    3. Click General Information tab

    5. Save

Filling out a Follow Up Form

Don't forget to ask other staff and search the wiki for potential solutions! But never hesitate to fill out a Follow Up Form.
  1. Go to the LEAD Follow Up Form web page
  2. Enter your name in the "Your name" field
    1. This is so staff can check with you if they have further questions or update you/provide training as needed

  3. Use the "Pick a category" drop down to select the service which the issue that needs followed up on matches best

  4. Fill out the fields
  5. Type a complete description of the issue that needs followed up on including where you put an item if there is an item involved in the "What needs following up on?" field, including where you left the item
    1. It never hurts to have too much information!
  6. Click the Preview button at the bottom of the form
  7. Review your submission
  8. Click the Submit button at the bottom of the form

Former OSU Student/Faculty Member

  1. Search in Alma to see if they still have an account, expired or not.

    1. If they DO NOT have an account in Alma, create a new one just like a Convenience Card account.

    2. If they DO have an account in Alma, expired or not, continue.

  2. They need a convenience card. (preferred)

    1. A staff member may make an exception to allow the former student/faculty to use their OSU ID as their library card (not preferred.)

      A note must be placed in Alma or on the library card application if this exception is made.

  3. A staff member must toggle the account type from "External" to "Internal"

  4. Changes to be made:

    1. The Primary Identifier must be changed to reflect their current library card.

    2. The User Group must be changed to Convenience Card.

    3. Add birth date if not in Alma.

    4. Update Expiration date by one year from today's date.

    5. Add password.

      Password = Patron last name (1st letter capital) and last 4 digits of ID no.

       If the patron's last name is 3 letters or less, add extra digits of the ID no. so total characters = 8

      (i.e., for a 3 letter last name add the last 5 digits of the patrons ID no.)

       The last name follows the following rules:

      1. No punctuation

      2. No hyphen

      3. No spaces

      4. Example:

        1. John Mac Gruder-Smith with ID# 000-186-954 would have the following password:“MacGruderSmith6954”

    6. SAVE!

  5. Update contact information.

  6. Update barcode to reflect current library card.

It is a good idea to go over how the patron will log in to their account as they will no longer use their ONID account.

Frequently Ask Questions @ LEAD Desk

Are Animals Permitted in the Library?

Only service animals are permitted in OSU Libraries. We follow OSU Administrative Policies and Procedures Manuals and other federal guidelines. 

As a matter of procedure, we assume that if the animal is under the control of the owner, it is a service animal. If the animal is barking or otherwise causing a disruption campus security is called for assistance because the animal might be alerting to the owner's medial needs. 

If it is necessary for staff to engage with someone to determine if their animal is permitted in the library the following two questions can be asked. The answer of yes is required for the first question and a specific task is required for the second. 

  1. Is this a service animal?
  2. What service does it provide?

More information can be found on the Spaces

Does the Library accept donations of books or other material?

No. Unless the item is by an OSU faculty that we currently don't own, is a Federal Document that is missing from our collection, or it is accepted for donation to the Special Collections and Archives Research Center (SCARC). All of these must be arranged in advance. Details can be found on the public Gifts and Donations webpage. 

Can I put up my flier or distribute them at Valley?

The first floor public bulletin board next to Java II may be used by anyone. It is unmediated. This means that anyone can put up one copy of their flier without asking us. It is not permitted to post fliers or distribute them elsewhere in the library. If they would like to request an exception, they should contact the Library Spaces Manager. Details about the library's policy can be found here: https://library.oregonstate.edu/administration/display

What is/do I do about that alarm coming from the stairwell?

When someone uses an emergency door by mistake, a loud alarm will go off. (This alarm is loud but localized–the fire alarm is much louder and all encompassing.) The key to turn off the emergency exit alarms is in the key cabinet in the locked closet. Unless you see something else, there is no follow-up needed for these incidents. 

Does the library have tax forms? 

During tax season (roughly January-May) the library provides patrons with physical copies of some of 1040 federal tax forms. The forms are kept on two metal racks directly across from the snack machines in the 2nd floor lobby. More information can be found on the page.

Guest Pass

Information Desk students and staff check out guest passes to public patrons, but if that desk is closed we do it.

There is a metal binder which houses the computer use guest passes. Binder is located in top locked drawer to left of center computer at the Information Desk.

Typically, there are passes made up in advance after Midnight each night.


How to Create a Guest Pass from Scratch

Login to the Info Desk computers (login info is in the metal binder)

There is a program called "PC Reservation," it has a purple icon. Open the program.

Click "Make Guest Pass" and select a number of passes you want to print (usually 10).

Save each file to the desktop with a different file name.

Open each file separately, and write down the number on the guest pass sheets in the front of the metal binder. Cut out.

Delete the files once done.

High School Visitors

A few times per year local high schools will bring in a class to check out books. The reason they have their own User Groups is to prevent them from receiving overdue fines, but they will still get replacement charges.

We encourage the teachers to bring in their library card applications in advance so they may be pre-loaded into Alma before their visit to ease desk congestion- but this does not always happen!

The steps for creating a High School class account are the same as a Convenience Card except: there are two special user groups for these students and their group depends on which school they attend.

  • High School Quarter; Lebanon School districts
  • High School Semester; Albany and Corvallis School districts 
  • NEWPORT high school has requested Convenience Card user group.

When creating a new account for these classes, be sure to give a library card pamphlet to the student.

Immediate Reservations

Patrons can make one reservation per day in advance through our website and as many immediate reservations per day at the LEAD Desk day as they wish. This reduces the chance that rooms and spaces will sit empty. If a patron with an advanced reservation doesn't check-in at the LEAD desk within 15 minutes of the reservation's start time, their reservation maybe cancelled by staff.

Making an Immediate Reservation

Use the Booking Grid and Availability tab to quickly make a reservation when the patron is standing in front of you and wants an immediate booking. Begin by selecting the category you want and hit "Go".

Click on the grid at the appropriate time for the appropriate seat and a popup will appear.

 

Verify the start time. Adjust the end time as needed. You cannot adjust the end time beyond the availability of the room.

 

Change the room if necessary. (This shows seats but the concept is the same.)

 

After you "Submit Times", the “Add Booking” window pops up.

This allows a fast transaction while still including patron information if you need to find the name later on. 

  1. Click Account and have the student swipe their ID card. The number will populate.
  2. Copy and paste the number into the Last Name field
  3. First Name will be "Student".
  4. Email: valley.library@oregonstate.edu. Do not send a confirmation email.
  5. Click the Internal Notes field and scan the key card barcode.
  6. Click "Add Booking".


Check in Patron

Do not hand the key card to the patron yet. You much check them into their booking first. If you forget to do this, the reservation may be canceled by staff.

Checking a Patron into their Immediate Reservation

  1. Click the booking on the chart (You should still have the key card in your hand)
  2. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click "Check In Now" link on the reservation.
  3. Hand the patron the key card. Tell them when their reservation ends.

"Crazy" Ideas:

Tiered reference service (Brandeis Model): lines for “get help with printing, directions, general information” and “get help finding a book, journal article, help with research.” Having 2 lines would allow PTLs to spend more time teaching information literacy/research skills, but may initially confuse patrons.

FAVORITE--Students at the desk, PTL behind the scenes (but still nearby, at consultation station) handling chat and more complex face-to-face questions as they arise. Would free up faculty librarians from chat duties and would give better opportunities for patrons to learn through doing with a professional, rather than the librarian doing it for them.

The 4 quick print stations – used as teaching tools instead to empower patrons and give them hands on experience with Primo and other library resources. Ex. The student sits/stands at the computer while the PTL or student worker guides them through the process of finding resources.  Kristin is against this idea since the quick print stations are very popular and busy.  Maybe catalog computers instead?

Consolidate service points of Circulation and Info Desk. Could this ever happen? How?

Change the LT3 position to Building Manager (similar to Donna’s old job) and have 3-5 PTLs working 20-30 hours per week staffing the Info Desk along with students.

Articles:

The Research Consultation Center (RCC) idea is intriguing...students/staff are specifically trained to differentiate between easily answerable questions and more in-depth ones:

Extreme Makeover Reference Edition

From: XXXXXXX
Sent: Monday, December 28, 2015 4:05 PM
To: Valley Circulation <valley.circ@oregonstate.edu>
Subject: Re: General/Reference Question

 

Dear David,

 

Thank you so much for these reference notes and scans. How fascinating! This recipe and it's naming go right back to pre-WW1 America.  I found it in New York City first and its appearance in the American culinary dialogue coincides with Anna Pavlova's 3rd tour of the US.  It remained a popular salad dish until after WW2, when it was largely forgotten.

 

I've been working with Dr Andrew Paul Wood tracing the origins of the pavlova cake and discovered  many never before documented pavlova-named dishes and desserts, with most emerging from the USA between 1909 and 1921.  These dishes emerge well before any antipodean pavlova "invention" claim.  I've attached a pic of a 1911 'Strawberries Pavlova' recipe we found, which could also be from America.  My next Pavlova recipe recreation will be the 'Pavlova salad!'

 

Many thanks again - I could not do this research without the help and support of rock-star librarians and reference desk experts, like yourself.

 

 ---------------------- 

On Tue, Dec 29, 2015 at 8:26 AM, Valley Circulation <valley.circ@oregonstate.edu> wrote:

 

Hello XXXXXX

I've attached scans of the 1947 Home Institute Cook Book with the Pavlova Salad recipe. I've also included the title, copyright, and associated recipe pages.

Since you asked about publication, the recipe is also included in the 1st edition (1937) of the cookbook as well (page 512).

 The 1937 edition is titled America's Cook Book and appears to be the 1st published edition of the book while the forward in the 1947 edition indicates that it is the 4th edition of the book.

The ingredients are the same except for the salt portion of the mayonnaise (1/2 - 1 teaspoon salt in 1937 vs 1 teaspoon salt in 1947).

The index of the 1937 also includes an extra 'o' in the name of the salad "Pavolova" but the recipe page is Pavlova.

 

Let us know if we can be of any additional help and I hope this helps with your research, 

David Moynihan

Collection Maintenance & Circulation

 121 The Valley Library, Corvallis OR 97331

 (541)737-7309
