LEAD Closing Procedures

Whenever you update this page:
  • Print a copy for the Doomsday Binder.
  • Print and laminate the and opening procedures task lists for the closing clipboard. 

3 HOURS BEFORE CLOSING

Put away extra laptops

Put away excess laptops that may have been left out of their cabinets. We usually leave one out.

  1. Remove the laptop from the bag and plug it in the corresponding slot in the charging cart.
  2. Make sure nothing extra was left in the pockets, zip the charger in the big inside pocket, and place the bag on the storage shelf (Behind the PC laptop storage carts and against the SMS wall around the corner from the main area behind the circ desk).
Shelve any incoming holds shelf items

Check the hold shelf area for any carts of incoming Summit or ILL materials, shelve them, and park the empty carts in the cart corral behind the course reserves shelves by the Media Hub backdoor.

Straighten/shelf-read hold shelf
  • Check for correct shelf order.
  • Readjust bookends, fixing places where gaps have formed and materials have fallen over.
  • Make sure the hold slip is appropriately placed in each item, with the patron name and the pull date showing.
  • If a patron has a bunch of things to pick up, sometimes the materials are stacked separately beside or below the main shelf. Check the main shelf for any other materials for that patron and add them to the stack.
  • See for more information
Audit boardgames
  1. Weigh any games that are on the LEAD desk island
  2. Follow the full instructions for conducting a board game audit from the , to audit any board games that exceed weight tolerance.
Straighten board game shelves and displays



2 HOURS PRIOR

Replenish forms and supplies

Check the front desk supply of:

  • forms: patron account applications, campus maps, and incoming reserve bookmarks – use the Ricoh Document Server to print more
  • pamphlets: replenish all pamphlets as needed 
  • business cards: lost and found referral, course reserve call number wallet card, and staff/office business cards – replenish as needed 
  • Other forms and pamphlets (like the building count sheets) can often be found on the library shared drive, which staff have access to.
  • receipt paper rolls are located ??? TBD
  • Pens and other supplies from the supplies cabinets in the back of the office.
Sort desk bins into recycling bin/shred folder

Empty all the small green recycling bins at the LEAD Desk

  • Put paper with non-confidential information in the big yellow recycling bag
  • Sort any remaining paper with confidential information (names combined with items checked out, ID numbers, addresses, etc.) into the confidential recycling bin
  • Sort any cans, bottles, plastic bags, corrugated cardboard, etc. into the bins in the office recycling center
Empty confidential shred folder

Take the contents of the "secure shred" folder back to the office recycling center and stuff the contents into the main confidential recycling bin (the green padlocked one).

Shelve/shelf-read course reserves

Shelf-read the course reserves range for correct call number order, checking for mis-shelved items.

Conduct the Materials Inventory (Sunday & Wednesday)

Follow the instructions. Make sure we catch check-in mistakes by printing the the saved "items for materials inventory set results in Alma, and checking that all items on the list are actually checked out and haven't been returned.

Straighten equipment

This applies to mostly anything considered small equipment and the general area too

  • Make sure items like headphones are neatly stacked
  • Sort out scientific calculators by type and stack them neatly
  • Make sure all the things that come in the big black mesh bags are in their correctly labeled spots
  • Wind up the mouse cords
  • etc.

1 HOUR PRIOR

Building walk-through (restart week 1)
  1. Walk through the whole building: along the perimeter and avenue of each floor, around the rotunda spaces, and past all the study rooms on the 1st, 5th, and 6th floors.
  2. Skip Java II area.
  3. Count the patrons on each floor and use the log on the closing clipboard to record the numbers.
  4. Note any building problems and report them to the lead staff member.
  5. Check that the 1st, 3rd, and 5th floor scanners work if you have time.

(STAFF) The floor counts get entered in the spreadsheet on the shared drive at S:\Shared\LEAD\Circulation\Opening & Closing\closing-bldg-walkthrough-statistics.xls. The printable count sheets are a second sheet on this workbook.

Print events and classroom calendars, post, and clean Willamette East and West

  1. Print Classroom Calendars

    1. Open events calendars for Autzen and Willamette East and Willamette West in a browser and the Outlook calendar for Nishihara Family Classroom 2024.
    2. Open “Classroom Calendar Templates” Powerpoint document (desktop icon).
    3. Put the date at the top of each slide.
    4. Copy the event and the time from the calendar and paste into appropriate Powerpoint slide.
      1. Individual Classroom Calendars
        1. Delete all but the name of the event (including name of person with the reservation) and the time of the event.
      2. All Events Calendar
        1. Delete all but the name of the event, time of event, and room name. You will have to type the room name for Nishihara Family Classroom 2024.
    5. Print all slides on Stimpy
      1. Change setting from Color to Grayscale and make sure is printing only one-sided.
    6. If there are no events we have permanent, laminated signs for each classroom and the desk located in the small filing cabinet under Stimpy.

    7. When closing out of the Powerpoint document, NEVER save your changes. 

  2. Post calendars in Autzen, Willamette East and West, and Nishihara Family Classroom 2024
  3. Clean Willamette East and West as you post the calendar.
    1. Clean whiteboards, wipe off tables, rearrange furniture if needed, and make sure computers are on and logged off.
Clean up Learning Commons

Instructions?

Clean up printer area

Instructions?

Check 1st floor emergency exits

Preferably while doing the walk through:

  1. Take the key labelled "Emergency Exits" from the key cabinet in the locked closet
  2. At the fire exits in the stairwells at the end of the avenue on the 1st floor, arm the fire exit alarms on both of the double doors by turning the lock to the "armed" position
  3. If the doors were disarmed, you will be able to feel the lock click back into place in the armed position.
    1. The doors in the East stairwell (by Java) have an indicator light on the push bar. If disarmed, about 10 seconds after arming the alarm, it will "chirp" loudly once.
  4. If the door was disarmed, do a "building maintenance" follow up form to alert the building manager that the doors were left disarmed.
Check 2nd floor copiers and scanners

Preferably while doing the walk through:

  1. Check the copiers for jams, and check that none of the scanners needs rebooting. See for more details.

  2.  Check the glass for any sensitive documents that have been left behind (like passports and other personal documents) and .

Clear 1st floor book drop

Preferably while doing the walk through:

Use the LEAD office key (on the Opening/Closing key chain) to access the 1st floor book drop closet. The closet is located downstairs behind the TL - TX compact shelving. Pull any returned materials out of the bin and process them through the Check-in Station.

Clean LEAD Desk counters/island

Use our cleaning supplies to wipe down the LEAD Desk counter (on both the public and the staff side), the LEAD desk island and any other surface in our front office area that is looking grody.

Clean drink parking shelf

Chuck any abandoned food, recycle abandoned cans or bottles, dump out liquids in the bathroom or outside, and wipe down the shelves.

Check in returned materials

Follow  to process and route all returned materials.

(Staff/Lead) Inventory "valley keys"

Building keys are kept in the secure closet key cabinet. Run a Physical Item search for "valley keys" and check if any of the checked out keys are actually in the secure closet already (if so, they will need to be backdated and checked in).

(STAFF/LEAD) Check valley.circ inbox

Check the valley.circ email inbox for voicemails and patron emails, then respond accordingly.

If you don't have access to the valley.circ inbox you can check the LEAD Desk line (7-7254) for voicemail messages (new or saved) and respond accordingly.

  • Voicemail dialing instructions are located near the LEAD Desk phone.

  • If a message requires a response but it is too late an hour to call back, record the details in the Follow-up Form for the morning staff to handle.

  • Delete messages you have addressed and save messages that still need to be addressed.
  • See the page for more information.

30 MINUTES PRIOR

Make PA announcement/turn lights off and on
  • Make a to prepare patrons for closing time.
  • Turn lights off and on: The light switches are to the right of the office door off the main building entrance. The light switches for public areas of the building are on the panel on the right, marked "Public Areas." Flash all lights by pressing the bottom half of the button to turn them off and the top half of the button to turn them back on. Only flash the lights once and try to cycle them for at least a second or two to avoid disturbing people who are sensitive to light flashes.



(STAFF/LEAD) Take checked in book cart to 3rd floor annex
  1. Retrieve the master key from the locked key closet
  2. Wheel the cart up one of the elevators to the 3rd floor
  3. The annex is the cubicle walled area behind the Mole Hole and Microforms printing equipment, open it with the master key
  4. Checked in book carts should be left at the end of the reshelving stacks (labelled with the call number ranges of the books that are supposed to go on them)

15 MINUTES PRIOR

Make PA announcement/turn lights off and on
  • Make a to prepare patrons for closing time.
  • Turn lights off and on: The light switches are to the right of the office door off the main building entrance. The light switches for public areas of the building are on the panel on the right, marked "Public Areas." Flash all lights by pressing the bottom half of the button to turn them off and the top half of the button to turn them back on. Only flash the lights once and try to cycle them for at least a second or two to avoid disturbing people who are sensitive to light flashes.
Charge the day's noise cancelling headphones

Plug six headsets into a USB-C cable from the case in the 6-port hub charging station.

Check in returned materials

Follow  to process and route all returned materials.


5 MINUTES PRIOR

Make PA announcement and flash building lights
  • Make a to prepare patrons for closing time.
  • Turn lights off and on: The light switches are to the right of the office door off the main building entrance. The light switches for public areas of the building are on the panel on the right, marked "Public Areas." Flash all lights by pressing the bottom half of the button to turn them off and the top half of the button to turn them back on. Only flash the lights once and try to cycle them for at least a second or two to avoid disturbing people who are sensitive to light flashes.
(STAFF/LEAD) Lock building doors

Retrieve the Opening/Closing key chain from the secure closet key cabinet. Lock the following doors:

  • sliding door leading to Java II (at the top of the stairs)
  • Java II building entrance (downstairs)
  • main entrance exterior doors
  • main entrance interior doors
How to lock the sliding doors at the main entrance...
  1. From the inside, wait for the doors to close.
  2. Turn off the automatic doors by placing the triangular key in the switch on the top right the door and turning it to the far left position (marked by two lines -- ).
  3. Lock the doors at the center by inserting the building key and turning it counterclockwise to activate the latch.
  4. Check the lock by pulling the doors apart slightly to make sure they are latched and do not open.
How to lock the sliding door leading down to Java II...

  1. Turn off the automatic door switch, the black knob on the right that controls the automatic function.

    The setting for automatic opening is at the top (photo)

    The setting for keeping the door closed is to the bottom left (photo)
  2. Stand on the lobby side of the door and wait for it to shut completely. (If you have to get through the door once it's turned off, you can manually slide it open and closed.)
  3. Lock the door at the center by inserting the building key and turning it counterclockwise?? to activate the latch.
How to lock the push-handle side doors...
  1. Use the hex key on the Opening/Closing key chain. Insert the key in the screws at both ends of the handle and loosen by turning counterclockwise. The handle should release outward and latch the door.
  2. When the door is closed, press outward on the frame to make sure it locked.
How to lock the Java II doors...
  1. Use the hex key on the Opening/Closing key chain. Insert the key in the hole next to the push bar and release it by turning counterclockwise. The push bar should release outward and latch the door.
  2. When the door is closed, press outward on the frame to make sure it locked.

If you have problems locking an exterior door, call the Department of Public Safety dispatch at the non-emergency number (7-3010, or 541-737-3010 from a non-campus phone) and wait for them to arrive before leaving.

As you are leaving, double-check all the exterior doors (main entrance and Java II entrance) to be sure they are closed and locked.

AT CLOSING

Make PA announcement/turn lights off and on
  • Make a to prepare patrons for closing time.
  • Turn lights off and on: The light switches are to the right of the office door off the main building entrance. The light switches for public areas of the building are on the panel on the right, marked "Public Areas." Flash all lights by pressing the bottom half of the button to turn them off and the top half of the button to turn them back on. Only flash the lights once and try to cycle them for at least a second or two to avoid disturbing people who are sensitive to light flashes.
Shut down LEAD desk workstations

Students should shut down the workstations they are using. Turn off keyboards and mice. Charge if needed.

Place "lost and found" bin on counter

Place the lost and found bin on a donor lobby-facing desk for the overnight custodial staff and DPS to deposit any items they find. The lost and found bin lives on the credenza near the staff station.

(STAFF/LEAD) Place closing keys in LEAD desk storage room
  • Place the Opening/Closing key chain back in the locked closet.
  • Check that the fob key has been placed on the slat wall.

  • Check that the Info Desk, Media Hub and other building keys are in placed in the locked closet.

Turn off office lights

Turn off all lights in the LEAD workspace. The light switches are to the right of the office door off the main building entrance. The light switches for the workspace are on the panel on the left and are marked: Office (Front), MediaHub, LEAD Staff Desks, and Office (Back). Press the bottom half of the button to turn them off.

The switches for the LED light strips are on the wall near the PA system.

It is okay to leave on the building lights for the public areas, because the overnight custodial staff will need them.

(STAFF/LEAD) Confirm security visit (in person or call 7-3010)

The Department of Public Safety is responsible for clearing the building at closing time. Sometimes the security officer greets you at the LEAD Desk. Sometimes the officer stands in the Learning Commons waiting for the closing announcement.

Note when the officer enters the building and inform the lead staff member if the officer has not arrived by closing time.

(STAFF/LEAD) If no one from the Department of Public Safety has arrived around closing time, call dispatch at the non-emergency number (7-3010, or 541-737-3010 from a non-campus phone) to confirm that someone is coming. Once you have called, it is not necessary to wait for the officer to arrive.

LEAD FAQ

A place for answers to questions about LEAD. Got a question? Please ask!

When should I expect to pay for food at work and when will it be provided for me?

Generally speaking, when food is purchased in one big order (like a catered lunch), there is a required work event where it isn't possible to bring your own food (like an offsite retreat), or if you are a participant in an official meal (like a lunch for an interviewee) then the meal will usually be paid for. For optional events (like a happy hour) or for required work events when you are able to bring your own meal (like a trip to Guin Library), then usually they will not be paid for. When the situation varies from these guidelines the organizer is expected to say so in their invitation. However, none of this prohibits someone from feeling generous and picking up a tab.

  • Fill paper and toner
  • Fix jams
  • Wake up card swipe and printer touch machines by touching the screens and making sure that they are working
  • Clean up printer area and counter
    • Pick-up extra paper from printers, floor, etc. Put in recycling or unclaimed print jobs bin.
    • Wipe down counter, clean up pencil shavings and empty pencil sharpener
    • Check to make sure staplers are full
    • Check to make sure tape, hole punch and paper cutter are in place and working

At the scanners...

  • Wake up
  • Make sure all lights are on and they are ready to use

At the Public Patron Computers...

  • Wake up
  • Wipe down desks

In the Learning Commons...

  • Wide down tables and desks
  • Organize chairs, etc.
  • Move furniture out of walkways
  • Log off computers left logged in 
  • Make sure that the ADA accessible workstation is on the LC (ONID login) image.

In the Nishihara Family and Autzen Classrooms...

  • Turn on lights
  • Organize furniture according to posted maps. 
  • Wipe down tables/furniture
  • Make sure instructor computer station is on

In Room 2511...

  • Make sure computer is on

 Unlock doors in the following order starting about 5 minutes before opening:

  1. Interior main entrance
  2. Interior sliding door leading to Java II
  3. Java II
  4. Exterior main entrance

Sliding doors: turn the regular key counter-clockwise until the door unlocks. Then, using the triangular key, turn the round knob located on the upper right side of the door clockwise until it points toward the 12:00 position.

Side doors: gently press the push handle and then lock it in place by lightly tightening the screws at each end with the hex key (be sure not to overtighten or the screws may be damaged).

Java II doors: press the push bar and then lock it in place by inserting the hex key in the hole and turning it clockwise.

LEAD Photos

Welcome to the LEAD Photos page! This space is meant to keep track of all of our fabulous staff, the amazing work they have done, and of the wonderful times we have spent together.

When adding a photo, please make sure that the file name includes the year and pithy description of the event, ex. "2016 summer circ meeting". Multiple images of the same event should have the same title with alphabetical or numerical additions to the end: "2016 summer circ meeting a", "2016 summer circ meeting b", etc. This will help keep the pictures sorted with each other as well as providing a quick and easy way of remembering when and where the picture was taken.

Photos can also be found on the LEAD Shared Google Drive and the LEAD Folder on the Shared Network Drive.

LEAD Staff Space & Things

LEAD Supply Ordering/Purchase Requesting

Lead Student Procedure: No Staff Onsite

If all staff persons are unexpectedly absent, the Lead Desk Student will take primary responsibility for the safe operation of the building and providing basic services.

The Lead Desk Student will:

  1. who are scheduled to work later in the day to ask if they can start early.
    1. If a staff member can come in quickly, there is no need to continue with the following steps.
  2. Email LibraryDeskStudents@oregonstate.eduto ask for volunteers to fill the shifts.
  3. Contact the LEAD Head at (541) 231-6109 to inform her of the situation.
    1. If she does not pick up, leave a message and also text her, if possible.
  4. Assess staffing needs and make any needed adjustments.
    1. Examples of adjustments:
      1. Re-assign work to the service desk. For example, a student scheduled to work on 3-D Printing may be moved to the desk.
      2. Decide to work past your scheduled shift and/or offer hours to others to work past their scheduled shift.
  5. Review the Emergency Procedures


LEAD Supply Ordering/Purchase Requesting

When requesting supplies, always check Benny Buy first and if the item(s) are not there or can be found elsewhere for less than the item can be requested through other sites/stores.

  • Ordering through Benny Buy
    • Benny Buy trainings are currently on hold; however, Tip Sheets can be found here.
    • OSU Libraries and Press administration (LAMP) has designated staff and faculty to various supply ordering roles within Benny Buy. 

      • Shopper - A shopper is a person who places an order.

      • Requester - A requester approves orders under $5,000 utilizing the eProcurement system.

      • Approver - An approver is the equivalent of a budget authority for the library, and can approve all procurement for the library.
    • Shoppers search for items in Benny Buy and submit request by assigning the shopping cart to the Requester. 
  • Search the Benny Buy home page first (search bar is at the top of the page).
  • If you don't find what you are looking for on your general search, I strongly suggest checking individual contracted vendors or "Punch Outs" for the items you need as it is easier to locate a broader inventory that way. 
    • Scroll down to the business that you would like to search and select shop now. 
    • When on a punch out site, add the item to your cart and then select review & checkout, then select submit order. You will then be taken back to the Benny Buy site.
    • Once on Benny Buy site again, select assign cart. The first time you will likely need to search for an assignee; however, once that has been done you should be able to select the requestor (Rima Reves or Beth Filar-Williams) from the dropdown. 

  • Ordering through other businesses/websites
    • If an item can not be found in Benny Buy or is available for a better price elsewhere,  please submit a request to Rima Reves (staff person that currently orders supplies for LEAD).
    • Send as much information as you have regarding the product you would like purchased.
      • Name of product
      • Specific numbers attached to product
      • Price
      • Quantity
      • Website link

Questions? Please ask either Rima Reves or your supervisor.

LEAD Wish List & Parking Lot of ideas

Below is a list of all of the equipment, tech, furniture, and other items that LEAD staff are interested in as well as a list of spaces and services that would need some sort of initial funding to get started. This is an informal list of items big and small that both the Circulation and Information desks might consider researching and maybe purchasing as funding becomes available. Please make child pages for well-developed and well-researched purchase ideas so that this page remains an informal compilation of all of the items that LEAD staff want. (see some ideas with photos NW Lib road trip 2015 slides)

Tech & Equipment  

[ Orange = Not Yet Purchased | Gray = Notes | Strikethough = Fulfilled ]

  • Portable chargers. Mobile device charging kits to use within the library, aka a portable charger with various cords? Or a portable charger that can charge laptops, too, like OOMF http://info.agati.com/oomf-charging (purchased ChargeTech Portable Power Banks Oct. 2018) 
  • Lightning to Micro USB adapter. We could add these to the micro USB charger bags and then all of them would become dual Android/iPhone chargers! http://www.apple.com/shop/product/MD820AM/A/lightning-to-micro-usb-adapter?fnode=74 (The small Apple adapters were a bit of a failed experiment because they go missing too easily, even when attached with a rubber cozy. We decided it's better to just have 2 separate types of phone cables.)
  • Universal laptop power supply like NCSU: https://www.lib.ncsu.edu/devices/universal-laptop-power-supply
  • Old MacBook Pro to new MacBook Pro or MacBook Air converter: http://www.staples.com/Apple-MagSafe-to-MagSafe-2-Converter/product_164142 (Instead of small adapters that go missing easily, we got a couple of old and new MacBook chargers to circulate by themselves. Does this count as fulfilled?)
  • Bluetooth keyboards? Free-standing monitors? (For the tablets or just for free use?) (We have a wired Arabic / English keyboard as of February 2017.)
  • Personal alarms? (To replace the one we got rid of in 2014. As of September 2016 we have some personal alarms for student and staff employees, but not for the public.)
  • More noise cancelling headphones! (Maybe ones that don't fold because the folding Bose break easily)
  • 4 function calculators? (We decided the need may not be huge even though about once a term we get a flood of students who need them for midterms)
  • Wacom tablets? (Since these are design/art specific they may be more in line with the Service Desk's equipment scheme)
  • Pocket projectors, like the Brookstone HDMI Pocket Projector. These would be for more recreational uses than the Service Desk's full size projectors.
  • Power strips or extension cords to use within the library? (Added two for circulation Oct. 2018, have five more - testing to see popularity and use)
  • Kangaroo Windows 10 portable PC (only $99 but may not work with ONID authentication)

Libraries, Games, and Play Conference; April 6, 2019. Washington, DC - Matthew

Beginning Keynote: Lindsay Grace - Engagement Design


  • Lindsay talked about how games and play can help support the needs of libraries and the communities that they serve. This is done through the connections that can be made with the communities that are being served as well as supporting education and helping to drive a thirst for new knowledge.

  • According to Lindsay, games equal structured play. Play is both practice and laboratory. It is practice insofar as it helps people utilize skills that can then be used in the real world; such as teamwork and individual thinking. In addition, he says that games thru play offer structures for engagement.

  • One important concept that was introduced was Ludoliteracy. Ludoliteracy is the ability or the means to understand how games and their systems work. People that are able to gain a good grasp of literacy can gain an increased capacity to play and experiment in regards to games.


1st session: Getting started with games: how to begin or expand


  • Accessibility and inclusivity of the games chosen and what is being offered. One thing to consider is what groups are we trying to serve?

  • One of the types of games that was discussed was allowing the children to create a board game using pieces provided by the teacher.

  • Most of this session revolved around games that could be used in the educational setting of elementary/middle/high schools.

  • One story that was told that I enjoyed was a parent that believed that video games were not good for kids and would not let his child play the games that were available. This story was told by one of the speakers, Sandy Farmer. Sandy said that she asked the parent for five minutes of his time to explain how games were actually good for children. She had him watch the children playing the games and how much fun they were having and that they were using analytical thinking in order to beat whatever game was being played at that moment. This shows that some people just need something shown, or explained to them in order for them to confront a prejudice that they might have toward a particular topic which in this case was about video games.


2nd session: Curating a board game collection


  • This session focused on how the library at American University started their board game collection. It also talked about how their collection works with some of the classes that are offered at the university.

  • The library worked with one of the local board game stores to begin their collection. They have a set budget for board games and inform the board game store what they are looking for.

  • A number of the games that have been purchased by the American University library was done to supplement some of the classes being taught at the university.

  • One suggestion that did come out of this session was for a display idea. “If you like this book, try out this game.” That seems like it would be an idea that should be fairly easy to implement with our board game collection at the Valley Library.

  • Another topic that was talked about was what to do about missing game pieces and where to get more. One website that was suggested was http://www.koplowgames.com/. This might be an east coast establishment but it at least is an idea of where we may be able to purchase bulk generic replacement or extra pieces.

  • The fun part of this session was going over to the library and seeing where and how they store their board game collection.

  • The board game collection is housed in the staff area of their circulation space which means that the games are not visible to the patrons. The games are placed in plastic bags that are hung from shelves against one of the walls in the staff area. Some of the bigger games are still stored in bags but are placed on the bottom shelf as they are too big to be hung up.

  • I asked them how often they process the games when they are returned. They only weigh and count the pieces maybe once or twice a term/semester when they do a board game audit.

  • One of the ways that they advertise their game collection is with a large poster, 3’ x 5’, that is on the wall next to the circulation desk. This poster lists their most popular games with pictures of said games spaced out in a grid.


Ending Keynote: Paul Reynolds, Fablevision


  • Paul is an award-winning author as well as one of the co-founders of FableVision. FableVision is a multimedia production studio that designs a wide variety of media and other interactives that serve to inspire, teach, and move people to action. Paul talked about the importance of nurturing creativity in youths. To that end, FableVision has created or collaborated on a number of programs that enable young people to learn new skills such as analytical thinking and problem solving. One of the programs that Paul talked about was the relaunch of the classic 90s game, Zoombinis. This program helps young people learn important skills such as algebraic thinking and data analysis as they help the zoombinis on their journey throughout the course of the game.

Library Patron Accounts - In-Depth Info

Convenience Card Account - Checklist here:

Out of Library Card Application forms?

Step 1: Determine Eligibility

Who can have a Convenience card?

The convenience card is the card that we give to many of our non-OSU patrons, but is also given to those that are on campus, but not technically part of OSU.

Patrons:

Description:

Residents

Includes any person who currently lives or pays property taxes in Oregon and has proof of address.

This DOES NOT INCLUDE anyone using an Oregon "General Delivery" address at the post office.

Minors

A minor is anyone under the age of 16. Oregon residence and Parent/Guardian signature required.

Alumni

Includes anyone with a current OSU Alumni Association card. Alumni can live anywhere in the world (don't have to have an Oregon address) as long as they are an OSU Alumni Association member.

Library privileges include borrowing at the Valley Library and the Guin Library at HMSC; their privileges don't include ONID computer use or remote access to online databases that require an ONID.

Oregon Passport Program

Anyone who has a library card at these participating libraries can also get a library card from us!

Here is a list of participating Oregon Passport Program libraries; http://www.olaweb.org/passport-directory

EPA

Environmental Protection Agency: Any member of the EPA with an EPA issued identification. Not all EPA members have OSU ID.

OSU Retired

An individual has retired from OSU if he or she has terminated from the University and is immediately drawing benefits or retirement allowances from their retirement plan offered through OSU employment.

GWLA

A member of the

Greater Western Library Alliance

What is GWLA?

The Greater Western Library Alliance (GWLA) is a consortium of 36 research libraries located in the central and western United States.

GWLA is a dynamic, effective, project-oriented consortium, nationally recognized as a leader in the transformation of scholarly communication, and a facilitator in the application of new information technologies.

What does that mean to me?

Members of GWLA can get a convenience card and check out materials. They do not need to be residents of the state of Oregon, but they do need to be a member of one of the GWLA institutions.

Here is a list of the GWLA participating institutions; GWLA Members

What do I do differently?

  • First, bring up the list of GWLA institutions, and check that their institution is on the list.
  • They need to have a University ID for their University. Otherwise, everything else is the same as a Convenience Card!
  • At the top of the Library Card Application, where it says "Where did you hear about our resident patron card?" put: "GWLA member," and the University they are affiliated with.

Associate

Permanent employees of organizations or federal agencies housed on OSU campus, providing teaching, research, or funding to OSU are eligible for the associate status.

OCLC

A member of the 

Online Computer Library Center

What is OCLC?

The Online Computer Library Center (OCLC) is a nonprofit cooperative organization "dedicated to the public purposes of furthering access to the world's information and reducing information costs".

OCLC is a global library cooperative that provides shared technology services, original research and community programs for its membership and the library community at large.

What does that mean to me?

Members of OCLC can get a convenience card and check out materials. They do not need to be residents of the state of Oregon, but they do need to be a member of one of the OCLC institutions.

Here is a list of the OCLC participating institutions; OCLC PDF list of participating institutions

What do I do differently?

  • First, bring up the list of OCLC institutions, and check that their institution is on the list.
  • They need to have a University ID for their University. Otherwise, everything else is the same as a Convenience Card!
  • At the top of the Library Card Application, where it says "Where did you hear about our resident patron card?" put: "OCLC member," and which University they are affiliated with.

Step 2: Library Account Creation (the steps)

How to create a Convenience Card Account

Do this first: Look up the patron BY NAME in Alma

  • If you find an expired account for the patron, see Expired Patron Accounts.
  • If the patron was once a student, and is now a convenience card patron, get a staff member! Only they have the permissions to toggle the account type.

To issue a library card WE REQUIRE:

  1. Government issued photo ID
    1. Drivers license, passport, military ID, etc.
  2. proof of OREGON address (either ID, or mail)
    1. They must be an Oregon resident, or part of OCLC or GWLA
  3. A completed Library Card Application

Dont Forget: Match the address from the government ID or mail to the one on the application.

  • The mail should be something official, like a phone bill.
  • If the addresses are different, ask the patron for proof of current address.
    • If they don't have proof, they need to come back when they do. They cannot check out items until we have proof of address.

What to do in ALMA:

In ALMA, under >Fulfillment > Check Out/Check In > Manage Patron Services > Register New User

Click to enlarge image of Alma screenshots: (there are two)

Enter the User details:  

  1. Fill out each required field with the information on the application.
    1. Legal Name: First name, Middle name, Last name
    2. Preferred Name: First name, Middle name, Last name (as applicable)
    3. Primary Identifier: the 9 digit Convenience Card number located on the back of the Convenience Card and starts with 000
      use the dash format so the patron can access their library account, example: 000-633-131
    4. User Group: Select Convenience card group from drop down menu
    5. Campus: Select correct campus from drop down menu (OSU Main Campus)
    6. Birth date
    7. Expiration Date: one year from date of record creation
      1. NO purge date, leave this blank.
    8. User Management Information
      Patron has institutional record: No 
    9. Password = Patron last name (1st letter capital) and last 4 digits of ID no.

      If the patron's last name is 3 letters or less, add extra digits of the ID no. so total characters = 8

      (i.e., for a 3 letter last name add the last 5 digits of the patrons ID no.)

      The last name follows the following rules:

      1. No punctuation
      2. No hyphen
      3. No spaces
      4. Example:
        • John Mac Gruder-Smith with ID# 000-186-954 would have the following password:“MacGruderSmith6954”
    10. Verify Password: same as above
    11. Email address: check appropriate box and enter email address
      1. If the patron does not have an email address put: noemail@noemail.com
    12. Addresses: Select Address type as "Work" and enter the patron's mailing address
    13. Phone number: Select appropriate box and enter telephone number area code first.
      Use format: (###) ###-####
  1. TIME TO ADD MORE INFORMATION INSIDE THE NEW ACCOUNT!
    1. Click to enlarge this image



    3.
  2. Choose Update User to add Alternate IDs and Patron Barcode
    1. Click on their ID number to enter their account.
      1. Click the "Identifiers" tab
        1. Click: Add Identifier
          1. Choose Identifier Type = Additional ID 1
          2. Value = Alternate ID Number (example: drivers license or passport number)
          3. Enter the ID type in the notes field (example: ODL, US passport, military ID, etc.)
          4. Add  
        2. Click: Identifier Type = Barcode
          1. Value = swipe the Convenience Card, it will populate the barcode from the card. (example: 0000000001)

      2. Add Pronouns Note and Close

        How to add a "note"
        1. Enter the patron's account
          1. Pull up their account by name or ID number in ALMA
          2. Click on their ID number
        2. Click the tab that says "Notes"
        3. Click the "Add Note" button
        4. In the Note Description put the patron's pronouns 
          1. Under drop-down field "Type" choose "Circulation"
          2. Click "Pop up note" (for yes)



  3. YOU'RE ALMOST DONE, TIME TO REVIEW THE PAPER APPLICATION:
    1. Are all the fields filled out?

  4. In the Staff Use section of :
    1. Always:
      1. Check off that you verified photo ID & address
      2. Write down the Convenience card number
      3. Enter today's date and your initials
    2. If applicable:
      1. Check off if the patron are coming to us as part of the Oregon Passport Program.
        1. Link to information about Oregon Passport Program
      2. If this a Summit Institution patron; write down the name of their institution and their school ID number
      3. If this is an Affiliate patron; write down the name of their spouse/partner
      4. If this is an OSU student/faculty/staff; write down their OSU ID number
  5. Place the application in the Circulation Inbox
  6. Move on to Step 3: Information for the Patron, aka. What to say to new cardholders!

CIRCULATION STAFF: If you are making an account exception for any reason please make a note on the application for review.

Step 3: Information for the Patron

What to say to new card holders

Please sign the back of your library card, a fine tip Sharpie marker works best on the hard plastic.

You may check out up to 25 items at a time, for up to 30 days at a time, with a maximum of 120 days. Media collection items, such as DVDs, have a 1 week checkout, with a maximum of 4 weeks. Lockers check out for 3 days. Remind them that they cannot share their card with others, and that they are responsible for everything checked out on their card.

Your items will renew automatically unless they are otherwise requested, have a block on your account, or your account is expired/expiring.

We recommend you change your password in your library account upon receipt of your new card.

    • Go to The Valley Library website, on the right corner there is a link for "My Account" 
    • Sign in as a Community Cardholder
    • On the left there should be a link to Personal Settings
    • Click on Edit Details
    • Click on Update Login Credentials (here is where you change your password)
    • Click Update when finished.

Please be sure to keep your email address on file current, that’s how we send you notifications such as due dates. You can change this by logging into your account online, or by contacting the circulation desk.

Your library account will expire within 1 year of creation, in order to keep it open another year contact the Circulation desk so we may verify your account information is still accurate. Circulation (541) 737-7254.

You may also use your library account to use one of the guest internet computers located near the Information Desk on the second floor for up to 3 hours per day. To log in the username is your library card number.

How Do I...

update expired patron accounts?

Expired Accounts

Convenience Card Accounts

  1. In ALMA, bring up the patron record
  2. Ask the patron for their address, telephone number, and email. Correct if needed.
  3. Change the expiration date
    1. Bring up patron record
    2. Click on their ID #
    3. Click General Information tab
    4. Update the Expiration Date for one year from today's date
    5. Save

Affiliate Accounts (and Affiliate Dependent)

  1. In ALMA, bring up the patron record
  2. In Atrium, verify their spouse/partner/parent is still an OSU Faculty/Staff/Student (you will need to ask for their partner/parent's name)
    1. If their partner is no longer an OSU Faculty/Staff/Student, if they are an Oregon resident you may convert their account to a Convenience Card account
  3. Ask the patron for their address, telephone number, and email. Correct if needed.
  4. Change the expiration date
    1. Bring up patron record
    2. Click on their ID #
    3. Click General Information tab

    5. Save

Visiting Summit Patrons

  1. Use the quick access computer to have the patron to login to their Summit institution account to verify they are currently active
  2. If so, bring up their patron record in ALMA

OSU Patrons

You should not have to update any OSU patrons. Banner updates current OSU Students, Faculty, and Staff every Sunday.

add or remove an Alternate Borrower (Proxy User)?

Alternate Borrowers (aka Proxy Users)

How to add a Proxy User (aka. Authorized Borrower) to an account:

  1. Only OSU faculty can designate other people to check items out for them.
    1. PROXY USERS CANNOT CHANGE ANY ACCOUNT INFORMATION ON THE FACULTY MEMBERS ACCOUNT. (No matter how pushy they are.)
    2. You cannot give any Faculty account information to the Proxy User (fines, address, etc. this is patron confidentiality)
    3. Proxy Users can ONLY borrow items on the Faculty member's behalf.
  2. The Proxy User must also have an account in ALMA; this means they must have an OSU ID card or a Convenience Card account.
  3. Ask the faculty member to fill out a Proxy User Application, if they haven't already.
  4. Check their OSU ID for "Faculty" printed under their name.
  5. If the faculty member is not showing up in ALMA, verify their faculty status in Atrium
  6. Open the faculty members patron record:
    1. Click on their ID number
    2. Click on the "notes" tab
    3. Click the "add note" button
    4. In the note field add note: Proxy Users: Doe, John
    5. In the Type drop-down menu select: Circulation
    6. Select User Viewable, yes.
  7. Click Add/Close
  8. Tell the patron that proxy users must present picture ID to check out items.
  9. Open the Proxy User's patron record:
    1. Click on their ID number
    2. Click on "proxy for" tab
    3. Search by name or ID number of the OSU Faculty member
    4. Click the "add user" button
    5. Click "save"
  10. Initial and date the application in the Office Use Only area "ALMA updated by" section
  11. Place the application in the Circulation Inbox

An Exception can be made if:

  1. If the Faculty member cannot bring the completed application in-person, they can submit it via their oregonstate.edu email address.
    1. A staff member can email them a blank application form, but a signed form should be completed before the proxy user is added.
  2. If a non-Faculty member wants to set up a Proxy.

Remove an Authorized Borrower:

  1. A proxy user can asked to be removed.
  2. The faculty can asked for the proxy to be removed.
  3. Go into the "notes" tab of the Faculty member removing their Proxy User
    1. Delete the "Proxy User" note
  4. Go into the Proxy User's account to the "Proxy For" tab
    1. Select the Faculty member being removed and "delete," then save.
use Atrium to verify student status?

Atrium can be tricky to understand, just because a status is "Active" does not mean they are a student.

Here are a few of the status' in Atrium:

  • PtStudent ← this is a student, in Alma the User Group will usually be "Undergrad" or "Post-Bacc"
  • PtEmployee ← this is a campus employee Staff or Faculty, in Alma the User Group will usually be "OSU Staff" or "OSU Faculty/GTA"
  • PtAssociate ← this is a tricky one, in Alma the User Group will usually be "Convenience Card" because most people who have an Associate status still only get Convenience Card level borrowing privileges


  1. Atrium is the system we use to verify if someone is a part of the OSU System.
    1. It is a real-time system and can verify new students/faculty/staff immediately.
      1. https://oregonstate.atriumcampus.com/
      2. If you need the username and password, please ask a staff member.
  2. Choose Login Method: Login with Atrium
  3. Click the "People" tab
  4. Enter the OSU ID number in the "Input Value" field with no dashes, no spaces
    1. There are alternate ways to search, such as by last name if you change the drop down menu from "University ID" to "Last Name". You should only need this if they are not providing an OSU ID, but an alternate form of ID such as driver's license.
  5. If they show up with an "Active" status account, they are still part of the OSU system. Their scheduled date of deactivation is below their picture. (Since this example is a staff account rather than student it has a bit more information.)
show a patron how to change their password in Primo?
  1. Click on My Account at the top right corner of the screen
  2. Have them login to their account by choosing “Community Cardholder” and entering their card number and supplied password (xxx-xxx-xxx, Smith2435)
  3. Choose "Personal Details" from the the My Account screen
  4. Click on "Update Login Credentials" in smaller box on the right side of the screen
  5. A new box will appear. Enter the old password and replace it with a new password at least 8 characters long containing upper and lower case letters and at least one number. Click update.
create a Computer Use Only card?

Computer Use Only Card

Computer Use Only cards are for anyone to be able to use one of the eight specially designated computers for public use. They can use the computer for up to three hours per day. Anyone may obtain a computer use card which allows access to the Valley Patron Computers in the Learning Commons but does not allow checkout of library materials. Only a NAME is required. Minors (under the age of 16) are required to complete a library card application with a parent/guardian signature. The convenience card may also be used for printing and copying.

What we need:

Their Name. No ID required. No application required.

In ALMA :

  • Create new user
  • First Name and Last Name

  • Primary Identifier using the 9 digit number on the back of the convenience card using the dash format 000-XXX-XXX
    (If you do not do this, they cannot log in to the computer)
  • user group:"Computer Use Only"
  • expiration date: 1 year from date of account creation
  • Password = Patron last name (1st letter capital) and last 4 digits of ID no.

    If the patron's last name is 3 letters or less, add extra digits of the ID no. so total characters = 8

    (i.e., for a 3 letter last name add the last 5 digits of the patrons ID no.)

    The last name follows the following rules:

    1. No punctuation
    2. No hyphen
    3. No spaces
    4. Example:
      1. John Mac Gruder-Smith with ID# 000-186-954 would have the following password:“MacGruderSmith6954”
  • email address, if they do not have one use: noemail@noemail.com

  • Choose Update User to add Barcode.
    • Click on their Patron ID number. to enter their account.
    • Choose Add Identifier
    • Choose Identifier Type = Barcode
    • Scan ID card for Value

SAVE! And you're done!

add a note?

Patron Notes

A "note" produces a note on a User's account if information is needed.

  1. Enter the patron's account
    1. Pull up their account by name or ID number in ALMA
    2. Click on their ID number
  2. Click the tab that says "Notes"
  3. Click the "add note" button
  4. In the Note Description box, write your note and end with your initials and the date.
    1. The "Type" from the drop-down menu should be General, Circulation, Library or Other.
    2. User Viewable should only be chosen if appropriate.
    3. Pop up is a great new feature for notes you want to Pop up in a User's account
      1. Pop ups are not blocks, they will not keep items from renewing or anything like that
    4. click to enlarge this image
create an Info Desk "guest pass?"

Guest Pass

Information Desk students and staff check out guest passes to public patrons, but if that desk is closed we do it.

There is a metal binder which houses the computer use guest passes. Binder is located in top locked drawer to left of center computer at the Information Desk.

Typically, there are passes made up in advance after Midnight each night.

How to Create a Guest Pass from Scratch

(There is a red folder at the desk with printed instructions inside as well.)

 At the information desk on the far right computer (mouse and keyboard live inside of Kristin's office) there is a program called "PC Reservation," it has a purple icon. Open the program.

Click "Make Guest Pass" and select a number of passes you want to print.

Save each file with a different file name.

Open each file separately, and either write down the number or print it. (Writing preferable to not waste paper.)

Delete the files once done.

Tricky Situations

for an OSU patron not yet in the system

OSU Patron Not In Alma

If you have a new OSU Staff, Faculty, or Student who has an OSU ID and their record doesn't come up...

  1. Search their name in ALMA.

  2. Check their status using Atrium.

  3. Have them fill out a library card application

  4. Create a new patron record as if you're making a convenience card, with these changes:

    1. Primary Identifier = OSU ID number (don't swipe the card to fill it out)

    2. User group: ask if they're an undergrad, grad student, etc.

    1. Expiration date: 6 months from today

    2. Patron has institutional record: click Yes

    3. Click Update User

  5. After creating the account, you have to add their barcode so their card will swipe.

    1. Click on their Patron ID number. to enter their account

    2. Click Add Identifier

    3. Select Barcode as Identifier Type

      1. Swipe their card in the Value field, which will then create the identifier, the pop up for adding an identifier will remain open. Click on Close.

      2. If they do not have their physical OSU ID card yet, manually enter the barcode

        1. EXAMPLE: April Zeller, Primary Identifier = 930-639-957, barcode= 930639957

for a Convenience Card patron who is now an OSU patron?

Convenience Card Patron is Now an OSU Patron

  1. Verify they do or will have an ONID account.

    1. If they are an OSU patron who does not and will not have an ONID account, keep the account type as "Internal"

      1. Not all OSU patrons get an ONID account, such as OSU Associates, because their department has to pay for the ONID account.

      2. "Internal" Patrons must log in to their library card accounts just like a Convenience Card patron would.

    2. If they do or will have an ONID account a staff member must toggle the account type from "Internal" to "External"

      1. This operation must be done by a staff member due to Alma required permissions students do not have

      2. "External" patrons log in to their library accounts using their ONID information

  2. Changes to be made:

    1. The Primary Identifier must reflect the number on their current OSU ID card. Format the number with dashes. (ex. 933-000-000)

    2. The User Group must be changed to reflect their new user group (ex. OSU Staff, Undergrad, etc.)

    3. Update expiry date

      1. External (ONID) patrons for 3 months. OSU patrons should automatically update on Sunday with the next Banner load.

      2. Internal (Non-ONID) patrons for 1 year.

    4. Verify contact information is correct; address, phone number, email

    5. Update barcode to reflect current OSU ID card.

    6. SAVE!

  3. REMINDER : Please tell or show the patron how to login to their library account. It will change when they switch their account.

for a former OSU student/faculty member?

Former OSU Student/Faculty Member

  1. Search in Alma to see if they still have an account, expired or not.

    1. If they DO NOT have an account in Alma, create a new one just like a Convenience Card account.

    2. If they DO have an account in Alma, expired or not, continue.

      1. This operation must be done by a staff member due to Alma required permissions students do not have

  2. They need a convenience card (preferred)

    1. A staff member may make an exception to allow the former student/faculty to use their OSU ID as their library card (not preferred.)

      A note must be placed in Alma or on the library card application if this exception is made.

  3. A staff member must toggle the account type from "External" to "Internal"

  4. Ask the patron to fill out an application form.

  5. Use the data from the appliation form to update thier account. Changes to be made:

    1. The Primary Identifier must be changed to reflect their current library card.

    2. The User Group must be changed to Convenience Card.

    3. Add birth date if not in Alma.

    4. Update Expiration date by one year from today's date.

    5. Add password.

      Password = Patron last name (1st letter capital) and last 4 digits of ID no.

      If the patron's last name is 3 letters or less, add extra digits of the ID no. so total characters = 8

      (i.e., for a 3 letter last name add the last 5 digits of the patrons ID no.)

      The last name follows the following rules:

      1. No punctuation

      2. No hyphen

      3. No spaces

      4. Example:

        1. John Mac Gruder-Smith with ID# 000-186-954 would have the following password:“MacGruderSmith6954”

    6. SAVE!

  6. Update contact information.

  7. Update barcode to reflect current library card.

It is a good idea to go over how the patron will log in to their account as they will no longer use their ONID account.

It is also a good idea at the top of the Library Card Application where it says "How did you hear about our resident patron card?" to put "Former Student/Faculty"

for Affiliate S/P or Affiliate Dependent?

Affiliate-Spouse/Partner

Affiliate-Spouse/Partner is a spouse, partner, or dependent of an OSU student, Faculty, or Staff member.

  • Issued an OSU ID with the title "Affiliate S/P" and an OSU ID # that starts with "100." (Some of them start with 93#, for example if they were a former student)

  • Same borrowing rights as their spouse/partner/parent- so you have to ask if their partner/parent is faculty, staff, or student.

    • Affiliate dependent (minor) also eligible for same borrowing rights

  • Not in Banner and need to have a 93 number created for them which is why we need a library card application.

Card Type Eligibility ILL Privileges? Database Privileges?

Creating an Account

  1. Search in ALMA by the patron's name to see if they already have an account.

    1. Library account, but is is expired; you can look up their spouse/partner by name in Atrium to verify they are still active and update their account accordingly.

    2. No library account, have them fill out a Library Card Application.

      1. Verify their spouse/partner by name in Atrium to verify they are still active and update their account accordingly.

    3. Verifying in Atrium

      1) If they have ANY other status than listed below, they are a Convenience Card User Group.
      1. PtStudent ← this is a student, in Alma the User Group will usually be "Undergrad" or "Post-Bacc"
      2. PtEmployee ← this is a campus employee Staff or Faculty, in Alma the User Group will usually be "OSU Staff" or "OSU Faculty/GTA"
  2. In ALMA, under Manage Patron Services, click the Register a new patron.
  3. Fill out each required field with the information on the application.

    • Primary Identifier: Enter their ID number from their OSU ID card. They will use this university ID number to log into their account online.

    • User Group: Use spouse/partner status in Atrium - faculty, staff, or student, and select correct group from drop down menu

    • Campus: Select correct campus from drop down menu (OSU Main Campus)

    • Expiration date: one year

    • Birth date

    • User Management Information Patron has institutional record = No 

    • Password = Patron last name (1st letter capital) and last 4 digits of ID no.

      If the patron's last name is 3 letters or less, add extra digits of the ID no. so total characters = 8

      (i.e., for a 3 letter last name add the last 5 digits of the patrons ID no.)

      The last name follows the following rules:

      • No punctuation

      • No hyphen

      • No spaces

      • Example:

        • John Mac Gruder-Smith with ID# 000-186-954 would have the following password:“MacGruderSmith6954”Verify Password: same as above


    • Force password change on next login: Yes. Always check this box.

    • Email address: check appropriate box and enter email address

    • Addresses: Select Address type as "Work" and enter the patron's mailing address

    • Phone number: Select appropriate box and enter telephone number area code first. (format xxx-xxx-xxxx)

  4. Choose Update User to add the Patron Barcode

    • Click on their Patron ID number. to enter their account.

      • Choose Add Identifier

      • Choose Identifier Type = Barcode

      • Scan ID card for Value

      • Add and Close

  5. Add note:

    • Click on the "notes" tab

    • Click the "add note" button

    • In the note field add note: Affiliate Account: Name of their Spouse/Partner

    • In the Type drop-down menu select: Circulation

  6. Save and exit the record.

  7. Fill out the Staff Use section of the application

    • Mark off that you verified their photo ID & address

    • Write down the name of their OSU Spouse/Partner

    • Write down today's date & your initials

  8. Inform patron about their library account

    • They have the same borrowing privileges as their spouse/partner
    • Library brochure
    • How to log into their online account
  9. Place application in Circ inbox
for Visiting Scholars?

If a Visiting Scholar needs an account created in ALMA:

(formerly known as Affiliate Faculty)

What do we need?

  1. A completed VISITING SCHOLAR Account Application Form.
    1. The form needs to be signed by the Department hosting the Visiting Scholar.
    2. If the Visiting Scholar has an OSU ID, verify their status using Atrium.
    3. If they do not have an OSU ID, they will need a Convenience Card

Use the information on the form to create a "Convenience Card" account for the patron.

Set their expiration date to the date they are listed as leaving.

Reminder: Visiting Scholars do not get ILL. No study rooms, no laptops, no kindles.

  • They also do not get Summit privileges unless they are from a Summit participating school.

for Associates?

Associate Information: (from the ID Center)

Permanent employees of certain organizations and governmental agencies that are housed on OSU campuses and provide teaching, research or funding for OSU programs are eligible for an Associate ID card. Associates are eligible to purchase Recreational Sports (Dixon) memberships, ONID (OSU Network ID) accounts, OSU Card Cash account, and checking out materials at Valley Library. Associates are not eligible for free Corvallis Transit bus rides, remote access to Valley Library databases or interlibrary loan privileges (unless they have an ONID account.) Associate ID card fee is $30.00.

  • Check out privileges same as a Convenience Card. See
  • If they don't have a OSU ID card they can contact their Verifier for any questions
    • The list of verifiers (excel file) comes from the ID center.

Creating a Library Account

  1. Have the patron complete a Library Card Account Application Form
    1. If the Associate has an OSU ID, verify their status using Atrium.
      1. In Atrium, their tag will say "PtAssociate"
    2. If they do not have an OSU ID, they will need a Convenience Card.
  2. Use the Associate's information to create a "Convenience Card" User Group account for the patron.
    1. If they have an OSU ID, use the ID card for their Primary Identifier and Barcode.
    2. If they need a Convenience Card, use the numbers from the card for their Primary Identifier and Barcode.

Reminder: No study rooms, no laptops, no kindles. They can get ILL/database access if they have an ONID account.

for patrons under the age of 16?

Same as a REGULAR CONVENIENCE CARD except:

  • The application must have both their signature AND a parent or guardian's signature on it
  • High school ID is an acceptable form of picture ID
    • If they do not have a photo ID, you may use the photo ID of the parent who signed for them

OREGON Address still needs to be VERIFIED in order to open an account for a MINOR because they can still receive FEES BILLED TO THEM. Some never know they have overdue fees until they get a COLLECTION NOTICE FROM THE STATE.

for a visiting High School class?

A few times per year local high schools will bring in a class to check out books. The reason they have their own User Groups is to prevent them from receiving overdue fines, but they will still get replacement charges.

We encourage the teachers to bring in their library card applications in advance so they may be pre-loaded into Alma before their visit to ease desk congestion- but this does not always happen!

The steps for creating a High School class account are the same as a Convenience Card except: there are two special user groups for these students and their group depends on which school they attend.

  • High School Quarter; Lebanon School districts
  • High School Semester; Albany and Corvallis School districts 
  • NEWPORT high school has requested Convenience Card user group.

When creating a new account for these classes, be sure to give a library card pamphlet to the student.

Patron Accounts FAQ:

Can a patron have a Convenience Card for printing/food without a library account?

Yes.

There are two ways they can obtain a Convenience Card for printing/copying/Orange Cash.

  1. The Orange Cash add-value machine will dispense a Convenience Card for $1.
    1. This is useful because they can add value to the card for printing/food while they are there.
    2. Currently located in the lobby beside the Pepsi machines.
  2. We can give them one
Can a patron have two separate accounts?

No.

The University provides only one 93# for each person, that is how we bill them when they accrue fines. Alma does not allow two accounts to have the same 93#.

Also, there is no reason for a patron to have more than one account.

The "Open for Update" button

"External" patron accounts (OSU students, faculty, and staff) have a button inside them called "Open for Update." This button allows you to add/edit certain information on an OSU account. 

IF for some reason you need to use this button, always choose "No." 


Why? Banner automatically updates account information on Sundays, and choosing yes will prevent very important information changes on patron's accounts.

What's the difference between "Affiliate" and "Associate?"

An Affiliate is the Spouse or Partner of an OSU Student, Faculty or Staff member. They are allowed the same borrowing privileges as their partner. Their OSU ID number always starts with "100."

 An Associate is an employees of an organization or federal agencies housed on OSU campus, providing teaching, research, or funding to OSU are eligible for the Associate status. Their OSU ID number starts with "93#" and the word Associate is printed on their card.

Weirdness: There are "Associates" with 100# IDs that are not Affiliates. The ID will have the word "Associate" printed on it when this is the case.

We've run out of convenience cards and I need more!

Extra Convenience Cards can be found in the locked closet on top of the key cabinet.

How do Visiting Scholars get an OSU ID card?

OSU ID card for Scholar's webpage

They need to work with the department that is hosting them to get an OSU ID.

Can a patron use an old Convenience Card?

Yes!

It is not uncommon for a patron to have a Convenience Card. Whether they used to be a patron or they bought one for photocopying, we can definitely use it for a Convenience Card patron account!

What do you do? Use the card. On the library card application just make a note "Already had card."

Patron says they are not getting their emails!

If a patron says they are not getting their notification emails:

  1. Double check their email address first. Verify there are no typos and it is a current email address.
  2. Ask if they checked their spam folder.
  3. Ask if they have their email address set up to redirect to another email address. When these emails are returned to us as "undeliverable" there is no way for me to note the account that it needs fixed, because the bounced email comes from the redirected account, not the address they have in Alma.
  4. Test their account while they are standing there. A lot of people have email on their phone and can verify emails are getting through while you're helping them.

Summit Institution Accounts

How do I CREATE a Summit Institution Patron Account?
  1. Search in ALMA by the patron's name and/or their University ID number to see if they already have an account.
    1. If they already have an account, ask them log into their Summit Institution library account to check their expiration date with the home library and modify their ALMA record accordingly.
    2. If they don't have an account, continue.
  2. Have the patron log into their account from their home institution library (https://www.orbiscascade.org/member/) to get the patron's library account expiration date and verify their status as a current student/staff/faculty.
    1. Make a note of when their library account expires. This will be their expiration date in ALMA.

  3. Ask the patron to complete a library card application form.  
     
     

  4. In ALMA, under Manage Patron Services, click the Register a new patron.
    Fill out each required field with the information on the application.
    • Name: first, middle, last
    • Primary Identifier: Enter their ID number from their SUMMIT institution. They will use this university ID number to log into their account online.
      • Is their home institution PSU or WOU? Use the barcode on their ID as their primary identifier, not the magnetic stripe. Do not add a separate barcode identifier to their account.
    • User Group: Ask the patron if they are Faculty, Grad, Staff or Undergrad and select correct group from drop down menu
      1. Summit Visiting Faculty
      2. Summit Visiting Graduate
      3. Summit Visiting Staff
      4. Summit Visiting Undergrad
      5. NEVER USE "Summit Institution Patron." Don't do it.
    • Campus: OSU Main Campus
    • Expiration date: home institution's expiration date, noted from when they showed their library account

    • Birth date
    • User Management Information
      Patron has institutional record: No 
    • Password = Patron last name (1st letter capital) and last 4 digits of ID no.

      If the patron's last name is 3 letters or less, add extra digits of the ID no. so total characters = 8

      (i.e., for a 3 letter last name add the last 5 digits of the patrons ID no.)

      The last name follows the following rules:

      • No punctuation
      • No hyphen
      • No spaces
      • Example:
        • John Mac Gruder-Smith with ID# 000-186-954 would have the following password:“MacGruderSmith6954”
    • Verify Password: same as above
    • Force password change on next login: Yes. Always check this box.
    • Email address: check appropriate box and enter email address
    • Addresses: Select Address type as "Work" and enter the patron's mailing address
    • Phone number: Select appropriate box and enter telephone number area code first. (xxx) xxx-xxxx
  5.  Choose Update User to add SUMMIT ID and Barcode (remember PSU is different and weird, see above)
    •     Click on their Patron ID number. to enter their account.
      • Choose Add Identifier
      • Choose Identifier Type = Barcode (not WOU or PSU)
      • Scan ID card for Value
      • Enter SUMMIT ID TYPE in the notes field. (Example: UO ID)
      • Add and Close

  6. Save and exit the record. Swipe or scan the card and see if it will pull up their record. If it doesn't look them up by name.
  7. Fill out the Staff Use section of the application
    1. Mark off you verified their photo ID & address
    2. Write in their Summit Institution, and their school ID #
    3. Today's date & your initials
  8. Place application in Circ inbox
Summit FAQ, Reminders, & Weirdnesses
  • BARCODE weirdness.
    • If a SUMMIT member has an ID with a BARCODE on the front, it usually means the magnetic stripe on the back is not unique. Do not add the magnetic stripe to their account at all, only the unique identifier.
    • Once they have an account in Alma, scan the barcode (as if you were checking out a book) to pull up their account in the Find and Manage Users screen instead of swiping their card.
      • Known schools with the barcode on the front of their ID card: (fill out a follow-up form if you know of other schools that need to be on this list.)
        • PSU (Portland State University)
        • WOU (Western Oregon University)
  • EXPIRATION DATE weirdness:
    • If their library account does not list an expiration/graduation date, give them a 1-year expiration date.
  • Linn-Benton Community College is NOT a Summit Library. Check the website: https://www.orbiscascade.org/member/

  • Does the patron have trouble logging in to Primo? Check in ALMA to see how their Primary Identifier number is formatted.  

  • Do OSU Faculty still get overdue fines for Summit/ILL items? YES. Yes they do. And not likely to be appealed.

  • Can graduated students order Summit items? No. Not even if their ONID still works. Summit privileges are paid for by student fees.
How do I find Summit Libraries?

Go to this website to find Summit Libraries: https://www.orbiscascade.org/member/

Can a Visiting Scholar get Summit privileges?

If, and only if, they are visiting from a Summit Institution library. Check this website to see the list of Summit Libraries

If they are;

  1. Verify they are currently enrolled or working at the Summit Institution
    1. Ask them log into their Summit Institution library account to check their expiration date with the home library and modify their ALMA record accordingly.
    2. Ask if they are Faculty, Staff, Graduate Student, or Undergrad.
    3. Change their User Group accordingly to one of the four specific Summit User Groups
      1. Summit Visiting Faculty
      2. Summit Visiting Graduate
      3. Summit Visiting Staff
      4. Summit Visiting Undergrad
    4. NEVER USE "Summit Institution Patron." Don't do it.
  2. Change their Primary Identifier to their Summit Institution ID number
  3. Make sure they have a password so they may log in to Primo
How do Summit Patrons request books?
  1. They will login to Primo as a "Community Cardholder"
  2. Their username will be however their Primary Identifier is formatted.
    1. Since different schools have different kinds of ID numbers there can be a variety of formats.
  3. Their password will typically be their last name and the last four digits of their Primary Identifier
    1. If it's not working just reset it for them
  4. Once they are successfully logged in to Primo, they can request books!
