Loans and Returns by Fulfillment Unit

truenone

Overview

The "Loans and Returns by Fulfilment Unit" statistics are going on hold temporarily as of Summer 2017. The person who created and was responsible for pulling these statistics every term (Amila Hadziomerspahic) left the library before being able to update these statistics or find someone to continue taking the statistics.

The two analyses in Alma Analytics that are used to pull these statistics - "Loans by Fulfillment Unit" and "Returns by Fulfillment Unit" - have not been updated since Summer 2016 so the statistics they pull may not be accurate. Both analyses need to be updated with RAS and CM staff member last names that left or were hired. The "Fulfillment Unit" bins in both analyses also need to be updated to account for any location code changes, additions, or deletions since then. See the instructions below for rough guidelines on how to update these analyses. Before restarting collection of these statistics, the two analyses need to be updated and troubleshooted.

Loan and return statistics by fulfillment unit by term. Includes breakdown by hour and breakdown by day of the week.

Statistics by Term

Each term's statistics are attached to this wiki page.

  • (for quick comparison)
  • (6/20/16-9/2/16)
  • (3/28/16-6/10/16)
  • (1/4/16-3/18/16)
  • (9/24/16-12/11/16)
  • (6/22/16-9/4/16)
  • (3/30/15-6/12/15)
  • (1/5/15-3/20/15)

Instructions on Collecting Statistics for Each Term in Alma Analytics

The analyses used to pull these statistics can be found in the shared Alma Analytics folders under: Shared Folders > OSU > Dashboards > Loans and Returns by Fulfillment Unit

  1. In Analytics: Shared Folders > OSU > Dashboards > Loans and Returns by Fulfillment Unit > Edit
    1. This dashboard has 2 analyses: one for loans and one for returns. The format of the 2 analyses is identical but where the "Loans" analysis will have "Loan Date" and "Loan Operator Details" > "Last Name", the "Returns" analysis will have the "Return Date" and "Return Operator Details" > "Last Name". Aka, you cannot accurately combine loans and returns in one analysis because the fields are in different folders/sections!
    2. Both analyses have an "OR" boolean for the two "Last Name" filters. One filter is for excluding specific people's (3rd floor RAS staff) loan and return contributions. The second filter ("Last Name is null") is so that we DON'T exclude the loans and returns made by staff and students who no longer work here. I.e., their Last Name values become empty/null when their staff accounts are removed from Alma and if you don't include the "Last Name is null" filter then all of their loans/returns will be removed from the data! These two filters need to look like the following so that the "AND" boolean is in front of the first last name filter and the "OR" boolean is in front of the second last name filter. The "OR" filter needs to be grouped with (aka, shifted under) the first filter (do this by clicking on the boolean until it turns from "AND" to "OR" and then shifts in).
    3. More on the first Last Name filter: The "Returns" analysis excludes returns made at the "Main Circulation Desk" (aka, the Valley 2nd and 3rd floor check-in stations including the Circulation Desk) by the following people (using the field "Return Operator Details" > "Last Name") because they are CM or RAS staff that do a lot of returning: Layton, Moynihan, Rankin, Sites, Sterling, Varbel. This list excludes Moynihan because most of his returns are performed as RAS and CM staff and not at the Circulation Desk. Update the excluded names as needed (as staff leave / are hired). Also update the name of the "Main Circulation Desk" if it changes.
    4. The "Loans" analysis excludes loans made at the "Main Circulation Desk" (aka, the Valley 2nd and 3rd floor check-out stations including the Circulation Desk) by the following people (using the field "Loans Operator Details" > "Last Name") because they are CM or RAS staff that do a lot of loaning: Layton, Rankin, Sites, Sterling, Varbel. This list includes Moynihan because his loans are all performed at the actual Circulation Desk. Update the excluded names as needed (as staff leave / are hired). Also update the name of the "Main Circulation Desk" if it changes.
    5. The "Fulfillment Unit" field is actually the "Item Location" field with all of the different location codes manually binned into the fulfillment unit they belong to. Click on "Fulfillment Unit" menu and "Edit formula" to see how the location codes are binned. A good way to check whether there are location codes that were missed by the Fulfillment Unit bins is to check if there are any loans/returns in the "Everything Else" Fulfillment Unit bin. If there are, find the location code of the items corresponding to those loans/returns and add them to the bin of the appropriate Fulfillment Unit bin. New Alma location codes will also be at the top of the "Physical Locations List" in the fulfillment configuration menu. The location codes are current as of June 2015, update the location code bins as needed.
    6. Because the laptops and are effectively double-counted because we check out both the laptops and the charger, we filter out the charger loans and returns using the fact that the chargers' Description field has the word "Charger" in it. This is ungainly but it's the only way to filter them out. Like the "Last Name" filter, the "Description" filter actually involves two filters connected with an "OR" boolean. The first filter is "Description does not contain Charger" (this removes all loans / returns where Description includes "Charger" but it also removes all loans / returns where the item has a null Description field!). The second filter is "Description is null" (this adds back in the loans / returns on items with null Description fields).
    7. Filters example for the loan analysis:
    8. The results of the analyses have all the cell values repeated in every row. This isn't the standard Analytics format. To get this effect, in the Results tab, click "Edit View" (the pencil button) on the table >  then click the "Table View Properties" button in the top menu > in the window, click "Enable alternate styling" and then "Repeat cell values"

  2. For the new term, in both of the "Loans" and the "Returns" analyses (click on "Edit Analysis" to edit each analysis), edit the date range (loan date or return date) to the start and end date of the term in the Criteria tab. Run it, save it and export it as an Excel file.

  3. Copy all 4 columns from the exported Excel file and replace the 4 corresponding columns in that term's statistics spreadsheet. The data for both analyses is in the Data tab of the spreadsheet. Do this for both analyses. Make sure that none of last term's data is still in the 4 data columns (do this by deleting last term's data from the 4 columns before you copy-paste this term's data in those columns.)

  4. For both sets of the "Hour" and "Day of the Week" columns, make sure to recalculate all rows by double-clicking on the lower right corner of the first calculated cell in the column. Then, just in case this term's data set is longer than the previous term's data set, go to the LAST calculated cell in the column (Ctrl+End in that column) and double-click on its lower right corner to make sure all additional rows get calculated "Hour" and "Day of the Week" values.
    1. The "Loan Date" column should always have the cell format of "Date". If it doesn't, the pivot tables will have incorrect "(blank)" rows/columns with loans and returns in them!
    2. The "Hour" column takes the data from the "Loan Time" column and rounds it to a value that corresponds to that hour's proportion between 0 and 1 using the ROUND() function. Then the column format has to be "Time" in order for this method to work correctly and convert the decimal to an hour value. David found this method on the internet of rounding time to the nearest hour.
    3. The "Day of the Week" column uses the TEXT() function to convert dates to text.

  5. Go to the "Charts" tab and refresh the pivot tables (the "Refresh All" button is in the Data tab), they should update automatically as should the pivot charts. Don't forget to update the term's name in the charts, e.g., from "Spring 2016" to "Summer 2016". If the pivot tables and charts don't automatically update here's what you have to change:
    1. Column Labels: filter out "In Library" and "(blank)"
    2. The hours column may be messed up. Select it, right click and "Format Cells", choose "Time" in the "Number" tab to ensure that the Row Labels are in "Time" format.
    3. There will be two "12 am" rows, the first and last rows, to group these two together as they should be, click on one of them and then on the "Group Field" button under Pivottable Tools > Analyze. In the Grouping window, group by "Hours" only and then OK. This merges the two "12 am" rows into one, and also changes the number format.
    4. You shouldn't have to manually update the last two charts that combine the return and loan data into one graph because each cell in those tables is calling values from the pivot tables using the "GetPivotTable" function.

Lockers

truenonefalse

Overview

Locker info is posted on the library website.  

  • Sandy Graham is the Locker Coordinator for the Valley Library.
  • The library has 366 lockers located throughout the building, along the avenue on each floor.
  • We also have  staff lockers located at the LEAD desk and in the Annex/Map prep areas of the 3rd-floor offices.
  • With a few exceptions, "even" numbers are lower lockers, and "odd" numbers are upper lockers.
  • Locker use policies are posted inside every locker door and also on the website.

Locker types

Expand

 30-day
Patron types

OSU students, faculty and community members

Locker will automatically renew three times:

  • As long as there is no wait list. If there is a wait list, you must return the key by the due date. You will receive the reminder email four days beforehand.
  • If the key has already renewed three times, you will receive the reminder email four days beforehand.
 Due date is automatically set to the last day of the term. They can be checked out for another term as long as employment continues.
Overdue fees and billing No overdue fees.  Lost locker keys are assessed a $30 fine. If the locker key is returned within a year, the $30 fee is removed.   Staff lockers do not get overdue fees. However, they will lapse into lost status if they are overdue for more than six days. Staff locker keys are considered employee office equipment and staff members who use them are not billed for lost keys.
Location  Lockers available for staff, faculty, students and community members  are located on all 6 floors
  • 6 lockable staff lockers near the LEAD main desk
  • 18 staff lockers in the 3rd-floor Annex and Mat Prep area
  • Media Hub manages their own lockers and they are located in the Media Hub department

If possible, staff should be given lockers closest to their primary work area

Borrowing

Locker keys are stored in the grey gladiator type storage bins at the LEAD desk. Staff locker keys are stored separately in their own bins.

Checking out a staff locker

See for more information about staff lockers

  1. Determine the staff member's eligibility:
    1. We do not require proof of employment (non-employees are unable to access the staff locker areas).
    2. Preference is given to student employees or others who do not have an individual work space.

  2. Ask for photo ID and bring up the patron record in Alma.

  3. Determine the primary work area of the student employee: LEAD desk or 3rd floor office.
  4. Retrieve an available staff locker key from the bin for the corresponding office. The staff locker key bins are located with all the other key bins at the LEAD desk.
  5. Scan the barcode to check out the key.
  6. The due date should be automatically set to the end of the current term.

    1. If the due date is not set to the end of the previous term, manually change the due date to the last day of the current term.

      Why does this happen?

      The end of term due date is an Alma calendar management event that has to be manually changed by the hours coordinator after the end of every term, which sometimes takes a couple days.
  7. If it is close to the end of term and the employee will be employed for the next term, change the due date from the default last day of current term to the last day of the next term.
    1. Be sure the locker key is selected and click Change Due Date (also an option in the Actions drop-down menu).
    2. In the Select Due Date window, click in the New Due Date field, use the mini-calendar to navigate to the last day of the next term, and double-click the date to select it. (Or just type out the date in the box.) Leave the due time field blank.
  8. Click Done.

Renewing

Renewing a staff locker key

Staff locker keys do not automatically renew, but employees can check them out again for a new term as long as they continue to work at the library. Follow the instructions above for .

Staff locker is in Lost Status and locker needs to be renewed:

  •  Select locker
  •  In the ellipsis sandwich box on the right, select "found item"
  •  Select locker again and change due date to end of quarter.

Requesting

Locker request policies

  • Location preference: Patrons sometimes ask for a specific locker or a locker on a particular floor. Locker are first-come, first-served basis if there is no wait list. 
  • Multiple requests: If multiple lockers are available then it is fine to check out multiple lockers to a patron. 
  • Locker records are not visible in Primo. Patrons are unable to place holds on lockers.  Lockers will auto-renew three times if there are no requests

Finding a key record by locker number in Alma

Repository search won't work because...

The locker number is only listed in the "alternative call number" field in the locker key item record. If it were listed in the "description" field like most items, having the unique entries for the individual locker numbers would cause the item records to separate and give patrons the ability to request locker keys at the item level in Primo which could break the request queue. Because a basic search doesn't include alternative call numbers, this means that individual locker keys cannot be easily found using a basic repository search.

Quick reference: Alma menu > repository search > advanced search > Find: physical items > add conditions > alternative call number > type (locker # you are looking for) in search field > Select "Go"

Detailed instructions:

  1. From the Alma main menu, select repository search
  2. Click the "advanced search" link in the repository search screen
  3. In the "Find" drop down menu select "physical items"
    1. The alternative call number search condition is only available from the physical items search
  4. Click the "add conditions" button
  5. Select the "alternative call number" checkbox
  6. Type the locker number that you are looking for in the search box
  7. Select the "Go" button
  8. There should only be a few items, but you can use the facet search options to select only equipment items which should filter out most things that are not lockers

Verifying which locker a patron has checked out

  1. Ask for photo ID and bring up the patron record in Alma.
  2. In the Loans tab, select Loan Display "All" and find the locker in the list. If the list is too long, you can search by title keyword "lockers" to locate it.

  3. The locker number does not display on this screen, so you have to click the barcode to open the locker item record.

    Picture

  4. On the item record screen, find the locker number in the Alternative call number field.

    Picture

Lost Keys

Patron forgot key and needs to get in locker

  1. Ask for photo ID and bring up the patron record in Alma to .
  2. Retrieve the master locker key from the key cabinet in the secure closet.
  3. Accompany the patron to the locker and unlock it for them.
  4. Explain that the locker door will lock when the patron closes it.
  5. Return the master locker key to the key cabinet in the secure closet.

Patron reports a key lost

  1. Ask for photo ID and bring up the patron record in Alma to .
  2. Check lost and found lockers keys on the Locker Coordinator's desk.

  3. Ask a LEAD staff member on duty to talk with the patron about the replacement process.

    Staff Responsibilities

    Explain the replacement fee ($30 and non-refundable once the lock has been changed, see replacement costs on the website) and ask whether the patron wants to keep looking for the key or go ahead with the replacement process.

    If the patron decides to keep looking:

    1. Look at the due date. Offer to renew the locker to give the patron more time to look without worrying about replacement fees.
    2. Offer to open the locker if needed (see ).
    3. Tell the patron to let us know if the key does not turn up, so that we can move ahead with the replacement process.

    If the patron is sure the key is lost:

    1. Note the due date for the key:
      1. In most cases we can offer the patron a different locker. When checking out the new locker match the due date to the lost locker.
      2. Mark the key lost in Alma: In the patron record, find the key in the Loans tab, then click Actions > Lost. Alma does not prompt you to confirm! The "Lost Item" message should indicate the replacement fee of $30 was charged.
    2. Picture

    3. Offer to open the locker, if the patron still has belongings inside (see ).
    4. Tell the patron to return the key if it is found. Returning a lost key reverses the replacement fee if the lock has not been changed and a replacement key cut.
    5. Fill out the Follow-up Form to alert the lockers coordinator a lock change is needed. Include patron info, locker info, and describe actions taken and decisions reached with the patron.

Patron returns a lost key

  1. Check in the key as you would normally.
    • If there is a popup message stating that the lock has been changed:
      1. Explain to the patron that the $30 key replacement fee is non-refundable once the lock has been changed, as we have already paid to get a new key cut.

  2. Fill out a follow up form and put key in the locker bin located (TBD).

Patron claims to have returned a key

  1. Do not use the "claimed return" button in Alma.
  2. Offer to renew the locker so the patron does not accrue overdue fees.
  3. Fill out a locker follow up form with as much information as possible and explain that the lockers coordinator will search for the key and get back to them.

Lost and found

Locker key turned in
  1. Fill out the Follow-up Form to alert the lockers coordinator a key was turned in and include as much information as possible. The lockers coordinator will contact the patron.  
  2. Place the key in the bin located in the locked closet labeled Lost and Found Locker keys with a note on the key with the date the key was found. Do not make a log entry in the lost and found binder.
Locker key claimed
  1. Ask for photo ID and bring up the patron record in Alma to confirm which locker the person has checked out.
  2. Retrieve the key from lost and found bin on the coordinator's desk.
  3. Give the key to the patron and remind them of their due date.

Items in Lockers

Patron finds a previous user's belongings in a locker

Ask a LEAD staff member on duty to take care of it.

Staff Responsibilities
  1. See if the last patron information is still available in Alma:
    1. Open the item record by clicking the barcode link in the current patron's Loans list or the Physical Items Repository Search results.
    2. Click on the History tab and select the "Fulfillment activities" button. If the last patron information is still available, it will be in the "Borrower name/id" columns on the right.
  2. Grab some boxes and go to the locker with the patron to remove the items.
  3. Label the items with the locker number, date, and last patron name/ID if known.
  4. Email the last patron if known.
  5. then submit a follow-up form.

If you can't get away from the desk:

  1. Offer the patron a different locker.
  2. Check in the key and put it in repair.
  3. See if the last patron information is still available in Alma:
    1. Open the item record by clicking the barcode link in the current patron's Loans list or the .
    2. Click on the History tab and select the "Fulfillment activities" button. If the last patron information is still available, it will be in the "Borrower name/id" columns on the right.
  4. Fill out the Follow-up Form with all the information you have so that the lockers coordinator can follow up.

Patron picks up items we removed from a locker

Personal belongings

Items can be removed from a locker if they are left in a returned locker or the key is billed and replaced.

  1. Ask for photo ID and bring up the patron account in Alma.
  2. Check the black closet. Personal belongings removed from a locker are placed in lost and found closet with the patron's name, locker number, and the date. Be sure you grab all of the materials, because sometimes they are multiple piles.
    • If it has been a long time since the locker was cleared, the materials were sent to central lost and found. Offer the patron a lost and found referral card.
    • If the personal belongings happened to be perishable food, it was thrown away.
Library materials
  1. Ask for photo ID and bring up the patron account in Alma.
  2. Check the hold shelf. Library materials removed from a locker will be on hold in Alma and can be checked out as usual.

  3. If you do not see any library materials on hold for the patron, refer to the scenarios described below:

    Background...

    Patrons must check out library materials before placing them in a locker. During the quarterly locker check, we open each locker and if we find any library materials, we look them up to make sure they are checked out. Any materials not checked out are removed to the LEAD office where:

    • available library materials get a request placed on the locker patron's account and are routed to the hold shelf for pickup
    • library materials with a patron request are placed on hold for the other patron
    • non-circulating library materials (such as current journals) are returned to the stacks

    In any case, we email the locker patron to explain the situation. We refer the patron to the Information desk for help locating any library materials we cannot place on hold (because they do not circulate or they have been requested by others).

Damage

Locker key returned with a broken tag or with no tag

  1. Fill out the LEAD Follow-up Form:
    1. Note that the key has not been checked in and make sure to include the date.
    2. If the patron is present, include name and ID too. Assure the patron we will look up the key and check it in. If the patron is worried about being penalized for the lost tag, explain that we do not charge a replacement fee for the tag (only the key).
  2. Place it in the LEAD desk inbox.

The lockers coordinator will look up the key, check it in (adjusting the return date accordingly), and replace the tag.

Patron reports trouble opening or closing a locker


Go to the locker with the patron and try opening and closing it. Common scenarios:

  • Patron wasn't sure how the key or the door handle works. For example, to close a locker you press the door shut, rather than lift the handle. Demonstrate and have the patron try it out.
  • Door sticks a little. Try pressing the metal prongs in the door a few times to see if it helps.
  • Handle is loose. Report this problem to the locker coordinator and offer the patron a different locker.
  • Lock is loose. Report this problem to the locker coordinator and offer the patron a different locker.

Fill out the Follow-up Form with complete locker info. Check in the key and place a work order on key by using the "scan in" tab in Alma and put key in locker coordinators inbox located at the LEAD desk (location TBD).  Check out another locker key to patron.


Staff Responsibilities

Lost & Found

Lost and Found Coordinator: 

Service Desk Responsibilities - Receiving Lost Items

  • Put all found items in the locked closet where keys are stored.
  • Items with food or liquid are to be emptied before putting in the lost and found.
  • Items that have a strong odor are to be placed in a bag and sealed before being placed in the lost and found.
  • Items with contact information are to be given to a staff member.  They will email the owner from the valley.library email account.
  • High value items (IDs, credit cards, wallets, cash, documents, keys, flash drives, medicine and items estimated to be worth $100 or more), are to be logged into the lost and found binder kept at the Borrowing and Information Desk.
    • Loose cash should be put in an envelope.  Put date, amount and your initials on the envelope. Do not separate cash from wallets.

  •  If Patrons ask to leave contact information for a lost item, fill out a follow-up form for them. Use the category 'Other' and collect contact information and a description of the lost item.

    1. Patrons may also fill out the Lost Item Form on the Central Lost and Found website

Service Desk Responsibilities - Helping Someone Seeking a Lost Item

  • Ask the person to describe the lost item.
  • Look in the lost and found before telling them that we have their item even if you are sure it is there. (It's better not to get anyone's hopes up!)
  • If we have the item check to see if it is logged into the lost and found binder.
    • If it's in the binder, have them sign for it and then give them the item.
    • If it's not, just give them the item.
  • If we don't have the item.
    • Encourage patron to check back again
    • Direct them to the Lost Item Form on the Central Lost and Found website.
    • Give them a business card with Lost and Found contact information, explaining how the Lost and Found process works.

Staff Only Responsibilities

Contacting the Owner

  1. Only staff members should contact owners about lost items.
  2. Email templates can be found on the  page and in the Valley Library email "Drafts" folder.
    1. Use corresponding high value, low value, or OSU ID templates
    2. CC Valley Library and Bcc the Lost & Found coordinator.

Timeline & Next Steps for Lost & Found Items

  1. All Lost & Found items are held for up to 1 week.

  2. High value items are bagged up by the Lost & Found Coordinator and picked up by OSU Department of Public Safety every Saturday.

    1. Unclaimed cash from the lost and found is placed in the key return box on the 4th floor as a donation to the LEA.

  3. All Low value items are boxed every Saturdays by the Lost & Found Coordinator and picked up by Campus Recycling.

Mail Delivery and Pickup

We are all responsible for taking care of our own outgoing mail and share responsibility for taking care of incoming mail. When you are in the loading dock,

    • If you don't wish to deliver mail yourself to others in the library you can put it in the Library Mail bin at the third floor mailing station
    • Outgoing Campus Mail, US Postal Service, and UPS items are placed on the "Outgoing Campus Mail" shelf in the loading dock
      • Mail should have payment method attached. 
        • Attach a  to USPS items
    • Outgoing Fed Ex items are placed on the "Outgoing Fed Ex" shelf in the loading dock
  • Incoming
    • Most mail and packages will be found in the LEAD shelf on the loading dock. Large package maybe on the floor or a cart.
    • Put mail on peoples desk unless it is too large in which case you can just put it in their workspace.
    • For Media Hub mail, please put mail just inside the back door into the staff space and on the wall to your right. Boxes can be placed outside of Teressa's office. 

For procedures related to accepting deliveries and the loading dock space, see:





Managing the "Promoting Your Materials" Request Form

Timing: By request

Through the "Promoting Your Materials" form, people can request: 

  1. Social media posts
  2. Kiosk slides
  3. Library newsfeed posts
  4. Library highlight tiles

 

How we process the request varies slightly depending on what they request. 

If a patron requests:

  1. Library newsfeed post
    1. You'll need permissions to edit the library website, but once you do, you will add a post to the library website. 
  2. Library Highlight Tiles
    1. Forward the information to the form to Kenna kenna.warsinske@oregonstate.edu & cc Eduardo (Kenna’s student worker) gonzedua@oregonstate.edu and the requester. This makes it easier for Kenna and Eduardo to follow up with the requester, and vise versa
  3. Social media post
    1. I usually will send a follow-up email along the lines of:
    1. I always try to email the requester back as soon as possible, even if it’s just to share that I received their request and will process it as soon as possible. 

Hello x,
Thank you so much for submitting a social media request form! It looks like you’d like to post a job advertisement on Tuesday, March 23, 2022 on Twitter, Instagram, and Facebook. We absolutely can do that! 

    1. Always try to note their answer to What is the latest date this can be posted?
      1. Is it possible to post it in time? If not, try to clarify expectations as soon as possible, and verify that if the post cannot be posted by that date that they still want it posted.
    2. If they have provided the graphics and caption- that’s great! Double check that it will be appropriate for the platform they want to use (is the file type compatible? Is the size of the graphic okay? Is the caption too long? Is there a super long link that you should shorten for instagram?)
      1. If you have to update the caption or graphic, I recommend emailing them with alternative options and explaining the situation. 
      2. If you make a beav.es link for them, pass it along to them! It may be helpful 
    3. If they have not provided graphics, that’s totally fine. It may extend the amount of time it takes us to post the info to social media.
      1. If they need a graphic, hopefully they have provided a description of what they’re looking for. If they haven’t, I will usually forward a similar post we’ve made in the past and offer to make something similar.
        1. I’ll say something like “Usually for a post like this, I like to include a graphic so the post is a bit more eye-catching. I’ve attached some examples of what we’ve used in the past. Would you like me to make something similar for you?”
          1. This also works if they initially do not request a graphic (see below) Usually requesters don’t ask for anything elaborate. If you get a complicated request, you can either make an attempt with the amount of time you have, or you can recommend the services of the graphic designers at the MU Creative Studio if there’s enough time allotted
          2. Sometimes folks will say they don’t need a graphic- I usually still offer to make one, with the insight that an image helps make the post more noticeable, and allow us to post on Instagram as well as other social media posts. If they still don’t want one, that’s fine! 
    4. Usually requesters have a caption in mind. If not, I’d keep it simple as possible
  1. Colleague-requested Social Media Series requests: Example: Crafternoons & Mental Health Book Recommendations: Sometimes, folks will request a series of posts to be posted periodically (often once-a-week) for a period of time (often through a term). Robin, who is the student worker for TED, usually supplies graphics and captions, which is so helpful! When the captions and graphics are already supplied, it makes our job a lot easier. Once the graphics have been created, the scheduling aspect is the same:
    1. With social media requests, you would have already been communicating with the requester about the frequency & timing of the posts. Once that’s established, (Similarly to #tbt) I recommend putting reminders on your outlook calendar to remember to post. (If you find an alternate system that works for you, that’s totally okay!) 
    2. You don’t have to post at the same time every week, but I would try your best to make sure to post on the agreed-upon dates, barring extenuating circumstances. Things happen, and when they do, I just recommend checking in with the requesting person.

Managing TV Slides

TV Slides:

Timing: Once a month

Process:

  1. At the beginning of the month before: Create a desktop folder named “[Next Month’s] TV Slides” this helps keep track of the necessary slides. 
  2. Over the course of the month: When creating and scheduling slides for the next month, make sure to create circ TV slides:


Appropriate TV slides: 

  • Term/break hours
  • Closures 
  • Small Equipment Slides
  • Ongoing programs
  • Vaccination Info

Not-great TV slides:

  • One-off events
  • Slides with a lot of text
  • Slides with tiny graphics
  1. At the end of the month before: review the collection of slides, verify file type, size, dates, etc. We update the TV slides once a month, so keep that in mind!

 Remember: All TV Slides MUST be 600x300 pixels, in JPEG. If not, they will not work

  1. Collect the USB drives on the TVs and replace the old files with the new files. (This is where that monthly folder really comes in handy!)
  2. When replacing the USB drives, be sure to double check all of the slides on the TVs to make sure they are all working. If not, you may have to troubleshoot. 
    1. Sometimes you have to reset the USB drive. If that doesn’t fix the problem, double check the file format and dimensions of the malfunctioning slides
      1. To reset the USB drive, insert a USB drive into your computer. 
        1. Open “This PC”
        2. Right-click the USB, select “format” 
        3. Under “format”, click “restore device defaults”
          1. This should clear the USB drive

Media Hub After-Hours Equipment Returns

If a patron brings a Media Hub item when they are closed and wants to return it, ask the patron if they can return it when they are open. Direct them to the hours posted the Media Hub website.

If a patron will be unable to return when the Media Hub is open, ask a staff member for help. LEAD staff can accept a Media Hub item for return as an exception. It isn't a service we're advertising; it exists so that we can help patrons who are truly in a bind.

Find additional copies of the form here: 

Staff instructions
  1. Obtain an After Hours Return slip from the "extra forms" binder beneath the counter.
  2. Have the patron fill out it out completely. There are 3 fields for them to fill out.
  3. The patron takes the yellow copy.
    1. If the patron refuses their receipt, they can't return their item.
  4. Fill out the Administrative Use Only portion.
  5. The white copy goes with the item.
  6. Place the return on the Media Hub equipment checkout desk (The "L" shaped desk next to the customer entrance to their studio space). Put the return slip on top of the item.
    1. At closing: The after-hours returns can stay on the Media Hub returns spot after the library is closed; they do not need to be moved to thier tech equipment room.
    2. Items without return slips: Sometimes Media Hub items are returned in Circulation's book drops or found in the library after they have already closed. For these items, put a note with the time it was returned on the item and place it on the Media Hub returns spot.

If we are out of After Hours Return slips: Contact Teresa Preddy, the Media Hub manager, and ask her for more carbon-copied return slips.

Notes from DLS Conference April 2014: Stephen Bells Keynote on Virtual Users

Keynote Steven Bell:  ()

  • " Alt-higher ed " --( article on it )  idea of how it's changing with online learning via MOOC like situations. Higher ed expensive, huge student debt, lots can be learned on your own online. Predictions of students going for a few years only enough to get some sort of a job (like an AA degree) but then use moocs for the key learning you need, at multiple institution,  3-7 years, non linear and unpredictable. Also companies are rising up to help train students in real world needs of employers by adding value to higher ed. Ex- Koru is a bootcamp for college grads from liberal arts institutions to learn key skills has already signed agreements w 13 institutions to get their grads into this bootcamp post graduation (costs extra though)
  • Virtual Gate Opening --  Next he talked about changing the online user experience. Focus on people not content as we are not gate keepers. One great example was the Enterprise Rental Car recent commercials  - "We all have the power to make it right" -  they redesigned their customer service instead of focusing on cars to people, as they discovered dealing w/ people's problems is always the biggest issue and provides best customer service. They went from bottom in rental car company customer service to almost the top in 2 years. Can we do this in libraries?  Another example is the  Seattle  Pikes Fish Market. Joseph Michelli is the visionary behind this change from the fish market going under to where it is today. Called a "Way we serve statement" or an  "experiential brand statement" NOT marketing but empowering statement and way of changing behaviors. (For Pikes is was "treat people as if they are world famous")  Should be an easy to remember phrase that employees live not a marketing gimmick/mission statement. Michelli has a Way We Serve development tool you can use in your library! (pdf)    Check out the book - The new Gold Standard, about the Ritz Carleton hotels experience to a amazing customer service motel. Their service credo "we pledge to provide the finest personal service and facilities for our guest" w/ steps of service -  intro self, make eye contact, ask if you met their need. Why this is so impt- everyone is responsible and can't push it off on someone else! Also check out the Zappos Experience for a more online UX. Lots to read!
  • Customer journey mapping -- To change the experience, need to study the customers journey, map it out and find a better process. Carnegie in Pittsburgh did this design process they mapped every customers potential journey.  Do this as a staff, virtual journey mapping,  even small processes such as ereserves, what are all the step for a customer and how many different processes are there!
  • 5 C's of distance library UX
    • Convenient - must be easy for them
    • Consistent  - things similar online so students can find what they need every time
    • Competent  - have everyone everywhere be ready to help in all areas
    • Connected - harder area to reach to make them feel connected
    • Community - this is the hardest!

Buy What's Actually Needed (Facts v. Opinions); Positive Relationships Creates Campus Advocates;  Library as a Source of Insight (Not Just Books); Develop Political Awareness

Hello Friends


Fridge Clean Out Alert


On next <DATE> the refrigerator and freezer in the Oasis will be cleaned out and anything that isn't labeled with a name and date will be discarded.


If you have something in the fridge that you aren't able to label before then, please let me know and I'll label it for you.


Oasis Reminders/General Use Information


The Oasis exists for the use of all staff in LEAD and MH. That is quite a few people! Please take the wilderness mantra to heart and try to always leave it in a little better shape than you found it.


Here are a few guidelines to help keep the Oasis in good condition:


  1. Label your items with your name and a date. Unlabeled items are subject to be discarded or eaten by others w/o notice.
  2. If you have items that you’d like to share, label them with who can use them. Examples include MH, LEAD, or ALL.
  3. Dishes, cups, and silverware are there for everyone to use. However, if you use them, YOU are responsible for cleaning, drying, and returning them to the Oasis. The closest place to do this is in the staff lounge on the 3rd floor. You can use work time to do this.
  4. Recycling: Please recycle what you can and rinse out containers and bottles before putting them in the bins. If you aren’t sure if something can be recycled, throw it out! Rima and Uta are both trained recycling ambassadors and can help with any questions you might have.


Questions? Please ask!

<NAME>

Oasis, the Office Food & Drink Area

Overview

The Oasis is the staff break area at the back of the Circulation Office (near room # 2011, which is the empty space at the back of the office) and it includes:

Staff and student employees from all LEAD units are encouraged to use this space during their paid or unpaid breaks, as it makes for an easier trip than going to the 3rd floor staff lounge. The Oasis does not have a sink, water cooler, or any cooking appliances with open heating elements.

We sell scantrons, bluebooks, and notecards at the Borrowing & Information Desk.

We do not accept cash for these transactions; instead, fees are added to a patron’s account using the “University Shop” code.

Alma transaction:

  • Bring up the patron's record in Alma
  • Click on the patron’s Active Balance or their ID number hyperlink
  • Click the “Add Fine or Fee” button. 
    • Fee Type = University Shop
    • Owner = Valley Library-Corvallis
    • Fee Amount = Total charge
    • Item Barcode = <blank>
    • Comment = what and how many were purchased. Ex: 4 large blue books.
  • Click “Add and Close”
  • Click “Save” to save the fee and “Done” exit the patron’s account


What if I accidentally selected "Credit" instead of "University Shop"?

If you accidentally selected "Credit" instead of "University Shop," don't panic! Use the following steps to fix the error:

  1. Now that there is a "Credit" on the patron's account, add the correct charge for the purchased supplies.
    1. Click the “Add Fine or Fee” button
    2. Be sure the Fee Type is listed as “University Shop”
    3. Fill in the corresponding amount
    4. In the Comment box, please note what and how much was purchased. Ex: 4 large blue books.
    5. Click “Add and Close”
  2. The patron's account will now have a zero balance. It is very important that you add a final charge to the patron's account using the fee type, "Other." This will ensure that the funds will come and go from the right place.
    1. Click the “Add Fine or Fee” button again
    2. Select "Other" as the Fee Type
    3. Fill in the corresponding amount
    4. In the Comment box, add a note that states: "To negate accidental credit"
    5. Click “Add and Close”

You will end up with three transactions on the patron's account, like the example below.

Ordering Supplies

Ordering Supplies 

We aren't currently reordering. Last order was in 2018. Consult with Department Head before placing a new order. 

  • The primary purpose of the coordinator is to manage the supply inventory and place orders in a timely fashion to avoid shortages or stock-outs. There is an excel sheet on the shared drive entitled "Office supplies - current inventory" for previous inventory numbers or to get an idea of how much to order at the start of term, etc. Keep it updated as much as possible to detect any trends in supply popularity.
  • In the past, orders were placed monthly as supplies got low. However, in Fall 2018, it was decided to order 6 months worth (based on past terms needs) to avoid so many trips to the Beaverstore.
  • Our order for Fall 2018 was as follows:
      • 250 packs of Oxford, blank, 3x5 notecards (<---- can also be lined depending on what the Beaverstore has available)
      • 200 large blue books
      • 100 small blue books
      • 350 large, blue scantrons (form 95677)
      • 75 small, green scantrons (form 882-E)
  • Submit a purchase order via Benny Buy
  • You will need to walk over to the Beaverstore to pick up the supplies; be sure to take a dolly, your OSU ID card, and a copy of the purchase order.

Checking for errors and fixing mistakes

  • Errors can only be fixed using the method listed about if a credit was issued in error.
  • Alternatively,
  • To be continued...


Analyzing purchasing trends

  • The informal sales sheet is kept on the Shared drive under Circulation > Office Supplies for Sale > Supply Stats (informal).xlsx

  • This spreadsheet is used to periodically input the handkept record of sales (using the sales sheets kept at the desk) and allows us to analyze the data to perceive trends and totals for each month, term, and year of supply sales.

  • The totals are not exact but provide a rough estimate. Thus far, there has been an upward trend in total sales as more students become aware of this resource. Additionally, notecards, psychology scantrons, and large blue books appear to be the most popular of items sold.

OSU Libraries & Press Party Pack

OSULP Party Pack + Tote Box + Bag

(document attached)

(document attached)


Thank you for reserving and using the OSULP Party Pack! By choosing to use reusable materials for your event, you are helping OSULP to operate as a more sustainable organization. Your participation in this effort is valued. The plates, cups, bowls and utensils in the OSULP Party Pack are dishwasher safe.

Contents of the Party Pack - PLEASE inventory before AND after your event.

large plates                                                         knifes                                          

small plates                                                         forks

bowls                                                                  spoons

cups                                                                   1 carry bag/1 Party Pack sign

 

Reservations & Care Instructions

  1. Please reserve the Party Pack in advance of your event to ensure its availability:
    1. Reservation Sheet (http://bit.ly/osulp-party)
  2. Email Uta.Hussong-Christian@oregonstate.edu (current contact) to arrange for pick up/return of the Party Pack
    1. you may wish to bring a book truck with you as the tote is bulky
  3. At the beginning of your event, remind your colleagues/attendees that the Party Pack items are not disposable
    1. provide a location for the items to be returned for cleaning (the plastic bin itself is a great option...store any extra serving ware in the tote bag)
    2. display the Party Pack sign near the Party Pack items
  4. Upon conclusion of your event, check the trash to make sure no Party Pack items were thrown away
  5. Please use the 3rd Floor Staff Lounge dishwasher or the 4th floor South Kitchenette dishwasher to clean and dry the dishes
    1. please do not stack the plates on top of each other in the dishwasher bottom rack as they are lightweight and may get pushed out of the rack onto the heating coils where they will melt
    2. you may need to do multiple loads of dishes; please use the dishwasher detergent pods included in the Party Pack (they contain biodegradable detergent and are free of dyes, chlorine and phosphates
      1. with dry hands, place one (1) detergent pod in the main detergent cup and close the cover (the pods do not need to be broken open, but can be if they do not fit)
      2. use the second/third detergent pods to do additional loads of dishes, if needed
    3. place the clean and dry dishes back into the plastic tub
  6. Please account for all Party Pack items and make sure the inventory matches the contents noted above
  7. Return the Party Pack to the location agreed upon with Uta Hussong-Christian
  8. Alert Uta Hussong-Christian if any Party Pack item breaks or is no longer usable
  9. Promote the use of the Party Pack to your colleagues

History

The Sustainability Committee brainstormed the acquisition of a Party Pack inspired by Corvallis's own Green Girl: https://www.facebook.com/Green-Girl-1724492821118516/

The Sustainability Committee presented the idea at the November 2016 Admin Briefing; Faye was receptive and indicated she was amenable to funding (the Committee had originally approached the OSULP Staff Association Committee in early November 2016 about funding but had not carried through with a detailed proposal). Based on Faye's response, the Sustainability Committee sought LEAD department approval (via Beth) and proceeded to order a 30-place setting from Preserve Products (https://www.preserveproducts.com/). They were running a 50% off promotional sale, so the order was placed for the 30-pack On the Go collection (https://www.preserveproducts.com/shop/shareware-on-the-go-tableware-pack-for-30-55) to which we added 32 bowls (https://www.preserveproducts.com/shop/tabletop/bowls).

The items were placed in a rugged plastic tote, accompanied by 3 dishwashing detergent pods for each use. The instructions above were printed and included in the tote.

Patron Notes

A "note" produces a note on a User's account if information is needed.

  1. Enter the patron's account
    1. Pull up their account by name or ID number in ALMA
    2. Click on their ID number
  2. Click the tab that says "Notes"
  3. Click the "add note" button
  4. In the Note Description box, write your note and end with your initials and the date.
    1. The "Type" from the drop-down menu should be General, Circulation, Library or Other.
    2. User Viewable should only be chosen if appropriate.
    3. Pop up is a great new feature for notes you want to Pop up in a User's account
      1. Pop ups are not blocks, they will not keep items from renewing or anything like that
    4.  click to enlarge this image

Patron Questions & Requests about Summit Loans

Most user requests concerning Summit Loans should be directed to Summit staff. 

  • Use OSU Summit <osu.summit@oregonstate.edu> to forward email questions when you are sure that it is about a Summit item. If in doubt, you can use <valley.ill@oregonstate.edu>
  • Use the LEAD Follow up for for in person questions.
  • Use (541) 737-4488 for phone questions.

Basic Renewals

If a Summit items has not yet been renewed and is not in lost status, you can renew it for them. This is what the item should look like in the patron account. The 'Normal' status tells you it hasn't been renewed yet. 

It can take a couple of minutes before the renewal request goes through the system and registers a new due date. Refreshing the browser or closing and reopening the account may help or may just give you something to do while you wait. If the renewal was successful you will see a new due date and the loan status will change from Normal to Renewed. If the renewal doesn't go through, please refer the issue to Summit staff.

If a fine accrues because an item that you are able to renew is renewed late, you should waive that fine. 

Claim Returns, Appeals, Due Date Extension Requests, Damaged, Lost, Failed Renewals 

Just about everything else including the items listed above should be referred to Summit staff. It is recommended that a warm handoff is used to refer user requests. When speaking in person or over the phone, you can tell them that they will hear back from Summit staff within one business day. When forwarding and email. You should include the user your response letting them know that you are referring them to your Summit collogues to help them and they should hear back with in one business day.

Phones

The phones at the LEAD public desk ring three times and then transfer to the desk phones of LEAD staff to pick up. When the library is closed or no one is able to answer. The caller can leave a voice mail which is forwarded as an audio attachment to the valley.circ inbox.

There are two phone and they are both AVAYA J169s. 

Manuals

  • J169 Quick Reference Guide (VOIP Phone-uses colored port cable)
  • J169 phone user manual (VOIP phone-uses colored port cable)

Desk Phone Numbers

  • (541) 737-7293
  • (541) 737-7254

Answering the phone

  1. Answer the phone only if nobody is waiting to be helped at the desk. 
    • If nobody is able to answer the phone, it's okay to let the call go to voice mail. 
  2. Greet the caller
    1. Sample greeting: "Valley Library, __________ speaking. How can I help you?” 
  3. If appropriate, transfer the call.
  4. If the caller has a complex question or issue that the team working the desk cannot resolve, fill out a Follow-Up Form with as much detail as possible and tell the caller we will follow up.

Transferring Calls

  1. Tell the person the number that you are transferring them too. 

  2. Press Transfer. The current call is put on hold.

  3. Dial the number for the transfer or push the desired Quick Transfer Button.
    1. Press Complete once the phone starts ringing to transfer directly
    2. Press Complete once the phone is answered and you've explained the call to transfer with mediation.
  4. Press Cancel to halt the transfer and return to the person on the line.

Quick Transfer Button List

7-3332 – Media Hub

7-4488 – ILL/Summit

7-3010 – Public Safety (non-emergency)

7-2075 – SCARC

7-7278 – LEAD Head

7-3411 – Admin

Picking up a shift

Regular emails are sent out notifying the department about open shifts, However, please also be proactive and check WhenToWork at the beginning of your shift to see if there are any shifts you can pick up.

  1. Find open shift that you want to take.
  2. Click on it.
  3. Change unassigned to your name.
  4. Change color to blue.
  5. Leave description as BU or SUB
    1. This is what it would look like it Steve picked up a BU shift
    2. This is what it would look like if Erin pickd up a primary shift
  6. Recommended: Add the shift to your Outlook calendar. 

Posting on Twitter

https://twitter.com/OSUValleyLib 

  1. Sign in: 
  1. Formatting guidelines for tweets:
    1. Tweets can only be 280 characters
    2. Hashtags are very helpful for getting engagement, but take up space
      1. Format hashtags so that each word is capitalized- examples: #ValleyLibrary #ThisIsKalapuyanLand, etc. - this makes it easier for screen readers to process
    3. If you post the link at the end of the caption, it will not count towards your character limit
    4. Pictures are helpful, even though it’s not as visual of a medium as Instagram or facebook. 
    5. Do not start a tweet with an @, it will post as a reply to the tagged persons latest tweet. A workaround is typing a tweet as: .@username (with a period first)
    6. Unlike with instagram and Facebook, you cannot edit a tweet once it’s published
    7. You can add alt text on pictures/graphics on tweets for accessibility

You can find OSU's best practices for Twitter Here: https://social.oregonstate.edu/twitter-best-practices

2018.11.30 - Sustainability Tips for the Holidays

As the season of entertaining and gift giving kicks into high gear, the following tips and ideas are offered to support more sustainable celebrations.

  • For library unit celebrations, don’t forget to reserve and use the OSULP Party Pack to reduce (or eliminate!) landfill-bound waste.
  • When entertaining at home, try to use some or all of these strategies to reduce (or eliminate!) landfill-bound waste: (from Corvallis Sustainability Coalition newsletter suggestion doc)
    • Use reusables instead of disposables whenever possible
    • If you must use plastic, wash and reuse instead of throwing out (they are sturdier than you think!)
    • If you must use paper napkins, compost in your Yard Debris cart
    • Place well-labeled recycling and composting bins for guests to use
    • Create your own platters instead of overpackaged pre-cut items
    • If you buy pre-cut, save the sturdy packaging for reuse next time
    • Reuse bows, ribbons, paper, boxes & gift bags from year to year
    • Use fabrics or scarves as gift wrap -- oh-so-reusable!
    • Use gift bags instead of gift wrap -- much easier to reuse (NOTE: gift wrap that includes foil elements cannot be placed in paper recycling)
    • Use Sunday newspaper comic pages for colorful, fun gift wrap or use plain craft paper wrapping and decorate with beautiful, reused ribbons and bows

2018.09.21 - Campus Recycling Posters Being Updated

Earlier this spring, Campus Recycling (and indeed the recycling community) announced changes to recycling guidelines in response to global recycling changes. Over the summer, Campus Recycling staff have been updating recycling bin signage to provide guidance on what can/cannot be recycled. Slowly this signage is being implemented across campus and in the library. PLEASE follow the new guides as these are the only items that will be accepted for recycling. In other words, PLEASE refrain from "wishful recycling" (putting items in the bin that you hope can be recycled...but which actually cannot by recycled.) If the item does not appear on the signage, then it needs to be placed in the trash. Some examples of items which cannot be recycled include: tubs (yogurt/cream cheese/hummus/margarine, etc.), plastic jars (nut butters/mayo/mixed nuts, etc), plastic clamshells (to-go salads/to-go sandwiches or wraps, etc.), and clear plastic pre-packaged salad bins. If you have any questions about plastic recycling, attend the Sept. 27th How to Recycle at OSU Brownbag event or contact Master Recyclers-in-Training, Uta Hussong and Rima Reves.

2017.12.18 - Sustainability Tips for the Holidays (Part III) - gift wrapping (from Corvallis Sustainability Coalition newsletter suggestion doc)

If gift wrapping is a scheduled activity in your near future, you might consider following tips to make this aspect of gift-giving more sustainable:

  • Reuse bows, ribbons, paper, boxes & gift bags from year to year
  • Use gift bags instead of gift wrap – much easier to reuse
  • Use fabrics or scarves as gift wrap -- oh-so-reusable!
  • Use Sunday newspaper comic pages for colorful, fun gift wrap
  • Use plain kraft paper as wrapping and decorate the wrapped package with natural raffia ribbon and cut greenery - so lovely (and compostable)
  • Try to avoid gift wrapping that contains shiny foil as it cannot be recycled
  • And finally, one the gifts have been opened, recycle gift wrap that cannot be reused

 

 

2017.12.04 - Sustainability Tips for the Holidays (Part II) - gift giving (from Corvallis Sustainability Coalition newsletter suggestion doc)

As the season of entertaining and gift giving kicks into high gear, the following tips and ideas are offered to support more sustainable celebrations.

  • Consider gift durability -- if it will break soon,perhaps don't buy it
  • Shop for pre-owned items -- get a good deal AND reuse!
  • Ask for wish lists to ensure the gift you give is wanted and gets used
  • Donate to someone's favorite non-profit in lieu of a traditional gift
  • Support local artists; buy local and Fair Trade gifts; be creative
  • Give the gift of service instead of stuff; create coupon books
  • Give homemade gifts with minimal or reusable packaging

Ready Reference for the Valley Library Inbox

This document provides basic responses to common questions in the Valley Library Inbox. Although it is roughly alphabetized by topic, you can search the page using Ctrl+F. If in doubt, ask! If you're a coordinator of a particular service feel free to edit these notes to fit your procedures. Use Heading 3 to title each section so it shows up in the table of contents.

Table of Contents

Handy Links:

  • Ready Reference page for chat reference (includes resources for things outside of LEAD)

Basic Procedures

  • Try to empty the Valley Library inbox by the end of your desk shift
    • If you're frequently unable to finish what's in the inbox, or if you're frequently "inheriting" a full inbox, talk to your supervisor for help
  • Respond to and complete anything you can while at the desk. Forward what you can't work on at the desk to the appropriate person.
  • Once an email has been responded to, file it in the Recent Communication folder (unless instructions below specify otherwise)
  • If in doubt, ask for help!

Frequent Questions

Patron Accounts Questions

Try your best to answer any patron accounts questions. If you have a situation you're uncertain about, send a message to Sagan for help.

Questions about logging in

  1. Community members log in using the Community Cardholders link, using their card number (000-xxx-xxx, with or without hyphens) as their user name. Usually they just need their password reset.
    1. Open their account > General Information tab). Email them the temporary password and ask them to change it once they log in
  2. Double check that their account isn't expired. If it is, renew it for another year.

Bounce backs/emails failed to send

Emails from “Mail Delivery System” with the subject line “Undelivered Mail Returned to Sender” are notification emails sent by Alma that bounced. The patron didn't receive the notification either because they don't have an email in their record or the email is invalid.

  • View the attachment to see the email address that bounced, and an explanation of why it bounced (typically something like “Host or domain name not found.”)

  • If the subject line is "Item(s) sent by OSU Libraries", you can just delete the email. This is what is generated when a patron tries to email a record to themselves from Primo, and mis-type their email address

  • Check the patron's account for typos in the patron's email, such as: ".con" instead of ".com" or ".gamil" instead of ".gmail." 

    • How to search by email address in Alma? Admin → Find and Manage Users → Search by Email

  • If the email has typos (either in the Identifiers or Contact Info tab), make corrections and save. 

    • If you make a correction to the email address, resend the email that bounced.
      • Check the Attachment tab in the account and look for one that matches the day/time the bounce was received.
  • The error "Your email couldn't be forwarded from XX to another email address" means the message was delivered to the official OSU email, but the patron has auto-forward set up incorrectly. Add a user-visible note in their account that they need to use their OSU inbox to receive messages and to contact CN for help.

  • If the email address looks like there's no typos, then place a user viewable, pop-up note in the record to verify/update their email address. Note template: “Emails are bouncing back from the address on this account. Please update with library. Date” The email can be deleted after the note is added.

  • If the user has noemail@noemail.com as their email address that is because it is a required field and the user doesn’t have an email address, you can delete the bounced email from the Circ Inbox.
  • If no user is found when you search by email, move the email to the Undeliverable Patron Emails folder for the Patron Accounts Coordinator to troubleshoot.

New Patron Accounts

  1. Create the patron account in Alma ()
    1. The patron must include a scan or picture of their ID with their application. If they have not, please reply asking them for it.

Example: 

Hello [patron first name]

Thank you for registering for an account with Oregon State University’s Library System! We are working on processing your account. To complete your registration, we ask that you please reply to this email with a scanned copy or photo of your photo ID. Once we receive this information, we will complete your registration in the next 1-3 business days. 

Please feel free to contact us with any questions you may have about this process, we will be happy to assist you! You can also give us a call at 541-737-7254. 

Thank you,

[Staff Name]

2.Forward the application form to Sagan so they can create a Banner account

3. Print out the application (do not print out the picture of the ID- if you do, please shred it.)

4. Place the patron's library card & application into an envelope, labelling it with their name, and add a post-it note with the date & place the envelope in the convenience card tray.  

a. We will mail the card to the patron if they have not picked it up in two weeks, so please place the name where you would address a piece of mail

5. Email the patron to let them know their account has been created. Please attach an electronic copy of the library brochure. Example:

Hello [patron first name],

Thank you for registering for an account with Oregon State University’s Library! Your account has been created and your card will be available to you to pick up at the circulation desk of the Valley Library until [insert date two weeks out]. If you are unable to pick up your card by that date, we will mail your card to the mailing address listed on your library card application. If you prefer, we can mail your card to you immediately- just respond to this email to let us know. 

Attached to this email, you will find a brochure that lists the services available with your account and directions for logging into your account for the first time.

Please feel free to respond to this email with any questions you may have about your account or our services. You can also give us a call at 541-737-7254. We will be happy to assist you. 

Have a good day,

[Staff name]


6. Move the email to Recent Communication.

7. Sagan will mail cards to patrons after two weeks. If you get an email asking for the card to be mailed to them immediately, please do so.

8. When a patron comes in to collect their card, verify their ID with the ID information on their application. 

Kiosk Slides

If someone requests a slide be added to the kiosks, please forward to Library.graphics@oregonstate.edu   

Laptop and Hotspot Requests

Information and Policies

  • Laptops ad hotspots are requestable in Alma and Primo.
  • Patrons can request either type of laptop based on their preference.
  • Patrons can have one request or loan for each laptop type (e.g. one Chromebook checked out and one Latitude requested, one Latitude requested and one Chromebook requested)
  • Patrons can request multiple laptops at once but they are only allowed to check out one 1 week laptop of either type at a time.
  1. Encourage patrons to request laptops and hotspots themselves in Primo by looking up "valley laptops" or "valley hotspots"  
    1.  Don't hesitate to show patrons how to do this on the dual monitor station or send them to the Information Desk for help placing requests.
  2. Alternatively, to place a laptop or hotspot request for a patron in Alma, follow the directions below:
    1. To place a laptop or hotspot request for a patron through Alma:
      1. Search for Physical Title > Keywords > type "valley laptops" in the search; "valley hotspots" for hotspots. 
      2.  As patron if they prefer a Chromebook or Dell, then proceed with the following:
        1. Select the three-dot button on the far right.
        2. Select "request".
        3. Request Type "Patron Physical Item Request"
        4. Requester box: Have patron swipe their i.d. here.
        5. Pickup at Select "OSU Main Campus > Valley Library".
        6. To complete the request, select Submit at the top right.
      3. There is only one type of hotspot available, so follow steps ii. 1-6 to place a hotspot request. 
    2. If a patron would like to come back later to pick up the laptop or hotspot and there are already available devices, you can place the laptop on the hold shelf immediately,

Laptop Hold Shelf

Location and policies

  • 1-week Dell Latitudes that are being held for patrons stay in their numbered slots in the Drogon and Rhaegal laptop carts.

  • 1-week HP Chromebooks that are being held for patrons also stay in their numbered slots in the Snoopy/Linus/Woodstock carts.

  • Laptops stay on the hold shelf for a maximum of 3 days.

To place a requested laptop on the hold shelf:

  1. Make sure you had the "Place directly on hold shelf" radio button set to "Yes" when you checked it in.

  2.  Follow the applicable "Privacy and Updating" instructions for the laptop type. This part should be taken care of when the laptop is initially returned by previous patron.
  3. Print the hold slip/receipt and re-shelve the bag.
    1. If the hold slip doesn't print for an extended period of time, follow the instructions to re-print a hold slip
  4. When the hold slip prints, double check the slip to make sure it goes with the laptop number you have.
  5. Plug the laptop into its numbered slot or non-numbered stack in the laptop carts.

  6. Tuck the hold slip between the lid and body of the device, much like a book, such that the patron name is visible.

Hotspot Hold Shelf

Location and policies

  • Hotspots that are being held for patrons go on the hold shelf (i.e. where we keep books on hold).

  • Hotspots stay on the hold shelf for a maximum of 3 days.

To place a requested hotspot on the hold shelf:

  1. Make sure you had the "Place directly on hold shelf" radio button set to "Yes" when you checked it in.

  2. Print the hold slip/receipt.
    1. If the hold slip doesn't print for an extended period of time, follow the instructions to re-print a hold slip
  3. Open hotspot case and tuck the hold slip in the case with the patron's name sticking out of the top.
  4. Zip the hotspot case 3/4 of the way so the hold slip name is visible from the hold shelf.
  5. Place on hold shelf according to last name. 

Renewals

  1. Look up the patron's account and identify if an item is eligible for renewal
    1. If it's an Interlibrary loan book, forward the email to valley.ill@oregonstate.edu and they will take care of it
    2. If it is a Summit book and this will be the 1st renewal, then renew it. If it has already been renewed once, email OSU Summit osu.summit@oregonstate.edu
    3. If it is an OSU item, renew the item and email the patron letting them know.
      1. Note: Loans on items for which a user can place a hold like books from the stacks and laptops with no holds and short loans (like headsets and laptops) when we have additional copies of the item on the shelf should be renewed by overriding the block for maximum renewals and for not renewable. 
    4. If is not eligible for renewal, email the patron the reason why.

Room Requests (single-occupancy)

  1. Please answer any basic clarifications surrounding policies (i.e., who is eligible for a research room?) and assistance with placing a request.
  2. Forward any questions about policy exceptions, or more complex inquiries, to the Rooms Coordinator/Lucinda Amerman. If in doubt, forward the email.

Alma Generated Emails

  1. Loan Receipt Confusion for Mailed Items
    1. Patron receives email and thinks that we want them to come in person to pick up. Email Response Template: "This item will be mailed to you via FedEx. You should soon receive another email with tracking information soon." – No need to copy valley.remote.
    2. Patron receives email and doesn't want item mailed/address is incorrect. Email Response Template: "I am copying my colleagues who have prepared your item for mailing in the hopes that they will be able to retrieve the item before it is picked up from FedEx to cancel your request/make the item available to pick up in person/correct your address." Copy valley.remote on email.

Claimed Returns

  1. What can be done by whomever is checking inbox and what should be forwarded to coordinator? <need to fill in more/check with coordinator>
  2. COVID adjustment. For Valley owned items we will 1st look to see if the book can be found on shelf. If yes, than remove from account and let patron know it has been resolved. If no, also remove from account, but set item to missing in Alma after doing so and send email to patron (sample below). 
    1. Sample Email: Subject: Question About Returned Books Text:

      I was unable to locate the <item> on this end. However, COVID has cause a lot of disruption at the library and elsewhere, so I have removed the <item> from your account and removed any fines or fees that may have been assessed. I would ask that you continue to keep an eye out for the <item>. If you happen to find it, please return to the library so others can use it.

When 2 Work Notifications

  1. These can be deleted when there are student supervisors working or they are for times in the future. During weekends and into the evenings, there may be a need to approve a request for a last minute sub or information about a student who won't be working so that you can reassign a student to a different task.

Course Reserves

  1. If you are not able to answer a question about course reserves it should be forwarded to the valley.reserves email address. Any emails that entail a request to add or remove something from course reserves or questions about policy should always be sent to the reserves email.  Questions that should be answered directly:
    1. Do you have X book on course reserves?
      1. Search for item in catalog. Share permalink if item is available.
    2. How do I request an item be added to course reserves?
      1. Share link to course reserves page and guide to click on appropriate button for either student or instructor.

OSU Student/Staff/Faculty with Problems Logging into "My Account" 

  1. In all instances, trying to clear their cache or use a new browser may fix it
  2. Verify what they are trying to access:
    1. If they are trying to access an ebook or an article, they may need to request access from E-Resources (see https://library.oregonstate.edu/requesting-library-access)
    2. If they are trying to access their library account in Primo, this may be caused by a problem in their Alma account
  3. Troubleshooting access to their library account in Primo:
    1. Do they have an active account in Alma?
      1. If no, check to see if they have an active account in Atrium.
        1. If yes and they are new to OSU and/or recently returning to OSU, create a new patron account for them. Have them fill out a Community Patron account form so the Patron Accounts Coordinator knows what is happening and has all the information needed. Their account will update the next time Alma downloads our patron database.
        2. If they are not in Atrium, they may not have an active ONID or not be registered for classes.
          1. The IS Help Desk can help troubleshoot ONID issues
          2. In the meantime, we can create a community patron account and check out local items to them

Study Room Keycards Overdue

  1. Sample emails for responses to our email notifying a patron that they were the last person to checkout a study room keycard. We should respond to the patron's email and cc  
    1. If the say that they have lost the keycard:

      1. Thank you for letting us know about the key card. I appreciate it. There is nothing more you need to do at this time and no fines or fees will be charged to you. However, please keep an eye out for the key card and return it to the library if it turns up.

    2. If they say that they will return it:

      1. Thank you for letting us know about the key card. I appreciate it. Please return the key card to the library as soon as you are able so that we can use it for other students.

    3. If they say that they already returned it:
      1. Thank you for letting us know that you returned the key card. I appreciate it. There is nothing more you need to do at this time and no fines or fees will be charged to you.

Offers of Book and Other Physical Donations

  1. Review the Gifts & Donations policy.
    1. If the offered donation doesn't meet one of the three exceptions (by OSU faculty & not in collection, Government Documents, or potential SCARC acquisitions), then respond to the email by referencing and linking to the policy and thank them for the offer and add that "we are not able to accept donations of printed books, journals, and other materials". 
    2. If the offered donation might fall under one of the three exceptions, forward the request to the appropriate contact listed in the policy. 
    3. Sample email: 

      Thanks for thinking of OSU Valley Library.  Unfortunately, we do not accept donations.  Our current policy is located here: https://library.oregonstate.edu/collections/faculty-donations.

When and how can I pay library charges (fines, fees, purchases)?
